scope: Raw retrieval only, not proof validation

data.claim: For two task-distinct hypotheses with legal scalar Gaussian responses N(f_i(x), sigma^2), sup_x |f_0(x)-f_1(x)|=Delta<infinity, and both errors <=delta<1/2, every adaptive learner has E_0[N] >= (2 sigma^2/Delta^2) kl(1-delta||delta). If Delta=0, acquisition is impossible. The costed form uses sup_x KL(P_0^x||P_1^x)/cost(x).
data.interface: Adaptive legal scalar evaluations; fresh independent Gaussian noise; bounded stopping or integrable stopping with truncation argument.
data.proof: Stopped-transcript KL chain rule: query selection contributes zero conditional KL; each response contributes <=Delta^2/(2 sigma^2); binary data processing lower-bounds transcript KL by kl(1-delta||delta).
data.cost: Expected query count and optional query cost; input/answer bits and decoder computation remain additional charges.
data.baseline: All adaptive strategies are covered; a finite known separated class has a nearest-residual upper bound in robust_observability.md.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Pair f_0=0 and f_B(x)=2^-B x on [0,1] has degree one but requires Omega(sigma^2 4^B) calls at fixed confidence. Exact hitting does not imply noisy margin.
unresolved: Efficiently acquire a robust design and margin for general succinct formula/predictive classes
External proof and novelty review

data.claim: For F_(D,H)={0} union {c x^k: c=a/b reduced, 1<=a,b<=H, 0<=k<=D}, legal rational x in [0,1], Gaussian scalar noise sigma, and supplied D,H, the minimax adaptive query count to identify the exact predictive function at error delta<=1/4 is Theta(1+sigma^2 max(H^4,H^2 D^2) log(1/delta)) at the report's explicit sufficient answer precision O(log H+log D).
data.interface: Noisy scalar evaluations at chosen rational points; target coefficient and degree withheld; overall finite grammar and global caps supplied.
acquired: exact coefficient and degree, hence predictive class
data.proof: Two probes x=1 and x=D/(D+1) give a two-coordinate code with minimum L-infinity gap Delta=min(H^-2,1/[3H(D+1)]). Gaussian concentration gives upper bound. Near adjacent rational constants and adjacent degrees give adaptive KL lower bounds matching both H^4 and H^2D^2 terms.
data.cost: Calls are tight at sufficient answer precision; query coordinate bits, response bits, clipping, output code, and finite codebook decoding are explicitly charged in the leaf. Minimum precision Pareto frontier remains open.
data.baseline: A nonadaptive two-anchor experiment attains the minimax adaptive order; a strongest same-class adaptive learner cannot asymptotically improve call order.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Without a global height or degree envelope, arbitrarily close distinct monomials prevent every fixed finite uniform guarantee. The theorem does not cover arbitrary rational functions or unknown noise.
unresolved: Minimum input/output precision and complete query-precision Pareto frontier
External novelty/priority review

data.claim: For exact oracle O_r(u)=chi_u(Q(r)), complete legal profiles agree iff Q(r)-Q(r') lies in intersection_u ker(chi_u). If the desired task differs on a common fiber, every deterministic/randomized adaptive learner has pairwise error >=1/2 under a uniform prior, at any query budget.
data.interface: Exact algebraic query maps; any legal query set and answer functionals.
acquired: only the quotient class visible to the oracle
data.proof: Fiber characterization is the definition of the joint observation map; couple both worlds with identical learner randomness and induct on transcript queries.
data.cost: Information cost is infinite for a task label not constant on fibers; targeted added matrix query includes input and full matrix output bits.
data.baseline: No adaptive procedure can beat the fiber obstruction; 2x2 matrices separate c[x,y] for c in {0,1}.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Over an infinite field, scalar points identify the commutative abelianization, so this does not make commutative PIT impossible. Over F_q with base-field-only queries, 0 and x^q-x are formally distinct but observationally aliased.
unresolved: Universal finite-dimensional query families for broad rational formula classes
No noise-stable universal matrix query claim

data.claim: For stationary two-state binary HMMs with r0=1/(8L), r1=1/(2L), emissions correct with probability 3/4, training restricted to independent length-3 episodes, and target the endpoint Y_(3+L) after a fresh length-3 context, constant expected-TV risk requires Omega(L^2) training episodes; adjacent-pair testing identifies the pair in O(L^2), matching the exponent.
data.interface: Passive independent fresh stationary episodes, each truncated at three observed symbols; no hidden-state labels/interventions/conditional oracle.
acquired: which HMM and its exact endpoint predictor
data.proof: Length-3 KL is O(L^-2), while average endpoint forecast kernels after context are separated by a positive constant. Le Cam/triangle-risk lower bound; adjacent observation pair has mean gap 3/(16L), so Hoeffding gives O(L^2).
data.cost: Omega(L^2) reset episodes and 3 symbols per episode. Rank/emission/pair-Hankel margins stay constant; minimum transition probability is Theta(1/L).
data.baseline: Pair-correlation threshold test is the matched two-point upper baseline; oracle-supplied realization has zero further acquisition cost only because it supplies the missing model identity.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Does not lower-bound one uninterrupted stream, one-step prediction, or HMMs with stated fast-mixing/positivity parameters.
unresolved: Independent audit of constants
Arbitrary-HMM minimax and uniform mixing dependence

data.claim: For L>=126, the supplied pair of stationary binary HMMs r0=1/(8L), r1=1/(2L), with emissions correct at 3/4, has minimax training-symbol cost Theta(L) for constant expected-TV prediction of Y_(3+L) from an independent fresh 3-symbol context, when training is one uninterrupted stream. A concrete predictor has risk <=c/8 using T=5179(floor(0.85L)+1) symbols, where c=(3/4-exp(-1))/8; if T-1<=c^2 L/8, every learner has max risk >=c/4.
data.interface: Known two-model family and L; only model index withheld. One uninterrupted stationary observed training path, followed by an independent fresh length-three evaluation context. No hidden-state labels or intervention oracle.
acquired: model index and its endpoint forecast
data.proof: For lag s=floor(0.85L), the product W=Y_tY_(t+s) has model means separated by at least d*=(0.7875-exp(-0.84))/4. Products from disjoint adjacent blocks are iid; Hoeffding with B=5179 makes model error <=c/8. For the lower bound, KL of a length-T observed stream is <=(T-1)/(2L), evaluation-context KL <=9/(4L^2), and the two forecast kernels have expected-TV gap >=3c/4. Pinsker and bounded-loss change of measure give max prediction risk >=c/4 below the stated T threshold.
data.cost: Exact-output upper: T=5179(floor(0.85L)+1)=O(L) symbols, one training start, O(T) scan, O(1) memory; forecast output may require O(L log L) bits and O(log L) growing-integer multiplications. For a rounded forecast at the same epsilon0=c/8 risk, use B=5879 to allocate c/16 to classification and c/16 to rounding; output uses O(1) bits and controlled powering uses O(log L) multiplications with O(log L) guard precision. Lower bound is Omega(L) symbols. Evaluation context adds three symbols and one start.
data.baseline: On the same pair/loss, independent length-three reset episodes have matching Theta(L^2) symbol complexity. Independent reset episodes of length Theta(L) match the one-stream Theta(L) symbol order; the stream adds only savings in charged episode starts.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Two-model, fixed-noise, fixed-risk theorem only; it does not establish a rank-agnostic or arbitrary-HMM guarantee, an optimal leading constant, or a gain over long reset episodes. Rank and pair-moment margins remain constant while minimum transition mass is Theta(1/L).
unresolved: External proof and novelty review
Generalization to unknown-state or general HMM classes under explicit mixing assumptions

data.claim: For finite-rank process f with complete witness block H_L, supplied rank cap R and column incoherence mu0, adaptive uniform-row completion from exact rational prefix queries discovers the unknown exact rank and a word basis, with independent held-out residual checking and full-block fallback. The successful-panel query bound is O(N R^(3/2) mu0 log(R/delta)+rN+validation), where N=|Sigma^{<=L}|.
data.interface: Adaptive exact rational scalar queries f(w) for observable prefixes; not passive sample access or full matrix outputs.
data.proof: Krishnamurthy-Singh random-row sequential column detection with exact residuals; every appended column is genuine, and an independent random row panel detects any remaining outside-span column with high probability. Finite Hankel pivot factorization yields a realization.
data.cost: Exact cell queries, basis storage, rational bit growth and arithmetic are charged in the leaf. If R=N or panel size >=N, no sub-full-block saving. No singular gap needed for exact oracle; noisy completion needs additional off-span margin and sampled-basis conditioning.
data.baseline: Direct full-block rank/elimination costs N^2 cells and O(N^3) field ops; a basis-supplied oracle costs O(qr^2) shift entries but is stronger; both are compared explicitly.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Without C_L no finite transcript certifies all future behavior; without useful R cap adaptive query advantage vanishes. The incoherence lemma source applies to matrix column spaces and process-specific lower bounds remain incomplete.
unresolved: Rank-free stopping/cap removal
Noisy trajectory-oracle robust adaptive basis discovery
External proof/priority review

data.claim: Two rational orthonormal dictionaries can be distinct modulo signed permutation and have zero coherence, condition number one, bounded atoms and two-sparse coefficients of magnitude >=5/13, yet induce the same full process law. Every source-only adaptive learner then has I(dictionary; transcript)=0; if a later task predicts atom 1, the source-only mean squared error is >=1/65 under a uniform two-world prior.
data.interface: Full raw source trajectory access or any adaptive scalar functional of its law, including exact population means.
supplied: dictionary candidate worlds and source process law
later task asks for atom-indexed behavior
acquired: observable source predictor/subspace may be learned; intended latent dictionary is not
data.proof: Explicit orthogonal rotations give different sparse bases for the same target Y=R1 and therefore identical data distribution; couple source trajectories and learner randomness. The later-task floor follows the squared-distance midpoint identity.
data.cost: Zero source information for any query/sample budget; side information is at least one bit for the two-world label, or later labeled task data are needed.
data.baseline: Full-data baseline has the same zero information; source prediction itself is solved by the invariant predictor R1.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Not an impossibility for canonical bases, invariant predictive subspaces, or multi-task sparse-code models with additional coefficient-distribution assumptions.
unresolved: Positive predictive dictionary acquisition under multiple task/normalization assumptions

data.claim: A complete finite Hankel block with sigma_r>=gamma and controlled empirical/rounding/SVD error supports unsupplied-rank thresholding. Uniform exact rank recovery fails without a gap (small-mass two-component mixture). All-future basis certification fails without a witness horizon/rank cap (delayed finite clock aliases any finite transcript).
data.interface: Independent reset trajectories or exact/noisy prefix probability queries on a declared finite block.
supplied: block completeness/witness horizon for all-future statement
error bound and, for noisy rank selection, singular margin
acquired: rank of the chosen finite block and truncated observable subspace
data.proof: Hoeffding plus Weyl perturbation and cutoff at 2R; two-point mixture and delayed-clock counterexamples show necessity of margins/horizon.
data.cost: Explicit N trajectories, observed symbols, pq storage/SVD, b-bit rounding and certified numerical error in spectral_unknown_rank.txt.
data.baseline: Nested-rank holdout validation and retained sample-frequency lookup receive same data and can outperform exact algebraic-rank selection on prediction risk.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Finite-block rank is not an all-horizon realization if completeness is absent; rank gap alone does not bound long products or recovery conditioning.
unresolved: Adaptive finite-sample basis acquisition with no rank/horizon and robust stability

data.claim: In the specified persistent noisy one-hot atom class, q+1 subset queries with O(beta^-2 log(q/delta)) repeated readouts recover the hidden atom/null class and an exact all-horizon finite-state predictor with probability >=1-delta. A fixed q-bit group-test bank matches costs; the same-data best-policy baseline can simulate the learner.
data.interface: Controlled subset-membership queries and persistent latent parameter; not passive fixed-feature moments.
data.proof: Hoeffding confidence intervals separate the active/null response; prefix or bit group tests recover index; model law is explicit product conditional on the index.
data.cost: q+1 calls, repeated noisy symbols, query descriptor bits, O(q) model code; exact cost ledger and finite 72-case check in leaf.
data.baseline: Nonadaptive group-test bank matches the same query/symbol order; strongest equal-interface policy can copy all learner state.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Does not give a general algorithm for arbitrary unenumerated observables or an advantage over equally informed same-interface policies.
unresolved: Generalization beyond the controlled one-hot class
External novelty review

data.claim: For a finite controlled HMM, if active and randomized assignment policies coincide on every reachable logged observable-history-conditioned action distribution and use the same reset/observation/stopping schedule, transcript laws and estimator risks are identical. In a separate one-sided-erasure pulse model, physical excitation can reduce expected cost versus idle-only passive sampling after action cost; adaptivity has no gain versus the best precommitted allocation with the same actions.
data.interface: Logged controls; known action and cost schedule; hidden state remains hidden in pulse example.
supplied: controlled HMM class and action policies
data.proof: Sequential kernel induction proves transcript equality; pulse result uses first informative emission probability per cost and exact stopping-cost lower bound.
data.cost: Action, emission, reset and stopping costs are explicit in leaves; action counts alone do not establish equivalence.
data.baseline: The strongest matched randomized assignment has the same full action allocation; idle-only passive baseline is weaker because it lacks excitation right.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Hidden-state clamps are a different interface; equal action counts do not suffice; feedback may matter with noisy sign flips or state-persistent dynamics.
unresolved: Adaptive action advantage in persistent-hidden-state noisy HMMs with matched allocation

data.claim: Against a retaining baseline permitted to compute and keep the same representation from the same source transcript E under equal memory/computation/query limits, no transfer learner using S=phi(E) has an information or simulation advantage. A strict net gain needs a named narrower baseline or real resource constraint and must include acquisition, failed search, validation, storage, and downstream costs.
data.interface: Equal source transcript and later workload; declared resource vector or scalar cost.
supplied: same downstream task/input and resource accounting
data.proof: The retaining policy can run the same phi and copy the learner's state/update rule; scalar break-even follows by adding one-time acquisition and per-task reuse costs.
data.cost: Acquisition+reuse compared against retained-data re-learning; storage, validation, failed branches, coding and arithmetic charged.
data.baseline: Best equal-information retaining/simulating policy; narrower baseline must be named explicitly.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: A real memory cap, preprocessing deadline, or restricted query/output interface can create a practical tradeoff; no empirical performance gain is asserted.
unresolved: Demonstrate an end-to-end gain against a competent, matched retaining baseline

data.claim: A stationary finite-state target P_(epsilon,m) can be epsilon-close in whole-process TV to one-state source Q while its exact causal-state count is m+1 rather than 1. Literal source-machine reuse has target-supported conditional TV error 1 on the rare component, though average actual-path error is epsilon.
data.interface: Exact source law is acquired, then reused unchanged on a shifted target law; target provides actual finite histories.
supplied: target shift class and future-horizon loss
data.proof: Mix all-zero process with epsilon mass on an m-cycle with disjoint support; exact causal classes follow from different infinite futures.
data.cost: Source machine O(1) state work; target exact machine needs m+1 states or a phase counter; no net amortization claimed.
data.baseline: Target-specific acquisition/validation can detect the rare component at cost depending on epsilon and m; not computed as a break-even result.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Not an ergodic target and not a uniform-mixing counterexample; expected risk vanishes with epsilon. This attacks exact state-count/worst-case conditional stability only.
unresolved: Stability under fixed-state, irreducible, uniformly mixing and support-overlap assumptions

data.claim: Given a size-s noncommutative rational formula over Q, exact full-matrix output oracle with explicit UNDEFINED status, and the public N51 rational affine-pencil hitting-list theorem, center acquisition plus an injective finite residual feature map and BFS closure recovers a valid affine matrix-inverse descriptor for the formula equivalence class. It preserves the original inverse-gate domain. Query bound Q<=L0+(1+kR)L1+R with k=nd^2 and R=(s+1)d.
data.interface: Exact full matrix-valued evaluation at legal matrix tuples; matrices of several charged dimensions; original undefined status.
supplied: formula class/size/variable count and coefficient field Q
acquired: valid formula descriptor on original domain
data.proof: Domain-preserving affine linearization gives residual series dimension <=R. A feasible-pencil hitting list makes the residual feature map injective; breadth-first residual closure builds minimal realization of that perturbed generic-entry series. Quotient invariance plus block-triangular specialization proves the learned descriptor remains defined on the original syntax-tree domain.
data.cost: Q full-matrix calls; max dimension Dmax<=max(d0,d(R+1)R e1); at most Q Dmax^2 returned rationals, with polynomial exact height under a supplied rational height h. Full input/output bit and exact elimination costs are charged in the leaf.
data.baseline: If the formula tree is given, direct evaluation is one formula traversal; descriptor acquisition only helps if formula is withheld and reusable descriptor is the target. N68 sparse-polynomial acquisition is a different known-sparsity interface.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: The learner is conditional on the hit-list theorem, not practical. It is not syntax-tree recovery or minimal affine descriptor for Phi; x^-1 example has a d-dimensional residual series for a one-state formula. All-field extension is only local unreviewed; no noisy version.
unresolved: Independent verification of N51 list theorem/generator and whole descriptor learner
Practical constants and finite-noise robust acquisition
All-field validity and historical priority

data.claim: For a complete finite p-by-q Hankel block of rank r with unknown r, an entry-only Bernoulli word-event oracle supports adaptive row/column CUR acquisition and unknown-rank cutoff with a high-confidence stopping test, provided left/right coherence, sampled-core gap, entry precision and residual-leverage bounds hold. The learner can return UNKNOWN or full-block fallback when the certificate does not pass.
data.interface: Each selected word query returns a fresh independent Bernoulli indicator for whether a reset episode begins with that word; only one chosen word event is observed per oracle call.
supplied: finite block/witness completeness for process-level rank
target error/confidence and numeric oracle model
acquired: factorized CUR approximation with certified operator error
data.proof: Random row/column sampling with matrix Chernoff yields span coverage; Weyl/Wedin perturbation controls sampled core and CUR error; fresh uniform residual cell tests reject underfit candidates using a residual-leverage promise and phasewise failure spending.
data.cost: Training samples per selected word, validation samples, precision, core arithmetic and full-block fallback are charged in adaptive_hankel_acquisition.txt. No trajectory-sample saving follows against a raw path oracle because each path exposes all prefixes.
data.baseline: Full-block spectral estimation on the same entry-only law may query all block cells; against raw reset trajectories the full-block baseline shares the same sampled data and CUR only changes compute/storage.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Without a useful gap or residual leverage, rank and underfit residual can be hidden; rank cap/witness horizon is still required for all-future realization. CUR output need not be a positive or exactly Hankel-compatible process.
unresolved: Independent source/proof audit
A robust sample-optimal learner under a legal passive trajectory oracle
Remove residual-leverage or sampled-core-gap assumptions

data.claim: For the explicit finite HMM pair whose known witness history h has probability p=q^T and conditional next-bit laws Ber(1/2±delta), n passive length-(T+1) episodes have exact KL n p d(delta), d(delta)=2delta log((1+2delta)/(1-2delta)); constant-error testing needs Omega(1/(p delta^2)) episodes. A conditional-sample oracle callable at h before the learner observes h removes the p factor; an exact law evaluator uses 1-2 queries but must resolve joint probability scale p delta.
data.interface: Three distinct contracts: passive reset observations, named-history conditional samples, exact full-law probability queries.
supplied: known finite HMM construction and witness h
data.proof: The episode laws differ only on event h; exact TV/KL scale by p. Conditional samples expose the continuation directly. Exact joint probabilities encode the contrast in a p delta-sized answer.
data.cost: Passive expected witness count k/p and emitted symbols, conditional sample count Theta(delta^-2 log(1/alpha)), law-query precision > log2(1/(p delta)) bits are explicit.
data.baseline: Chernoff/majority tests on equally informed observations; conditional oracle is stronger because it skips history generation.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: If the policy must observe h before querying conditionally, its expected p^-1 wait remains; exact evaluator with additive error larger than p delta loses the constant-query advantage.
unresolved: General HMM class and state/horizon discovery costs

data.claim: For every T and delta in (0,1/2), two explicit stationary irreducible aperiodic finite-state HMMs with 2^T context states have identical laws on every observation block of length <=T yet their next-symbol conditional laws differ by TV 2delta at every supported T-context. Under passive episodes capped at T, exact minimax expected-TV risk is delta regardless of sample count.
data.interface: Stationary passive trajectories truncated at T, arbitrary number of independent episodes; next-symbol forecast after observed T-context.
data.proof: A binary de Bruijn shift context chain has uniform stationary contexts; transition bias depends on the oldest context bit, which has not appeared in <=T-block laws. Pointwise midpoint predictor attains risk delta; common transcript law gives matching lower bound.
data.cost: No amount of capped passive samples or numeric precision resolves it; one extra observation or one exact on-support conditional-probability query identifies sign. Hidden-state count 2^T and mixing time Theta_delta(T log T) are charged.
data.baseline: Constant midpoint predictor is minimax; length-(T+1) likelihood test has Chernoff rate from the leaf.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Exponential state count and growing mixing time; not a fixed-state or uniform-fast-mixing lower bound.
unresolved: Lower bound under fixed state count, bounded mixing, or a longer accessible horizon

data.claim: For a known one-hot length-d weighted-automaton family with N=n^d candidate words, amplitude Delta, per-call excitation cap E, Gaussian noise sigma and selectable midpoint comparator, adaptive point-query identification has minimax query order Theta(N+N sigma^2/(Delta^2 E)(1+log(1/delta))) for delta<=1/4. No-hit and zero-reference KL lower bounds match a pairwise tournament. A richer signed dense-group interface reduces high-SNR calls from N to log N while transmitting N weights per call.
data.interface: One named word scalar query with per-call excitation; separate richer dense linear-sensing interface; threshold/finite response bits are part of the contract.
acquired: hidden word index and exact automaton
data.proof: Point query lower bound combines probability of ever hitting unknown coordinate with an adaptive zero-reference KL sum; tournament gets matching rate. Dense signed halves implement binary search under a different vector-query contract.
data.cost: Calls, total excitation, query addresses/weight vector, response bits and evaluation work charged separately; exact finite verifier covers only noiseless fixtures.
data.baseline: Matched adaptive point tournament and signed group search; compressive binary search is neighboring prior art.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Fixed quantizers without useful midpoint can alias; dense-query call advantage ignores N-entry query bill; not a general unknown WFA theorem.
unresolved: General WFA or HMM family learning
Noisy finite-bit Pareto frontier under a fixed quantizer

data.claim: For the supplied one-path template over {0,1,#}, where the hidden target is L_w=Pref(w#) for a word w of length at most H and M=2^(H+1)-1 candidates, exact nonadaptive membership requires exactly M-1=2^(H+1)-2 calls, while adaptive membership uses H+1 to 2H calls and hence has optimal order Theta(H). If membership addresses are instead sampled IID from a designer-chosen distribution before labels, exact-label minimax cost is Theta(M log(1/delta)) for 0<delta<1/4, without an additional log M factor. The minimal DFA size |w|+3 and real Hankel rank |w|+2 are hidden and recovered from w.
data.interface: Scalar membership oracle for named strings x in {0,1,#}*. The class template and horizon cap H are supplied; target word w is hidden. Nonadaptive queries are fixed in advance. Passive IID addresses are sampled independently of labels and target. Equivalence-oracle access is a distinct stronger contract.
acquired: target word w and exact semantic predictor f_w
minimal DFA and Hankel rank for this supplied template
data.proof: Membership-positive sets are laminar subtrees and terminal singletons, so q fixed addresses induce at most q+1 response patterns; terminal queries for all but one target attain M-1. An adaptive prefix walk uses at most two calls per level; information needs at least ceil(log2 M)=H+1. For exact passive IID labels, target-specific certificates of at most three addresses give O(M log(1/delta)); a parent-child edge with query mass at most 3/(M-1) gives the matching lower.
data.cost: Each response is one bit. Adaptive address lengths total O(H^2) symbols, stores O(H) bits. The exact fixed schedule has M-1 calls and Theta(H 2^H) literal address symbols. Passive IID sample count is Theta(M log(1/delta)) and mean address length Theta(H), so address symbols are charged separately. A favorable equivalence oracle can return w# in one call, but that payload is Theta(H) symbols and requires teacher-side target search.
data.baseline: Best exact fixed nonadaptive membership schedule is M-1; best exact adaptive order is Theta(H); exact-label passive IID membership is Theta(M log(1/delta)). A stronger equivalence query to {epsilon} can reveal the full target as counterexample w#, but is not a unit-cost membership query.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: The path-transition template is supplied. This does not establish arbitrary weighted-automaton, HMM, or unknown-Hankel-basis acquisition. The exact adaptive constant remains H+1<=Q<=2H; no novelty or priority claim.
unresolved: Exact optimal adaptive query count within H+1 to 2H
General hidden-basis discovery without a supplied path template
Novelty and external proof review

data.claim: For the same supplied one-path membership template with independent known BSC(epsilon) labels and 0<epsilon<1/2, every passive IID address distribution and every delta-correct learner requires n >= (M-1) kl(1-delta||delta)/(3 d_epsilon), where d_epsilon=(1-2epsilon) ln((1-epsilon)/epsilon). A uniform-address traversal learner uses O(M (1/2-epsilon)^(-2) log(H/delta)) noisy passive samples. The log H gap is unresolved. Adaptive noisy membership has an information lower bound of order H/[1-h2(epsilon)] and a repeated-prefix-walk upper O(H (1/2-epsilon)^(-2) log(H/delta)).
data.interface: Same membership addresses as A18, with independent known BSC(epsilon) answer noise. Passive address schedule is a designer-chosen target-independent IID distribution; adaptive schedules may depend on previous noisy answers.
data.proof: For each parent-child edge, the two languages differ on only the child prefix and the two terminal queries for parent and child. Any address separates at most three edges, so some edge has mass <=3/(M-1); its per-sample KL is at most 3 d_epsilon/(M-1). Binary data processing gives the lower. Uniform-address sampling with repeated majority labels along the recovered path gives the upper. Adaptive lower follows from BSC channel capacity and Fano; majority repetition in the prefix walk supplies the upper.
data.cost: Noisy passive upper is O(M g^(-2) log(H/delta)) samples, g=1/2-epsilon, with mean address length Theta(H) and separately charged address symbols. The lower charges one noisy bit per membership answer. Adaptive upper is O(H g^(-2) log(H/delta)) calls; each address has length at most H+1.
data.baseline: Matched best designer-chosen passive IID distribution for the lower; uniform support over all nonempty binary prefixes for upper. Adaptive uses the same BSC answer channel with sequential prefix queries.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Only independent BSC noise with known epsilon and supplied one-path template. Passive log H factor and active noisy-query constant/channel gaps are not sharp; no theorem for arbitrary predictive systems.
unresolved: Remove or prove necessary the passive log H upper factor
Sharpen active noisy-query constants and compare to optimal noisy search
External proof and priority review

data.claim: For an HMM hidden-state cap R, populations probabilities through length 2R-1 suffice to reveal a complete predictive Hankel basis. Raw-trajectory estimators can recover unknown observable rank and a finite realization under explicit singular-gap and, for CUR, coherence/conditioning assumptions.
data.evidence: algebraic_rank/RESULT.txt; spectral_raw/RESULT.txt; spectral_source_reconstruction/RESULT.txt; noisy_realization/PROOF.txt; raw_hankel_concentration/theorem.txt
data.interface: Raw observed prefixes from independent episodes or an explicitly mixing single stream; no entry oracle or supplied basis. The exact sampling interface differs by leaf and must not be merged.
data.cost_and_baseline: Word tables can be exponential in R; sample counts depend on the explicit gap/mass/conditioning terms. Full raw-data baselines see all prefix indicators and can simulate CUR selection; no trajectory-sample advantage is proved.
data.open_gate: Rank-free task-risk certification without a singular gap, and stable positive-HMM realization at finite precision, remain UNKNOWN.

data.claim: For the stationary symmetric binary HMM with both unknown transition and emission parameters lambda,m in [1/2,3/4], two raw lag moments from one path give worst-history one-step TV O(T^-1/2), one-step KL O(T^-1), and H-step future KL O(H/T); a full-path Le Cam pair matches the one-step TV and KL rates.
data.evidence: full_predictor_unknown_transition/RESULT.txt; work/programmes/acquisition_learning/cycle2/full_predictor_unknown_transition/derivation.md; exact fixture verify.txt
data.interface: One stationary raw observation path, unknown transition and emission parameters, no hidden labels or conditional-query interface.
data.cost_and_baseline: T symbols, one initial stationary start, O(T) streaming work, O(log T) moment counters, two parameter outputs. The full-path lower bound applies to the strongest same-data learner.
data.open_gate: This is a structured two-state class with fixed margins. Generic-HMM dependence and filter-stability transfer remain UNKNOWN; no matching lower in growing H is proved.

data.claim: A K-state/K^2-parameter fast-mixing family has expected one-context TV minimax risk of order min(1,K/sqrt(N)); the full-support HMM version has context mass, transition/emission floors, and unnormalized pair-block singular scale explicitly shrinking as 1/K.

claims.claim: For the specified two-model emission-sign family, the full raw-trajectory likelihood is the hidden-state sum in RESULT.txt Section 3, and its theta likelihood ratio depends only on observed token signs.

Under observable-cue action A=C, each reset episode supplies a BSC(eta) token with probability a_A; under every action precommitted before the current cue, it supplies such a token with probability a_O, with a_A>a_O when epsilon<1/2 and q_H>q_L.
At fixed episode budget n, the exact minimax predictive-law failure risks are R_n(a_A,eta) for the adaptive class and R_n(a_O,eta) for the precommitted class, for TV radius D/3.

For epsilon=.01, q_H=.99, q_L=.01, e_0=.01, e_1=.99, eta=.10 and alpha=.05, exact minimax sample counts are 3 adaptive versus 7 precommitted episodes; with reset, pulse, and two symbol-observation costs of one each, costs are 12 versus 28.
This finite construction establishes neither a general controlled-HMM advantage nor novelty/priority.

data.claim: For the stationary symmetric two-state HMM with unknown lambda,m in [1/2,3/4], two lag-product statistics from one length-T raw path yield E[(lambdahat-lambda)^2+(mhat-m)^2] bounded by 65863/(4T), and the fitted predictor has expected worst-finite-history one-step TV <385/sqrt(T), one-step KL <=1354896/T, and H-step conditional future KL <=1354896 H/T.
data.interface: One stationary raw observation stream Y_1,...,Y_T; no hidden labels, resets, selected-word queries, interventions, or parameter values. The known class is the symmetric two-state HMM with lambda,m in [1/2,3/4].
data.proof: RESULT.txt sections 4-8; work/programmes/acquisition_learning/cycle2/full_predictor_unknown_transition/derivation.md
data.cost: T symbols, one initial stationary start, O(T) time, O(log T) counter bits plus two parameters, O(|h|) prediction time; precision and fixed-point rounding budgets in RESULT.txt section 8.
data.baseline: A full-path estimator can compute the same moments and reproduce the learner; the lower bound FPUT-2 applies to every raw-path estimator.
data.limitations: Structured two-state class with fixed positive margins and known family; not a theorem for arbitrary HMMs, unknown rank, or vanishing singular gaps. Novelty and external proof validation are UNKNOWN.

data.claim: For T>=15, every estimator of the full raw path has worst-finite-history one-step TV risk at least (25/1024)*sqrt(7/(32(T-1))) and one-step KL risk at least 4375/(16777216(T-1)); these lower bounds also apply to any H-step conditional future KL loss for H>=1.
data.interface: Same class and raw-stream interface as FPUT-1. The comparison uses a local transition-parameter pair with a common emission parameter.
data.proof: RESULT.txt section 9; full hidden-path KL, data processing, Pinsker, and Le Cam reduction are given.

data.limitations: The lower bound is a fixed-margin parametric local alternative; it does not characterize arbitrary-HMM or growing-horizon KL minimax dependence.

data.claim: For this symmetric two-state HMM only, each lag-k product Y_t Y_(t+k) is a function of k iid hidden transition increments and two iid emission signs; products at start-time separation d>k are independent. Therefore its sample mean variance is at most (1+2k)/(T-k).
data.interface: Stationary hidden chain with symmetric transition correlation lambda and conditionally independent emissions as in FPUT-1.
data.proof: RESULT.txt section 5 proves Y_t=S_t E_t and Y_tY_(t+k)=E_t E_(t+k) product D_j, including cancellation of the initial hidden sign.
data.cost: No asymptotic mixing approximation; exact finite dependence for the specified lag-product sequence.
data.baseline: Generic finite-state HMM observation processes need not be finite-dependent; this proof is not transferred by geometric mixing alone.
data.limitations: Special symmetry and binary-state factorization are essential; generic-HMM covariance control remains UNKNOWN.

data.claim: For K=2m and either s=1 or s=3/4, the stated stationary K-state block family has expected one-context predictive-TV minimax risk at least (s^2/8) min{1/8,(sqrt(3)/16)K/sqrt(n-1)} and at most min{1,sqrt(25/3)K/sqrt(n-1)}.
data.quantifiers: Every even K>=2 and integer n>=2; infimum over all proper row-stochastic predictors from one stationary raw observed trajectory, supremum over theta in [-1/8,1/8]^(K/2 x K/2).
data.evidence: Full proof in RESULT.txt; exact rational fixture checks K=2,4,6,8 in check.py/check_output.json.

data.claim: The family has uniform stationary hidden/observed marginals, Dobrushin coefficient <=5/8, t_mix(1/4)<=3, min transition entry >=3/(8K), min full-support emission entry 1/(4K) for s=3/4, sigma_min(P)>=3/8, sigma_min(E)=3/4, sigma_min(Q)>=27/128, and sigma_min(J)>=27/(128K).

data.title: Rank-free stopping from a single raw trajectory
data.status: conditional theorem proved in note; exact finite examples checked; no external proof review or novelty audit

interface.data: One stationary raw output stream over a known finite alphabet; learner reads forward and may stop adaptively.
forbidden_or_absent: independent resets or free validation trajectories
supplied feature dictionary or row/column basis
interface.enumerated_features: All words over the alphabet through the known witness length L; no basis is supplied.

promises.spectral_gap: Known rational gamma > 0; every nonzero singular value of H_L is >= gamma.
promises.minimum_history_mass: Optional all-history coverage promise: every u in Sigma^{<=L} has probability >= p_min > 0.
promises.mixing: Known rational C_beta >= 1 and tau > 0 with beta(k) <= C_beta exp(-k/tau), under the stated block-coupling convention.
promises.confidence: delta in (0,1/4), rational for exact implementation.

result.finite_matrix: H_L[u,v]=Pr(uv), u,v in Sigma^{<=L}; rank(H_L)=rank(H)=r when L>=r-1.
result.algorithm: At look j acquire n_j=2^j fresh length-(2L+1) windows with g_j skipped symbols between windows; estimate all prefix probabilities; construct exact rational Hhat and Ghat=Hhat^T Hhat; compute positive inertia at gamma^2/16 and 9gamma^2/16; stop when both counts agree at a value d<=R, all histories were seen (if coverage requested), and the exact-comparable confidence radius E_j is < gamma/4.
result.certificate_type: Data-dependent high-probability certificate, not deterministic identification from noisy data.
result.correctness: Under the promises, returns unknown r with probability at least 1-delta. If the optional p_min coverage gate is omitted, the rank-only rule remains valid with rescaled confidence budgets.
result.stage_bounds: Let delta_j=delta/(3*2^(j+1)), k_j=ceil(log2(2M/delta_j)), h_j=ceil(log2(N/delta_j)). A sufficient look j obeys n_j > 8 N^2 gamma^(-2) k_j and, when coverage is requested, n_j >= p_min^(-1) h_j.

costs.raw_symbols: Across looks through J, fewer than 2 n_J windows and fewer than 2 n_J(B+g_J) trajectory symbols including skipped gaps.
costs.prefix_table_bits: O(M log(n_J+1)) counter bits plus a shared denominator; retained raw windows would cost O(B n_J log q) bits.
costs.linear_algebra: O(N^3) integer/rational arithmetic operations per look for Gram construction and each exact inertia computation.
costs.bit_arithmetic: Conservative schoolbook bound O(N^5(b+log N)^2) per look for exact inertia, where b=O(log N+2 log n_J+2 bitlen(gamma)); details are in RESULT.txt.
costs.model_coefficients: No realization coefficients are output; coefficient-bit cost is therefore zero. Prefix-frequency rational table is charged above. Future-prediction coefficient precision is outside the theorem.

same_data_controls.full_block_empirical_hankel_svd: Uses exactly the same windows and word counts and has the same concentration/gap sample bound. The result adds rank-free sequential stopping and exact inertia certification; it does not reduce the full matrix/table cost or claim adaptive small-basis acquisition.
same_data_controls.retained_samples: Keeping windows costs O(B n log q) bits and does not improve the statistical bound; streaming counters discard the raw windows but retain O(M log n) count bits.
same_data_controls.basis_supplied: A supplied row/column basis is a different, privileged interface; its supply/search/certification cost is not treated as free.

lower_bounds.claim: Without a uniform singular gap, no uniform finite rank-discovery sample bound holds even at fixed state cap, witness horizon, positive history mass, and geometric mixing.
lower_bounds.construction: Stationary symmetric binary Markov chain with P(1|0)=1/2-theta and P(1|1)=1/2+theta has H_1 singular values 3/2, theta, 0; distinguishing theta=0 from theta>0 costs Omega(theta^-2) symbols.

lower_bounds.claim: If the output must certify exposure of every candidate history, a prefix of mass p_min can require Omega(1/p_min) symbols to appear.
lower_bounds.construction: Binary Markov chain P(1|0)=epsilon, P(1|1)=1/2 has stationary history mass Theta(epsilon), constant geometric mixing, and all-zero path probability 1-O(T epsilon). This does not isolate p_min after fixing the Hankel gap, which also shrinks.

lower_bounds.claim: Without a state cap/witness horizon, no uniform finite word horizon identifies rank.
lower_bounds.construction: An order-m parity-dependent binary chain agrees with iid fair on every block of length <=m but has nontrivial dependence at length m+1 and predictive rank >1; its state count is 2^m. This is not used as a separate lower bound under a uniform mixing envelope.

lower_bounds.claim: Without mixing or independent restarts, a single long path may fail to reveal rank even when horizon, rank cap, gap, and minimum history mass are fixed.
lower_bounds.construction: A stationary mixture of constant-zero and constant-one paths with weights 0.9 and 0.1 has rank two and length-T TV distance 0.1 from the deterministic all-zero rank-one path for every T.

source_ledger.source: Hsu, Kakade, Zhang, A Spectral Algorithm for Learning Hidden Markov Models, COLT 2009/JCSS 2012.
source_ledger.use: Original observable-operator/spectral-learning baseline; paper explicitly uses independent sequences for its sample analysis and discusses discounting effective sample size by mixing for a long sequence. It is not the proof of this rank-free theorem.

source_ledger.source: Carlyle and Paz, Realizations by Stochastic Finite Automata, JCSS 5(1), 26-40 (1971).
source_ledger.use: Finite-rank/finite-state realization background. The finite witness length used here is derived directly.

source_ledger.source: Yu, Rates of Convergence for Empirical Processes of Stationary Mixing Sequences, Annals of Probability 22(1), 94-116 (1994).
source_ledger.use: Primary source on empirical processes under beta mixing and block/coupling methods; this note uses a direct finite-class Hoeffding bound after a standard block coupling.

source_ledger.source: Berbee, Random Walks with Stationary Increments and Renewal Theory, MC Tracts 112 (1979).
source_ledger.use: Original coupling reference. Repository metadata/full-text link were checked; the 42 MB full text could not be retrieved in this pass. The block-coupling inequality is stated with its convention and can be proved sequentially from the beta coefficient definition.

source_ledger.source: Hoeffding, Probability Inequalities for Sums of Bounded Random Variables, JASA 58(301), 13-30 (1963).
source_ledger.use: Original source for the independent-block Bernoulli concentration inequality.

No sharp joint dependence on M, N, gamma, and p_min is established.
No coordinate-stable realization, coefficient precision, or future-horizon prediction theorem is established.
The gap, mass, and mixing envelope are assumed known; estimating them from the same path is not addressed.

data.topic: unknown-rank Hankel/CUR from raw HMM trajectories

input_interface.trajectory_length: B burn-in symbols discarded plus L retained symbols

process_class.mixing_bound: Dobrushin coefficient <= rho=1-alpha; burn-in bias <= rho^B
process_class.coherence: left and right singular-space coherence <= supplied mu_0

proved_claims.statement: For D_L=sum_(h=0)^L a^h unique word events, eta=sqrt(log(2D_L/delta_e)/(2N))+rho^B uniformly bounds all empirical word probabilities with probability >=1-delta_e.

Uniform row/column sampling at s_R,s_C=O(mu_0 R log(R/delta_s)) captures the finite Hankel singular spaces with probability >=1-delta_s; a core cutoff at 2 epsilon_W recovers unknown r when kappa_0=lambda_0 sqrt(s_R s_C)/(2 sqrt(pq)) >=4 epsilon_W.
Under stated entry, core, and product precision budgets, ||H_hat_CUR-H||_op <= epsilon, hence each finite block word probability error is <=epsilon.
For epsilon<=lambda_0/4, finite-block left and right singular subspaces have sine-angle operator error <=2 epsilon/lambda_0.
For k-symbol contexts, positive emissions and epsilon<=min(nu^k/2,nu^k/(8a)) yield one-step finite-context next-symbol total-variation error <=4a epsilon/nu^k.

Each raw path supplies the prefix indicators for all words through length L; any CUR procedure on these data is postprocessing of the same observations. The full-data baseline can simulate it, so CUR has no information or trajectory-sample advantage under identical paths.

Within a stationary positive mixing two-state binary HMM family with fixed transition/emission lower bounds, ranks 1 and 2 can be made arbitrarily close in length-L raw-path total variation; with contrast z=1/(10NL), N-episode exact-rank testing error is at least 0.45.

costs.burn_in: B >= ceil(log(2/eta_*)/(-log rho)) when 0<rho<1; B=1 suffices for rho=0 unless exact stationary reset gives B=0
costs.numerical_precision: Certified absolute zeta_W and zeta_CUR budgets; counts are exact rationals

data.matched_baseline: Same raw paths: all D_L prefix-word counts, full empirical p-by-q Hankel, full SVD, plus retained-path or count-table predictor. Same episode/reset cost; CUR can save downstream dense storage and SVD arithmetic only.
unknown_or_not_claimed: uniform exact rank recovery without a positive finite-block singular gap
finite-block coherence from positivity or mixing alone
process-valid lower bound against all coherence-adaptive algorithms
hidden-state label recovery or parameter identifiability
prediction conditional on the entire infinite past
a predictive-risk advantage over full raw-data model selection
data.novelty_status: Conditional application of standard matrix concentration, CUR, and perturbation results; no novelty or priority claim.

data.statement: For an m-state discrete HMM with pi>0 and rank(O)=rank(T)=m, iid length-three observation triples suffice for LearnHMM(m,N) to produce a rank-m observable operator model whose length-t joint distribution has L1 error at most epsilon with probability at least 1-eta, provided N meets Theorem 6's bound C*t^2/epsilon^2*[m/(sigma_m(O)^2 sigma_m(P21)^4)+m*n0(epsilon0)/(sigma_m(O)^2 sigma_m(P21)^2)]*log(1/eta), epsilon0=sigma_m(O)sigma_m(P21)epsilon/(4t sqrt(m)).
data.source: Hsu-Kakade-Zhang, arXiv:0811.4413v6, Conditions 1-2, Sections 3.1-3.2, Figure 1, Theorem 6, Appendix A / Section 5.1; https://arxiv.org/abs/0811.4413
supplied: requested error epsilon, confidence eta, horizon t
acquired: empirical P1, P21, and P3,x,1 from observation triples
data.cost: N independent triples = 3N observed symbols; theorem has a universal unspecified constant C and real-arithmetic SVD/pseudoinverse; finite-precision bit runtime is not supplied by the source.
data.boundary: Fixed-rank theorem; not rank-free. Joint L1 at a requested horizon, not pointwise word error.

data.statement: With column-stochastic T, P1=O*pi, P21=O*T*diag(pi)*O^T, and P3,x,1=O*T*diag(O[x,:])*T*diag(pi)*O^T. For any U with U^T O invertible, b1=U^T P1, b_infty=(P21^T U)^+P1, and Bx=(U^T P3,x,1)(U^T P21)^+ satisfy b1=(U^T O)pi, b_infty^T=1^T(U^T O)^-1, Bx=(U^T O)Ax(U^T O)^-1 and telescope to all word probabilities.
data.boundary: The empirical b_infty formula must use P-hat_1. Figure 1 prints P_1 unhatted, whereas Section 5.1's proof uses P-hat_1; this record flags the likely source typo.

data.statement: Under HKZ Condition 1, rank(P21)=m. From an independent pilot of N_r iid triples, let q_r=n*sqrt(log(2*n^2/delta_r)/(2*N_r)), let R_r=q_r+zeta for certified singular-value error zeta, and return m_hat=#{j: sigma_tilde_j(P-hat21)>2R_r}. If sigma_m(P21)>=4R_r, then m_hat=m with probability at least 1-delta_r. Using an independent fitting batch of N_f triples and LearnHMM(m_hat,N_f), the joint guarantee is at least 1-delta_r-delta_f when N_f satisfies HKZ Theorem 6 at the true m.
data.proof_method: Cellwise Hoeffding over n^2 pair events, Frobenius-to-operator bound, Weyl singular-value perturbation, and independence of pilot and fitting batches.
data.explicit_margin_setting: For sigma_m(P21)>=mu>0, zeta<=mu/8 and N_r>=32*n^2*mu^-2*log(2*n^2/delta_r) imply R_r<=mu/4 and exact rank selection.
data.cost: N_r+N_f independent triples; rank pilot costs 3N_r symbol events and uses n^2 exact counters of ceil(log2(N_r+1)) bits. The conservative pilot sample bound is O(n^2*mu^-2*log(n/delta_r)).
data.boundary: Conditional on a positive pair-moment singular margin and certified finite-precision SVD. Does not remove HKZ fitting margins or prove a uniform gap-free rank guarantee.

data.statement: The source supplies statistical sample bounds and arithmetic-level SVD/matrix product descriptions, but no certified finite-precision bit complexity for computing Uhat, pseudoinverses, or stable Bhat operators. Empirical moment counts themselves have exact rational encodings with O(log N) bits per counter; the remaining numerical precision/runtime must be separately specified.
data.scope: This is a source guarantee boundary, not a proof that no efficient certified implementation exists.

data.claim: For a stationary d-state HMM on q symbols with known A_ij >= rho/d and emissions E_i(a) >= e, one raw path permits an exhaustive rational-cover conditional-likelihood estimator satisfying R_H^h(P,Qhat) <= inf_{Q in Theta_d} R_H^h(P,Q) + tau + 2 M_H sqrt(log(4 N_D/delta)/(2B)) + 2 zeta with probability >= 1-delta. Here h>=0, H>=1, M_H=H log(1/e), and R is expected conditional KL on a fresh stationary length-(h+H) block. No rank, singular gap, observable dictionary, labels, or probability oracle are supplied.
data.inputs_and_proof: Known rational rho,e, state cap D (or cap-free penalized union with the same common rho,e), stationary raw path, fixed h,H. Grid row rounding plus stationary-word log-likelihood continuity gives a tau-cover; Doeblin coupling of separated blocks and Hoeffding plus finite union bound give the oracle inequality. Full proof: outputs/research/acquisition_learning/cycle3/rank_free_hmm_mle/RESULT.txt.
data.cost: For denominator K_d >= max{12 d^2/(rho^2 tau),12 d(h+H-1)/(rho tau),12(h+H)/(e tau)}, N_d=binom(K_d+d-1,d-1)^d binom(K_d+q-1,q-1)^d. B >= 2 M_H^2 log(4 N_D/delta)/epsilon_stat^2 yields statistical slack epsilon_stat. Gap g=ceil(rho^-1 log(2(B-1)/delta)); raw symbols T=B(h+H)+(B-1)g. Exhaustive score cost O(B(h+H) sum_{d<=D} N_d d^2), exponential in model dimension; rational and log precision are charged in the result.
data.baseline_and_failure: Same-block saturated conditional table is an explicit equal-data comparator; a full-path retainer can replay either estimator and use all omitted symbols. Han-Jiang-Wu 2024 already gives a stronger no-mixing expected terminal one-symbol risk result for the full fixed-(d,q) stationary HMM class; this theorem's distinct contribution is explicit high-probability risk control for a frozen fitted model on fresh finite-H blocks under supplied floors. No statistical advantage is claimed. Does not prove unknown-rho/e adaptation, infinite-history frozen-model risk, or identifiability. Without mixing, the leaf's reducible two-state stationary example gives max expected fresh empty-history H=1 KL >=1/64 nats for every path length; this target is not conditional on an infinite past.
data.novelty: UNKNOWN; no external proof or priority review.

data.claim: For the class of all stationary HMMs with a fixed hidden-state size k and observation alphabet size ell, Han-Jiang-Wu Theorem 1 states that for n >= C k(k+ell), the minimax expected KL risk for predicting X_(n+1) from the same raw path X_1:n is at most C[(k ell/n) log(n/(k ell))+(k^2/n) log(n/k^2)], attained by an n^{O(k^2+k ell)} dynamic-programming estimator. A matching lower is stated when ell>=k and n>=k ell, or n>=k^C and k,ell>=2. For fixed k,ell this is Theta(log n/n). Their HMM class imposes no full-rank, identifiability, mixing, or emission-floor condition.
data.inputs_and_proof: The paper defines Risk as sup over stationary finite-block HMM laws of E_{X^(n+1)} KL(P(X_(n+1)|X^n)||Q(.|X^n)). The source's Proposition 1 converts joint-law redundancy plus a memory term to terminal risk; the HMM memory and redundancy lemmas yield Theorem 1. Source spans: arXiv:2404.15454v1 abstract, §1.1, Theorem 1, §2 Proposition 1, §3.3. This packet verifies the source theorem statement and interface, not an independent reconstruction of its full proof.
data.cost: One stationary observed path of n symbols; terminal one-step distribution output. Dynamic programming runs in n^{O(k^2+k ell)} time (polynomial in n for fixed k,ell, with the state/alphabet dimension in the exponent); no reset or mixing input. The result is expected risk, not a confidence certificate or reusable finite-state realization.
data.baseline_and_failure: This is the decisive baseline for any claimed general rank-free terminal expected prediction result. It does not establish frozen-model H-step joint KL, a high-probability post-selection risk certificate, efficient computation polynomial in k,ell, or a retained predictive-state representation.
data.novelty: Source-reported prior art; not a new programme result.

data.claim: For any stationary finite-alphabet process with supplied beta envelope, any training-selected predictor q_S(v|c) with q>=xi on context length L and future horizon H has fresh stationary expected finite-block KL bounded by min{ln(1/xi), Rhat + r ln(1/xi) + 2 sup_{u<=r}(h2(u)+u ln K)}, with confidence at least 1-delta-M beta(g+1); K=a^(L+H), r=min{1,sqrt(((K+1)ln2+ln(1/delta))/(2M))}.
data.inputs_and_proof: One raw training prefix followed by M later validation blocks of length L+H separated by g discarded symbols; supplied beta envelope; arbitrary selected predictor and independent learner random tape. Sequential maximal coupling reduces to iid stationary blocks, finite-cell TV confidence and conditional-entropy continuity prove the bound. Full proof: outputs/research/acquisition_learning/cycle3/lead_beta_certificate/RESULT.txt.
data.cost: T >= n+g+M(L+H)+(M-1)g. For TV radius r0, M >= ((K+1)ln2+ln(1/delta))/(2r0^2); dependence penalty M beta(g+1). K grows exponentially in L+H; certificate table storage and outward-rounded logs are charged.
data.baseline_and_failure: Full raw-path retention exactly simulates selection and certificate. Does not estimate beta from the same path, certify every context, or bound continuation after the terminal training history.
data.novelty: UNKNOWN; elementary ingredients, combined theorem internally proved only.

data.inputs_and_proof: Population observable conditional laws; no hidden parameter or rank oracle is needed to define the quotient. Insert P(F|C) inside the log and use KL nonnegativity. data.statement: For every epsilon>0, delta in (0,1/2), and hidden-state cap D>=2, there is a finite-bit, full-support binary order-one predictor q and two stationary HMMs with at most two states such that R_P0(q)<=epsilon/2, R_P1(q)>=2epsilon, and the complete infinite observation-path laws have TV p chosen so (1-p)(1-delta)>delta. Therefore no randomized post-hoc certifier for q can be both (epsilon,delta)-complete and sound, even when it sees the entire infinite raw path.
data.interface: One stationary raw path; sequential observation access; no reset, hidden-state, conditional-entry, dictionary, mixing, context-floor, or gap oracle; q is supplied before path; certificate is a finite stopping PASS/NO decision.
assumptions: Stationary HMM class includes reducible transition matrices
Binary output alphabet
data.costs: q uses O(L+B) dyadic coefficient bits; B=O(1+epsilon/p), L=O(log(1/epsilon)) for small epsilon; P1 stationary weight p has O(log denominator(p)) bits; lower bound holds against unbounded computation and full-path retention.
data.limitations: This is a post-hoc certificate impossibility for a supplied q, not a lower bound against every data-dependent learner. Exact infinite-path indistinguishability uses reducibility.

data.statement: For the same q and any almost-surely finite adaptive certifier that is complete on P0, there exists an irreducible two-state stationary Markov HMM P_a with the same stationary state-1 mass p, no lower bound on its mixing rate, R_Pa(q)>=2epsilon, and an all-zero prefix overlap large enough to force false certification probability above delta. Hence no certificate can be uniformly complete and sound over irreducible chains without a supplied rate bound.
data.interface: Same as preceding claim; certifier may use all raw symbols and internal randomness, but must stop almost surely on each low-risk instance.
assumptions: No positive lower bound on the transition or mixing rate
Candidate q is fixed and supplied
Uniform completeness and soundness over the class
data.costs: For finite horizon T, choose a=2^-M with M large enough that (1-p)(1-a)^(T-1) preserves the testing overlap; coefficient length M is O(log T plus confidence margin), and b=a(1-p)/p has O(M+log denominator(p)) bits. The exposure waiting time from state 0 is geometric with mean 1/a.
data.limitations: Each fixed irreducible alternative is eventually distinguishable with unlimited time. The theorem rules out uniform finite stopping without a rate, not eventual pointwise discrimination.

data.statement: Whether every data-dependent predictor learner lacks a finite-time high-confidence guarantee for stationary-history predictive KL under the same finite-state HMM class is not established. The proved result concerns certification of a fixed supplied predictor.
data.reason_unknown: Robust or universal predictors may avoid the bad q; existing literature establishes no-gap expected-risk prediction for fully observed Markov chains.

data.statement: Nonnegative rational weighted perfect matching partition functions admit a one-query approximation-preserving reduction to the half-filled rational real-matrix fixed-filter normalizer Z_{N/2}(A); an exact rational-square-variant construction also gives nearest-grid recovery from one exact target value.

The exact alternative writes pq as a binary sum of squares for w=p/q, uses one site per rational-square variant, and has R(0)=PM_w exactly. Both specify perturbation, error transfer, bit length, conditioning, and exact zero handling.

The compact chart has log condition number O(N(q+log N)); arithmetic is exact. This is not a vertex-count exponent-preserving reduction.

Replace each positive integer edge weight W by a simple two-port graph with signature (1,W,0,0), O(log W) vertices and O(log^2 W) edges. Every source matching uses m/2 edges, so the expanded unweighted count is D^(m/2) times the rational weighted partition function. Divide the OA113 estimate by this exact factor.

data.statement: The canonical fixed-sector row-activity polynomial F_{A,k}(x)=sum_{|S|=k}(sum_{J subset S^c, |J|=k} det A[S,J]^2)x^S is not always real stable or Rayleigh, even for 0/1 rational A. Therefore these examples do not admit a direct same-variable PSD determinant pencil representation.

Path P5 adjacency, k=2: exact coefficient list (0,1,2,1,1,3,2,1,1,0), exact rational upper-half-plane zero, and Delta_14=-99/100 at a positive real point.

data.title: The natural fixed-sector paired-Gram and joint determinant-square polynomials are not stable in general
data.input: A is the 4x4 directed-cycle permutation matrix with entries in {0,1}; k=2. Define H(x)=sum_{|S|=2} det(G[P(S),P(S)]) x^S and P(x,y)=sum_{|I|=|J|=2,I disjoint J} det(A[I,J])^2 x^I y^J.
data.claim: H=x1*x3+x2*x4 and P=x1*x3*y2*y4+x2*x4*y1*y3. Borcea-Branden-Liggett Theorem 4.1 implies every real multiaffine stable polynomial has nonnegative Rayleigh differences; Delta_13 H and Delta_(x1,y2) P equal -1 at all variables 1. Both polynomials are therefore unstable. A is orthogonal, so kappa_2(A)=1.
data.proof: For a permutation matrix, det(A[I,J]) is nonzero iff J=pi(I), in which case its square is 1. At half filling in the directed 4-cycle, disjointness leaves exactly the two alternating classes. Direct differentiation gives the two negative Rayleigh differences.
data.costs: The witness has constant dimension, 0/1 entries, exact integer coefficients, and no numerical conditioning issue.
data.falsifier: A direct enumeration finds a third nonzero disjoint minor pair, or either Rayleigh difference is nonnegative at the all-ones point.
data.scope_limit: Refutes stability of these natural polynomials as a blanket premise only. It does not rule out another representation, an algorithm using the supplied matrix, or non-stable coefficient extraction.
data.evidence: evidence/verify_cycle_counterexample.py and evidence/cycle_fixture.json; finite cycle replay n=4,6,8

data.title: Paired-Gram polynomial stability and exact evaluation for independent 2-site off-diagonal blocks
data.input: n=2s and a supplied site partition makes A=direct-sum_b [[0,a_b],[b_b,0]], with a_b,b_b nonnegative rationals. The target is Z_k for 0<=k<=s.
data.claim: Writing L_b=a_b^2*x_(b,L)+b_b^2*x_(b,R) and c_b=a_b^2+b_b^2, the paired-Gram polynomial H_k(x)=e_k(L_1,...,L_s) is real stable when nonzero, and Z_k=e_k(c_1,...,c_s).
data.proof: A nonzero block minor uses one row and one opposite column; selecting both sites violates disjointness. Block factorization gives the elementary-symmetric identities. For Im(x)>0, each nonzero L_b(x) has positive imaginary part, and e_k is stable by its product-of-linear-factors representation and Gauss-Lucas.
data.costs: A descending coefficient DP uses O(sk) rational operations. If L is total input bit length and D is the product of entry denominators, log D<=L; output numerator and denominator have O(kL+s) and O(kL) bits. A conservative schoolbook bit-time bound is O(sk(kL+s)^2). Exact suffix DP samples the target in expected polynomial fair-bit time. The joint row/column polynomial P_k can still fail stability, already for one block with a_1=b_1=1.
data.normalization: The fixed-sector unfiltered norm is S_k=[t^k] product_b(1+t*a_b^2)(1+t*b_b^2), and physical Gutzwiller acceptance after number-sector preparation is Z_k/S_k. The full unnormalized BCS denominator is product_b(1+a_b^2)(1+b_b^2). These can be exponentially small as probabilities; physical retries cost expected 1/p. The classical exact sampler has no physical postselection cost.
data.falsifier: A block-compatible disjoint minor that uses two selected sites in a 2-site block, or an exact coefficient that disagrees with the stated elementary-symmetric polynomial.
data.scope_limit: This is a structural subclass with a supplied block partition, not a general sparse-matrix result; stability alone is not used as a counting oracle.
data.evidence: Proof and exact recurrence in RESULT.txt

data.title: Uniform importance sampling is an FPRAS under support-density and weight-ratio promises
data.input: Explicit nonnegative rational A, 0<=k<=n/2, Omega={(I,J): |I|=|J|=k, I disjoint J}, N=|Omega|. Supplied promises rho=|{w>0}|/N>=rho_0 and max(w>0)/min(w>0)<=R_0, with R_0/rho_0 polynomial in n and input bit length.
data.claim: Uniform exact sampling from Omega and exact evaluation of w=det(A[I,J])^2, followed by a median-of-means estimator of N*E[w], returns a relative-epsilon estimate of Z_k with probability at least 1-delta using O((R_0/rho_0)*epsilon^-2*log(1/delta)) samples.
data.proof: E[w^2]/E[w]^2<=w_max*N/Z<=R_0/rho_0. Chebyshev gives constant success per O((R_0/rho_0)/epsilon^2)-sample group; a median of O(log(1/delta)) groups amplifies confidence.
data.costs: Clear rational denominators once. Bareiss computes each minor in O(k^3) integer operations with O(k(L+log k))-bit intermediates, yielding conservative O(k^5(L+log k)^2) bit operations per sample; output rational height is polynomial. Total sample and bit costs are detailed in RESULT.txt. The promise is not verified by the algorithm.
data.normalization: For arbitrary rational A, S_k=[t^k]det(I+t*A^T*A) gives fixed-sector acceptance Z_k/S_k; det(I+A^T*A) is the full BCS norm. S_k is exactly computable in polynomial bit time. Physical postselection retries still cost 1/p, separately from estimator runtime.
data.falsifier: The second-moment inequality or the exact uniform proposal distribution fails, or the supplied rho_0,R_0 do not bound support density and positive weight ratio.
data.scope_limit: This is a promised-class FPRAS only. No polynomial-time verifier for the promises and no generic importance sampler are claimed.
data.evidence: Full estimator derivation in RESULT.txt

data.title: Every fixed atom-probe list for all half-filled directed-cycle instances is exponential
data.input: Even n=2q, k=q; inputs range over directed Hamilton-cycle permutation matrices, and a probe tests one individual legal minor pair (I,J).
data.claim: Any input-independent atom list that hits every nonzero target on this family has at least binom(n,n/2)/2 atoms. Any fixed proposal has an instance with support mass at most 2/binom(n,n/2); m atom probes cannot guarantee 2/3 hit probability unless m>=binom(n,n/2)/3.
data.proof: Each input support is {(S,S^c),(S^c,S)} for the alternating classes of its cycle. Every balanced S can be made an alternating class by ordering S and S^c alternately around a Hamilton cycle. Complement pairs partition the legal atom universe into binom(n,n/2)/2 disjoint possible supports. On the all-zero transcript before the first hit, an atom-probe algorithm that sees only prior queried weights follows one common query path; m queries cover at most m complementary classes.
data.costs: The lower bound is exponential in n because binom(n,n/2)>=2^n/(n+1). The instances have 0/1 entries, Z=2, and matrix condition number 1.
data.falsifier: A cycle input has additional positive atom pairs beyond its alternating classes, or a legal atom belongs to two different complement classes.
data.scope_limit: This applies to input-independent term-probe lists or black-box probes whose choices depend only on previous queried weights. It does not apply to algebraic evaluations aggregating terms or algorithms that inspect and exploit A; the cycle itself has a linear-time exact solution.
data.evidence: Combinatorial proof in RESULT.txt; cycle replay n=4,6,8 and two-block evaluator replay in evidence/cycle_fixture.json

claims.interface: Formula tree in Q<x_1,...,x_n>, at most m vertices, total rational-leaf encoding length C, supplied unary support bound t, at most t distinct nonzero words, t <= poly(n+m+C); exact full M_(2t)(Q) response to one tuple query; no inverse gates.
claims.claim: With B=n+1, D=2t, and (A_i)_(a,b)=binom(b,a)B^a i^(b-a) for a<=b, f is zero iff f(A_1,...,A_n)=0.
claims.proof: The row v_D(z)=(1,z,...,z^(D-1)) satisfies v_D(z)A_i=v_D(Bz+i). Each word has an injective base-B code alpha(w), and v_D(1)f(A) contains the first 2t power moments of its at most t distinct integer codes. If f(A)=0, the first r moments vanish; the r-by-r Vandermonde matrix is nonsingular, forcing every coefficient to vanish.
claims.costs: Dense tuple output O(n t^3 log(n+1)) bits; deterministic construction polynomial in n,t. For formula size m and total constant bits C, response entries have O(C+m+m t log(n+1)) numerator/denominator bits and the full response has O(t^2(C+m+m t log(n+1))) bits. Naive formula evaluation uses O(m t^3) rational operations and conservative O(m t^3 H^2) bit operations for H=O(C+m+m t log(n+1)). The oracle computation and its full response are charged separately from tuple generation.

data.claim: If positive sector weights g_k approximate positive target weights f_k pointwise within relative error delta, then reweighting both by any supplied nonnegative rational likelihood table preserves normalized joint distributions within TV at most delta/(1-delta), independently of event mass.
data.quantifiers: Finite sector set k=0,...,N; finite outcome set T; f_k>0; 0<delta<1; (1-delta)f_k<=g_k<=(1+delta)f_k; h(k,t)>=0 with at least one positive entry.
data.proof: For r_k=g_k/f_k and R=Z'/Z=E_P[r_k], R is in [1-delta,1+delta]. On common support Q/P=r_k/R. The maximum possible ratio deviation gives TV(P,Q)<=delta/(1-delta). Full proof in RESULT.txt §2.
data.cost: For each explicit f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N), the direct rational Taylor/range-reduction construction uses r_k=O(N), m_k=O(1+log(N/delta)), and produces g_k with O(N m_k(log N+log m_k)) bits; all N+1 weights are constructed in deterministic time polynomial in N and the encoded rational delta. Normalization and a K-category CDF use polynomial-bit rational arithmetic; a dyadic grid uses O(log(K/gamma)) bits. Exact output and intermediate bit sizes are included.

The explicit target weights are directly approximable in polynomial bit time, so neither N125 nor a sector-mixture oracle removes a representation/acquisition barrier here. The direct construction is internally proved; it is not a novelty claim.

data.claim: If positive rational Dicke-sector weights g_k satisfy a<=g_k/f_k<=b, normalization yields a full-space Loewner sandwich with L=b/a; every CP map preserves it, and after conditioning on any nonzero outcome the normalized output trace distance is at most L^2-1, independent of event probability. For direct lower Taylor weights a=1-delta,b=1.
data.quantifiers: Finite N; rho=sum_k p_k |D_k><D_k| and sigma=sum_k q_k |D_k><D_k| with p_k,q_k>0 and raw g_k/f_k in [a,b], 0<a<=b; any finite-dimensional CP trace-nonincreasing map Phi; P=Tr Phi(rho)>0. The direct explicit-weight instance uses f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N), 0<delta<1, and a=1-delta,b=1.
data.proof: Normalization gives G/F as a p-weighted average in [a,b], hence q_k/p_k in [a/b,b/a]. Both states vanish outside the same symmetric subspace, so L^-1 rho<=sigma<=L rho on the whole Hilbert space. CP order preservation and normalization imply L^-2 tau<=upsilon<=L^2 tau, whence D(tau,upsilon)<=L^2-1 by the positive-part trace bound. Full proof in RESULT.txt section 3.
data.cost: The order lemma has no CP-map cost claim. With direct rational Taylor weights, delta=eps/16 for rational 0<eps<=1/2 gives conditional trace distance at most 128 eps/961, for every N. The direct weight construction and bit sizes are charged in RESULT.txt section 2; no Cycle-3 premise is used.
data.source_boundary: This is an internally proved generic relative-order stability lemma instantiated by explicit direct rational weights. It does not imply that arbitrary CP maps are classically simulable and does not rely on N125/Cycle-3.

data.claim: For every N>=1 and rational 0<delta<1, the explicit Gaussian-sector weights f_k=exp(-(k-N/2)^2/N) admit deterministic positive rational approximants g_k with (1-delta)f_k<=g_k<=f_k and polynomial construction time/bit size in N and the encoded delta.
data.quantifiers: N>=1 integer, k=0,...,N, rational delta in (0,1). Let u_k=(2k-N)^2/(4N), r_k be the least power of two >=1+u_k, v_k=u_k/r_k, and m_k the least odd integer with 2^m_k>=6r_k/delta.
data.proof: Set g_k=(sum_{j=0}^{m_k}(-v_k)^j/j!)^{r_k}. The odd Taylor partial sum lower-bounds e^-v, the next even sum upper-bounds it, and their gap is at most 2^-m. Since e^-v>1/3, the lower/upper ratio is at least 1-delta/(2r). Raising to r and using Bernoulli gives g_k/e^-u>=1-delta; the upper inequality follows from the lower Taylor bound. Positivity follows from the same alternating-series bound. Full derivation in RESULT.txt section 2.
data.cost: r_k=O(N), m_k=O(1+log(N/delta)); each g_k numerator and denominator has O(N m_k(log N+log(m_k+1))) bits. Horner evaluation plus repeated squaring constructs all N+1 weights in deterministic polynomial bit time. A conservative normalized weight/MPO-entry bound is B_sigma=O(N^2 m_*(log N+log(m_*+1))+N), m_*=max_k m_k.
data.source_boundary: Elementary alternating Taylor bounds and rational arithmetic; no external theorem, N125, or Cycle-3 premise. This is a matched baseline, not a novelty claim.
data.falsifier: Any exact rational fixture violating positivity or the proved lower/upper bracket; the executable verifier checks finite fixtures only.
data.evidence: consumer_gate/verify_direct_relative.py: exact Fraction brackets on all k for N=1,2,4,8,20 at delta=1/16. This is finite corroboration; general guarantee follows from the analytic proof.
data.unresolved: No unresolved correctness gap is identified for this construction; the scientific question is whether a different legal interface requires separability/product-state preparation, where the direct rational MPO baseline may not suffice.

claims.statement: If the L03/leaf04 prime-subfield arithmetic exponent premise holds, one deterministic Turing machine given characteristic c=0 or a promised prime p and rational delta>0 halts with an exact prime-subfield rank-r decomposition of some T_u satisfying r<u^(9/4+delta).
claims.quantifiers: For every rational delta>0 and every c in {0} union the primes, there exists a finite witness; a single exhaustive-search procedure works on all such encoded inputs. The termination proof is conditional on the all-field exponent premise.
claims.interface: Input c and delta in binary; output u,r and complete rational coefficients or residues mod p. The output program embeds into every field of that characteristic. A bit-time evaluator over a field still needs its own exact element representation and operation costs.
claims.proof_or_basis: Stagewise enumerate all candidate u,r and finite coefficient arrays satisfying r^B<u^A, where 9/4+delta=A/B; verify each trilinear identity exactly. The source-derived exponent premise guarantees one accepted finite candidate.
claims.supplied_vs_acquired: The exponent premise is supplied/source-derived; the block witness is acquired by exhaustive search, not supplied. Search time and witness height are not bounded by the source.
claims.costs: Finite total search time conditional on premise. In terms of first-witness maximum dimension/rank/coefficient height S, a simple encoding enumeration is bounded by 2^O(S^4) times polynomial verification, including exact power-comparison bit length O(A log u+B log r) for 9/4+delta=A/B; this need not be polynomial in binary bits(delta). No useful bound S(c,delta) is known here. Exact recurrence arithmetic and coefficient bits remain charged.
claims.matched_baseline: Exact identity verification for a proposed block is polynomial in its finite encoding length; exhaustive candidate discovery is intentionally an unbounded acquisition baseline.
claims.falsifier: A valid c,delta for which the conditional exponent premise holds but no qualifying prime-subfield block witness exists, or a nonterminating/unsound exact candidate verifier.
claims.unresolved_gate: Any useful computable bound on witness size, search time, coefficient height, or practical crossover; primary source does not provide one.

claims.statement: A supplied exact rational Laurent witness with r rank-one terms, factor exponents in [-d,d], and formal identity G(t)=T+O(t) yields rank_Q(T^tensor m)<=r^m(2md+1)^2, with explicit rational coefficient-height and dense output bounds.
claims.quantifiers: For every m>=1 and every witness meeting the stated exact input contract.
claims.interface: Exact Laurent coefficient arrays over Q are supplied. If the witness is acquired rather than supplied, add its acquisition cost. A represented extension E/F of degree k incurs an explicit k^3 descent factor and basis/multiplication-table costs.
claims.proof_or_basis: Expand G(t)^tensor m, take the constant coefficient, and for each of r^m summand words choose exponents u,v; w=-u-v is forced. Rational common denominators give H_m=O(m C H + m H + m log(d+1)) bits per coordinate.
claims.supplied_vs_acquired: Witness supplied in exact symbolic form; no witness finder is claimed by this lemma.
claims.costs: Rank at most r^m(2md+1)^2; dense output has at most that many terms times sum_i n_i^m vector entries; exact construction is output-sensitive and generally exponential in m. Precision is unnecessary for exact input; approximate-only recovery needs a denominator-height bound and exact re-verification.
