claims.claim: For a fixed finite local endotactic reaction family in fixed species dimension d, the supplied deterministic affine-barrier corollary yields a compact positive invariant range K for any number of compartments when each edge uses the same scalar transport coefficient for every species. K is independent of graph size, topology, and the magnitude of locally bounded edge coefficients, including coefficients proportional to h^-2.

interface.initial_data: Each cell concentration belongs to one fixed compact Q0 subset of the positive orthant.
interface.reaction: A fixed finite local reaction family, with bounded supplied rates; the source's common-species transport corollary permits local measurable mixtures.
interface.transport: Nonnegative locally bounded scalar edge coefficients, identical across species on each edge.

claims.proof: The local affine minimum F_s uses fixed slopes r_lambda in R^d. For G=min_(v,lambda) L_(lambda,s)(x_v), an active label at v satisfies L_(lambda,s)(x_w)>=G=L_(lambda,s)(x_v) for every w. Hence r_lambda dot sum_w m_vw(x_w-x_v)=sum_w m_vw(L_(lambda,s)(x_w)-L_(lambda,s)(x_v))>=0. The reaction derivative at an active label is nonnegative; the source's compact plateau is therefore invariant. The sign proof is independent of N_h and m_vw.
claims.consequence: A mesh family with concentrations initially in Q0 has an h-independent all-time L-infinity bound and positive coordinate lower bound.
limitations: This is invariant-range confinement from bounded positive initial profiles, not an all-data classwise absorber or a uniform entry time for arbitrary spatially unbounded initial data.
PDE convergence still needs a specified consistent mesh, discrete coercivity/compactness, and convergence of h-dependent reaction controls.
claims.source: Local 7 October reconstruction, d-326696af15b5e02b.html, sections 'Switching, convex mixtures, and invariant transport' and 'Common-species transport on arbitrary finite topologies', especially lines 739-924.

claims.claim: Under shape-regular quasi-uniform finite-volume assumptions on a fixed bounded domain, the common-scalar invariant range gives a subsequential reaction-diffusion PDE limit that remains in the same compact positive convex K. The same conclusion holds for diagonal species diffusion when every facet normal of K is a common nonnegative left eigenvector of every edge diffusion matrix and the diffusivities are uniformly elliptic.

uniformity_criterion.transport_normal_test: For each facet normal a_i and edge matrix A^h_vw, require (a_i)^T A^h_vw=mu^h_i,vw (a_i)^T with mu^h_i,vw>=0.
uniformity_criterion.reaction_test: At each site, the local reaction field points into K on each active facet; uniform boundedness on K is required for compactness.
uniformity_criterion.mesh_test: Symmetric conservative consistent graph Laplacian; discrete H1 energy equivalent to the piecewise-constant gradient; diffusivities bounded below; initial interpolants converge in L2.
uniformity_criterion.controls_test: For the finite reaction list, coefficient fields are fixed or have a weak-* convergent subsequence.

claims.proof: The eigenvector condition turns edge transport on facet i into sum_w mu_i,vw [g_i(x_w)-g_i(x_v)]>=0 whenever x_v is on that facet and all x_w are in K, so Q^N is invariant. Uniform boundedness of reactions on K and the symmetric diffusion identity yield a uniform L-infinity_t L2_x bound and an integrated discrete H1 bound. The equation bounds time derivatives in discrete H^-1. Standard discrete Rellich/Aubin-Lions compactness gives a strongly L2-convergent subsequence; closed convexity of K gives u(t,x) in K almost everywhere. Strong concentration convergence and weak-* rate convergence pass the bounded polynomial reactions to the weak PDE.
claims.limitation: This is a conditional compactness and limit statement, not supplied as a theorem by the reaction-network source.

claims.claim: For the stochastic graph exit estimate with a transported facet, D_h=kappa h^-2 and bounded degree give eta_i(h)=Theta(h^2), Q_i(h)=Theta(h^-2), theta_i(h)=Theta(h^2), rho_i(h)=Theta(h^4), and B_i(h)=O(1). The displayed estimate is useful uniformly over N_h~h^-p sites and time T only if V_h h^4 dominates log N_h+log(V_h T), in addition to the source's fixed local V_h>=V0 requirement.
claims.exact_bound: P(tau_Q<=T)<=N_h sum_i exp(-V_h theta_i(h) zeta_i)+V_h T N_h sum_i B_i(h) exp(-V_h rho_i(h)).
claims.physical_scaling: If local volume V_h=Omega_h h^p, then the load-bearing exponent is Omega_h h^(p+4). Fixed Omega_h=Omega violates V_h>=V0 as h->0 and sends the formal exponent to zero. A polynomial high-density scaling sufficient for this certificate is Omega_h h^(p+4)/log(1/h)->infinity for fixed T.
claims.reaction_rescaling: A reaction changes concentration by nu/V_h and fires at intensity V_h k phi^V_y(X), so the drift is k phi^V_y(X)nu -> k X^y nu. The finite-volume factorial correction is at most D_i/V_h with D_i=K sum_r |a_i dot nu_r| E_(y_r)(U); V_h>=V0=max(1,max_i ceil(2D_i/gamma_i)) preserves half the supplied margin. This local threshold is independent of N_h but fails under fixed-density voxel scaling V_h=Omega h^p.

limitations: The stochastic graph theorem assumes common species hopping; it is not a theorem for unequal species diffusivities.
The bound is finite-horizon confinement, not infinite-time survival, stochastic permanence, or a continuum limit.

claims.claim: The local strict-inward reaction polytope Q={1<=x<=3, 1<=y<=3, x+y>=3} is not automatically invariant under species-dependent transport, even with linear reactions 0<->A and 0<->B having drift (2-x,2-y). On two sites, A hopping at alpha/h^2 and B at beta/h^2 with beta>alpha gives both sites initial lower-sum-facet gap epsilon; the first-site facet gap becomes negative by time c h^2 for the explicit h-range below.
claims.active_facet: The first site exits through the lower sum facet x_(1,A)+x_(1,B)-3=0. Both initial site gaps are exactly epsilon>0.
claims.parameters: alpha=1, beta=3, c=log(3)/4, epsilon=1/1000 give g_h(c h^2)=1-(1-epsilon)e^(-c h^2)(1+1/(3 sqrt(3)))<0 whenever h^2<(4/log(3))*log[(999/1000)(1+1/(3 sqrt(3)))], a positive threshold about 0.63720237. Since g_h(0)=epsilon>0, the exact certified upper bound on the first exit time is tau_h<=c h^2; the first zero need not equal c h^2. The limit is epsilon-(1-epsilon)/(3 sqrt(3))<0.
claims.independent_exact_check: At h=1 and t=log(100/99), the gap is -1621541844091699/200000000000000000. This rational value was recomputed exactly with fractions.
claims.continuum_falsifier: For D_A=3,D_B=1 and initial profiles x=3/2-(1/10)(1-cos(4z)), y=3/2+(1/5)(1-cos(4z)), the smooth positive data lie in Q and touch the sum facet at z=0. There the PDE gap derivative is 1+3(-16/10)+16/5=-3/5, so the solution immediately leaves Q.
claims.scope_limit: This falsifies transfer of this product-polytope/affine certificate. It does not show absence of another absorber or failure of permanence for the stable linear example.

claims.claim: The affine family uses a finite slope set fixed before its auxiliary scale and lies in local dimension d. Its strict drift in the scale box is delta_s=kappa H s^M after K L s^H<=kappa H, and the plateau lies within [sqrt(s),s^-1/2]^d. For a fixed local network these constants do not depend on mesh size when reused sitewise; the source supplies no useful uniform lower bounds on H or s_P, or upper bounds on W_s, across varying network families or if the whole dN graph is treated as one growing-dimensional network.
claims.consequence: The sitewise common-scalar transport corollary is the valid route to h-uniform confinement; silently applying the single-network absorber theorem in dimension dN does not establish uniform constants.

claims.claim: Saint-Raymond's 2009 Theorem 2.1 is a primary-source incompressible Euler limit for general entropically convergent initial fluctuations, with an additional uniform large-velocity bound on the solution family.
claims.quantifiers: For smooth bounded Omega or T^3 and a measurable a.e.-positive Grad-cutoff kernel 0<b(z,omega)<=Cb(1+|z|)^beta with int_S2 b(z,omega)domega>=Cb^-1|z|/(1+|z|), beta in [0,1], let q>1. Assume epsilon^-2 H(f_epsilon^in|M)<=C, g_epsilon^in weakly convergent locally and epsilon^-2 H->(1/2)int M|g^in|^2, plus int M((f_epsilon-M)/M)^2 dv<=C for a.e. (t,x). Then fluctuations are relatively weakly compact; each limit is an infinitesimal Maxwellian whose fields solve incompressible Euler and a transported thermal scalar, with a fast acoustic corrector and strong corrected L1_loc convergence, up to the target solution lifespan. The field data are rho^in=int M g^in, u^in=int v M g^in, theta^in=(1/3)int(|v|^2-3)M g^in; u(0)=P u^in and theta(0)=(3theta^in-2rho^in)/5.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2009, Theorem 2.1 and proof equations (3.29)-(3.35); collision entropy inequality; modulated entropy; tail/dissipation estimates; Lipschitz target flow.

claims.scope: Imported theorem statement; not independently re-proved. We instantiate q=2 and the hard-sphere kernel.

claims.claim: The high-velocity condition in the general-data theorem is used to close an energy-flux estimate that relative entropy alone cannot close.
claims.quantifiers: Saint-Raymond states that g_epsilon |v|^3 is not controlled by relative entropy and uses a Chapman-Enskog decomposition plus tail and entropy-dissipation control; for q>1 the proof gains epsilon^((q-1)/2), equal to epsilon^1/2 at q=2.
claims.dependency: Saint-Raymond 2009, discussion preceding Theorem 2.1 and proof equations (3.32)-(3.34); C1-C3 show entropy convergence does not itself control the flux.
claims.falsifier: A proof of the same distributional energy-flux bound from assumptions (a)-(b) alone, covering the explicit family in C1.
claims.scope: Indispensability is established for this flux-closure inference, not for the truth of Euler convergence under weaker hypotheses.

data.question: Does finite-time propagation of chaos or mean-field stability hold uniformly for all t under only smooth globally Lipschitz deterministic Vlasov interactions and finite first moments?

scope.model: One-dimensional Vlasov equation with K(r)=r^2/2, force K'(x-y)=x-y, and its N-particle empirical system.
scope.initial_data: For every N, iid Z_i(0)~Normal(0,I_2), with position and velocity independent.
scope.metric: Phase-space W1 with cost |x-y|+|v-w|; position-marginal W1 gives a lower bound by projection.
scope.quantifier: The result is a counterexample to a universal theorem over the stated deterministic class, not over dissipative or stochastic subclasses.

claims.statement: For fixed T<infinity, the tagged position marginal rho^N_{1,t} is O_T(N^-1) close in W1 to the Vlasov position marginal rho_t, uniformly for 0<=t<=T.
claims.evidence: q(t)=cosh(2t), q_N(t)=(1-1/N)cosh(2t)+(1+t^2)/N; W1=sqrt(2/pi)(sqrt(q)-sqrt(q_N)) and is bounded by sqrt(2/pi)cosh(2T)/N.

claims.statement: At t_N=log(N)+c, for each fixed real c, W1(rho^N_{1,t_N},rho_{t_N}) tends to exp(c)/(2sqrt(pi)); hence uniform-in-time tagged chaos in W1 fails.
claims.evidence: At t_N, q/N^2->exp(2c)/2 and (q-q_N)/N->exp(2c)/2; rationalizing square roots yields the limit.

claims.statement: For each finite N the tagged position W1 error diverges as t->infinity, asymptotic to exp(t)/sqrt(pi)*(1-sqrt(1-1/N)).
claims.evidence: q(t)~exp(2t)/2 and q_N(t)/q(t)->1-1/N.

claims.statement: The Vlasov solution map has no time-independent W1 Lipschitz stability constant on centered Gaussian initial laws near Normal(0,I_2).
claims.evidence: Scale data by a; position W1 at time t is sqrt(2/pi)|a-1|sqrt(cosh(2t)), while initial phase W1<=2sqrt(2/pi)|a-1|. The ratio is >=0.5sqrt(cosh(2t))~exp(t)/(2sqrt(2)).

claims.statement: A primary-source W1 stability theorem provides finite-time control for this model but does not give a uniform-in-time factor.
claims.evidence: Iacobelli 2022 states the directly applicable classical Dobrushin estimate W1(f1(t),f2(t))<=exp[(1+2B)t]W1(f1(0),f2(0)); for this R model B=1, so the factor is exp(3t). Its refined Theorem 2.1 is recorded separately because its displayed proof uses the torus.

claims.statement: Uniform-in-time chaos theorems for dissipative stochastic kinetic models do not contradict this deterministic unstable counterexample.
claims.evidence: Monmarche 2017 treats a Vlasov-Fokker-Planck/Langevin system with friction, noise, strictly convex external confinement, and a semiconvex interaction under Assumption 1.

data.claim: For the specified one-dimensional harmonic mean-field Langevin particle system with iid initial vectors of finite covariance, the empirical mean fluctuation has exact N^(1/2) scaling and covariance governed by the 2x2 Lyapunov equation C'=AC+CA^T+sigma^2 e2 e2^T.
data.full_quantifiers: For every N>=1, gamma>0, omega>0, sigma>0, kappa in R, and iid Z_0^i in R^2 with mean m_0 and covariance Sigma_0, define A=[[0,1],[-(omega^2-kappa),-gamma]]. Then G_N=sqrt(N)(M_N-m) solves dG_N=AG_N dt+sigma e_2 dW_N exactly, and Cov(G_N(t))=C(t) for all t>=0, where C(0)=Sigma_0 and C'=AC+CA^T+sigma^2 e_2e_2^T. For finite fourth initial moment, the associated finite-test empirical fluctuation field converges in C([0,T]) for every fixed T<infinity and finite family of compactly supported smooth tests to the Gaussian weak SPDE specified in RESULT.txt.
data.supplied_inputs: N, gamma, omega, kappa, sigma, iid initial law; independent Brownian motions.
data.proof: Summing the particle equations gives the exact mean SDE. The standard iid vector CLT gives the initial Gaussian fluctuation; the normalized sum of Brownian motions is standard Brownian. Matrix Itô gives the covariance ODE. For the finite-test field, synchronously couple particles to iid nonlinear copies, represent the interaction as a common linear shift, apply the iid functional CLT to finitely many test processes, and Taylor-expand smooth tests. The empirical weak equation has a quadratic remainder of order N^(-1/2) times a tight product on each fixed horizon.
data.costs: 2x2 matrix exponential/Lyapunov calculation; one global mean and O(N) local drift arithmetic per numerical time step. Exact-real analysis only; no parameter acquisition or discretization error is claimed.
data.matched_baseline: The iid nonlinear copies driven by the same initial samples and Brownian motions and the supplied deterministic mean path.
data.falsifier: An exact solution contradicting the summed mean SDE, covariance integral, or weak test covariance equation under the stated model and moments.

data.claim: If both the centered kinetic matrix A_0 and mean matrix A are Hurwitz, the expected error for each fixed 1-Lipschitz observable is O(N^(-1/2)) uniformly over all t>=0, with an explicit constant.
data.full_quantifiers: For every fixed gamma>0, omega>0, sigma>0, kappa<omega^2, iid initial Z_0 with finite covariance Sigma_0, every N>=1, every deterministic f:R^2->R with Lip(f)<=1, and every t>=0, choose M_0,M_A>=1 and rho_0,rho_A>0 such that ||e^(A_0t)||<=M_0e^(-rho_0t) and ||e^(At)||<=M_Ae^(-rho_At). Set K=M_0^2(tr(Sigma_0)+sigma^2/(2rho_0)). Then E|mu_t^N(f)-mu_t(f)| <= sqrt(K)(1+|kappa|M_A/rho_A)/sqrt(N). The same constant bounds sup_{t>=0}sup_{Lip(f)<=1} E|mu_t^N(f)-mu_t(f)|; it is not a bound on E[W_1].
data.supplied_inputs: Stable model parameters and iid initial law with finite covariance.
data.proof: The centered nonlinear copies have uniformly bounded second moment K. Their sample mean deviation Y_N has L2 norm at most sqrt(K/N). The common particle-to-copy shift solves Delta'=A Delta+kappa e2 Y_N^x. Semigroup decay and Minkowski yield ||Delta||_L2<=|kappa|M_A sqrt(K)/(rho_A sqrt(N)). The iid empirical sampling term for each 1-Lipschitz f has expected absolute value at most sqrt(K/N).
data.costs: The displayed constant depends on semigroup decay and nonnormal conditioning. It becomes large near a zero eigenvalue. No entropy, log-Sobolev, or oracle cost is charged.
data.matched_baseline: Iid nonlinear copies with the same information and noise; their sampling contribution is explicitly separated from the common interaction shift.
data.falsifier: For a stable parameter choice, an exact evaluation of the left side exceeding the stated right side refutes the bound.

This is scalar at each time, not measure-valued path convergence. The model here is a closed-form special case; priority remains UNKNOWN.

data.claim: A uniform-in-time O(N^(-1/2)) hydrodynamic error holds for every interaction strength, including critical and unstable mean modes.
data.full_quantifiers: False already in the model of KFL-1. For critical kappa=omega^2, gamma,sigma>0 and deterministic iid initial data Z_0^i=(0,0), Var(m_N^x(t)-m_t^x)=sigma^2/(gamma^2N)[t-2(1-e^(-gamma t))/gamma+(1-e^(-2gamma t))/(2gamma)]. At t=cN this tends to sigma^2c/gamma^2. For unstable kappa>omega^2, put q=kappa-omega^2 and r=(-gamma+sqrt(gamma^2+4q))/2>0; for l=(r+gamma,1), Var(l dot (m_N-m_t))=sigma^2(e^(2rt)-1)/(2rN), which is order one at t=(log N)/(2r)+s.
data.supplied_inputs: The same exact harmonic Langevin system; deterministic zero initial condition; sigma>0.
data.proof: At criticality, solve the velocity OU mode and integrate it once to obtain the position variance. In the unstable case, project the exact mean SDE onto a left eigenvector with eigenvalue r and solve the resulting scalar unstable OU equation.
data.costs: Closed-form 2x2 linear SDE calculation; no numerical or oracle cost.
data.matched_baseline: The deterministic McKean-Vlasov mean m_t, which is identically zero for the counterexamples.
data.falsifier: The closed-form variances can be checked directly by Itô calculus; either variance failing at its stated horizon would falsify this counterexample.

data.claim: Primary fluctuation results establish finite-horizon Gaussian empirical-field CLTs for general McKean-Vlasov diffusions and for a recent class of degenerate kinetic McKean-Vlasov equations, under topology- and interaction-specific assumptions; critical models can require different scaling and non-Gaussian limits.
data.full_quantifiers: Fernández-Méléard (1997) report weighted negative Sobolev OU-field convergence for their stated model class on finite horizons. Hao-Zhang-Zhao (2026-07-15), Theorem 4.5, assume iid initial data, b=0, time-independent K, beta in (1,2), K in K_beta intersect B^(beta-2,infinity)_(2;a), |K|^2 in K_0, and mu_0 in B^(2d+1,infinity)_(1;a) intersect B^(2d+1,infinity)_(2;a), and prove finite-horizon convergence in C([0,T];B^(alpha-3,2)_(2;a,ell-1)) for every ell<0 and alpha<-2d. Their Theorem 4.10 gives a smooth-test expectation bound C N^(-1/2) uniformly in t in [0,T]. Dawson (1983) reports a non-Gaussian critical fluctuation regime for a mean-field oscillator model.

data.proof: These are source-reported published/preprint theorems, not proofs reconstructed in this leaf. The kinetic paper states the assumptions and theorem explicitly in its v1 HTML; its CLT uses additional regularity beyond its separate entropy propagation result.
data.costs: The kinetic CLT has topology-specific anisotropic Besov regularity and finite-horizon constants; Theorem 4.10 constants depend on T, test family, K, and mu_0. The path-space entropy theorem separately requires entropic-chaotic initial data. No uniform-in-infinite-time conclusion is claimed by these cited CLTs.

data.claim: A uniform-in-time quantitative Gaussian CLT for each smooth scalar test is already established for a small-coupling smooth kinetic Langevin class, but this does not establish full measure-valued process convergence.
data.full_quantifiers: Bernou-Duerinckx, Theorem 1.4 (arXiv:2405.19306v4 dated 2025-02-16; submitted 2024-05-29): for dimension d>=1, the Langevin model dX_i=V_i dt, dV_i=-(kappa/N)sum_j grad W(X_i-X_j)dt-(beta/2)V_i dt-grad A(X_i)dt+dB_i with beta>0, W smooth bounded and even, A(x)=a|x|^2/2 with a>0, iid initial law mu_0 satisfying integral exp(|z|^theta)mu_0(dz)<infinity for some theta>0, there are lambda_0,kappa_0>0 depending only on d,beta,W,A,theta such that for 0<=kappa<=kappa_0, all N>=1, t>=0, and phi in C_c^infinity(R^(2d), there is C_0 depending only on d,beta,W,A,mu_0 with d_2(sqrt(N) integral phi(d mu_t^N-d mu_t), integral phi d nu_t)<=C_0(N^(-1/2)+exp(-lambda_0 t)N^(-1/3))||phi||_(W^(4,infinity))^2. Here nu_t is the centered Gaussian linearized Dean-Kawasaki fluctuation field and d_2 is the second-order Zolotarev metric on scalar laws defined in the source. Remark 1.5 supplies an improved bound O(N^(-1/2)) when c_t(phi)=||phi||_(W^(2,infinity))^(-2)Var[integral phi d tilde-nu_t] is bounded below uniformly in t, where tilde-nu is the initial-fluctuation-only linearized field. The theorem is for each test and each time, uniformly in the bound; it does not provide convergence of the empirical fluctuation process in a full measure-valued path topology or a supremum over the test class.
data.supplied_inputs: Primary paper, model parameters, iid stretched-exponential initial law, smooth even W, quadratic confinement, positive beta, and small nonnegative kappa.
data.proof: Source theorem, not reconstructed in this leaf. The paper derives uniform-time ergodic estimates for the linearized Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation using hypocoercivity and combines these with Lions expansions and Stein’s method. No entropy-chaotic initial assumption or log-Sobolev premise is stated for Theorem 1.4; the decay estimate is established under the stated small-coupling and confinement assumptions. Direct applicability to the exact model in KFL-1 is not claimed: its unbounded mean-force interaction does not meet the paper’s stated smooth bounded pair-potential hypothesis.
data.costs: The theorem states existence of lambda_0,kappa_0,C_0 with dependencies rather than numerical values. Its proof uses smoothness, stretched-exponential moment control, small coupling, and a hypocoercive ergodic estimate. No computational cost is reported.
data.matched_baseline: The empirical measure of the interacting kinetic Langevin system compared with the scalar projection of its Gaussian linearized Dean-Kawasaki limit.
data.falsifier: A mismatch between the quoted theorem statement and arXiv:2405.19306v4 Theorem 1.4/Remark 1.5, or a counterexample satisfying all its assumptions and violating the stated scalar d2 bound.

data.claim: There is no positive exponential relative-entropy decay exponent uniform over all collision frequencies nu>0 and torus lengths ell>0 for the unit-temperature kinetic Fokker-Planck equation, even if the finite multiplicative prefactor may depend on nu and ell.
data.quantifiers: For every d>=1, nu>0, ell>0, and every all-state bound H(F_t|M)<=C(nu,ell) exp(-lambda(nu,ell)t) H(F_0|M) with finite C, lambda<=2 min{nu,(2pi/ell)^2/nu}.
assumptions: Periodic domain T^d_ell, standard Gaussian M(v)=(2pi)^(-d/2) exp(-|v|^2/2).
Forward equation d_t F+v.grad_x F=nu div_v(grad_v F+vF).
Relative entropy is with respect to normalized dx times M(v)dv; initial states are probability densities with finite entropy.
The claimed inequality is required for every admissible initial density and all t>=0; its prefactor is finite for each parameter pair.
data.proof: For k=2pi/ell, phi=cos(k x_1-k v_1/nu) is bounded, mean zero, and direct differentiation gives G_nu phi=-(k^2/nu)phi. Thus F_t=M(1+epsilon exp(-k^2 t/nu)phi), 0<epsilon<1, is a positive probability solution. Its KL entropy equals J(epsilon exp(-k^2 t/nu)), where J(a)=(2pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2pi)(1+a cos theta)log(1+a cos theta)dtheta=a^2/4+O(a^4). Its asymptotic exponent is exactly 2k^2/nu, forcing lambda<=2k^2/nu. For the other constraint, linearize any all-state KL inequality at M using bounded mean-zero velocity perturbations; density extends the resulting L2 semigroup estimate to h=v_1, for which exp(tG_nu)h=exp(-nu t)h. Hence lambda<=2nu. Together these give the stated bound and refute a common positive rate as ell->infinity, nu->0, or nu->infinity.

costs.representation: One spatial Fourier mode and one velocity coordinate; O(1) exact symbolic operations.

data.baseline: The exact fixed-parameter mode is compared with the established DMS/ADSW quadratic L2 hypocoercivity bounds. These do not imply a nonlinear KL lower bound.
data.falsifier: Substitute phi into G_nu and verify the residual; or compute the positive KL solution above and compare its asymptotic exponent with any proposed lambda.

data.claim: For fixed nu>0 and ell>0, the linear kinetic Fokker-Planck semigroup on T^d_ell has an explicit exponential quadratic-L2 estimate with exponent lambda_DMS=(1/12)nu k_*^2/(nu^2+k_*^2), k_*=2pi/ell.
data.quantifiers: For d>=1, every mean-zero initial perturbation F_0 in L2(dx M^(-1)dv), all t>=0, and the equation and equilibrium in KFP-UNIFORM-RATE-OBSTRUCTION, ||F_t-F_infty||^2<=3 exp(-lambda_DMS t)||F_0-F_infty||^2.
assumptions: Same periodic unit-temperature Gaussian KFP model as the first claim.
The claim concerns quadratic L2 entropy only; it does not assert a global nonlinear KL inequality.
data.proof: Use the primary-source DMS modewise bound for unit collision rate: ||Fhat(t,xi)||^2<=3 exp[-(1/12)|xi|^2/(1+|xi|^2)t]||Fhat_0(xi)||^2, with Gaussian constants Theta=1, K=3, theta=kappa=1. Rescale time s=nu t; the effective Fourier parameter is eta=xi/nu. Thus the squared-norm exponent in physical time is (1/12)nu|xi|^2/(nu^2+|xi|^2). On T^d_ell the least nonzero frequency is k_*=2pi/ell. The zero spatial mode is purely microscopic and has squared-norm rate 2nu, larger than the displayed nonzero-mode rate. Parseval gives the stated estimate.

modified_entropy.operator: A_eta=(I+(T_eta Pi)^*T_eta Pi)^(-1)(T_eta Pi)^*, T_eta F=i(v dot eta)F, Pi F=M integral F dv

macro_micro.microcoercivity: -<L0F,F>=integral M|grad_v(F/M)|^2 >= ||(I-Pi)F||^2 by the unit Gaussian Poincare inequality.

claims.statement: For every Leray-Hopf solution with u0 in L2_sigma(R3), (1/2)||u(t)||_2^2 + nu int_0^t ||grad u||_2^2 <= (1/2)||u0||_2^2 for almost every t>0; the strong form holds for a.e. starting time s and all t>=s. Smooth decaying solutions satisfy equality for every 0<=s<=t.

claims.statement: Under u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), p_lambda=lambda^2 p(lambda x,lambda^2 t), ||u_lambda||_(Lq_t Lp_x)=lambda^(1-3/p-2/q)||u||_(Lq_t Lp_x); LqLp is critical exactly when 2/q+3/p=1. In particular, L-infinity_t L3_x and L5_t L5_x are critical, the L-infinity_t L2_x norm scales lambda^-1/2, and both its squared energy and integrated enstrophy budget scale lambda^-1.

claims.statement: There is no uniform bound ||u||_(L5((0,T)xR3)) <= F(E0,D_T) over all smooth finite-energy unforced solutions and arbitrary finite T if F(a,b)->0 as a+b->0. In particular, no estimate with right-hand side C(E0+D_T)^alpha for fixed C<infinity and alpha>0 can hold uniformly.

data.statement: For every m>0, T_b>0, gamma>0 and spatially homogeneous velocity Kramers-Fokker-Planck equation with force F(t), initialized at its Maxwellian equilibrium and differentiated at F=0, the current response kernel is chi_gamma(t)=1_{t>=0} exp(-gamma t)/m. Its causal resolvent is chi_tilde_gamma(z)=1/[m(z+gamma)] for Re(z)>0. The equilibrium velocity covariance is C_gamma(t)=(k_B T_b/m)exp(-gamma t) for t>=0, so chi_gamma(t)=beta C_gamma(t) exactly.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: m,T_b,gamma are fixed positive real numbers for each member of the family.
beta=(k_B T_b)^(-1), sigma^2=(beta m)^(-1), M is the centered Gaussian with variance sigma^2.
f is normalized; integrations by parts have vanishing velocity-boundary terms.
The observable is mean velocity and the input is force, with force entering the acceleration as F/m.
The response means the derivative at zero applied force, at fixed gamma; position and nonuniform spatial modes are outside the stated model.
data.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt, sections 'Linear response and resolvent' and 'Fluctuation–dissipation identity and proof'. The first Hermite mode vM is invariant, L(vM)=-gamma vM; the OU SDE gives the covariance directly.

supplied_vs_acquired.note: This is an analytic model calculation, not an empirically fitted response.

costs.analytic_arithmetic: O(1) scalar operations after the parameters are supplied
costs.precision: For chi(0)=1/(m gamma), relative parameter errors propagate at first order as |Delta chi|/|chi| <= |Delta m|/m + |Delta gamma|/gamma. An absolute gamma error |Delta gamma| <= epsilon*m*gamma^2 suffices locally for absolute response error epsilon.
costs.trajectory_acquisition_if_empirical: A time horizon gamma^(-1) log(1/epsilon) is needed to observe decay to relative level epsilon; sample-count cost is not derived.

equal_input_baseline.direct_kinetic_method: Solve the linearized PDE; chi(t)=exp(-gamma t)/m and step response at T is (1-exp(-gamma T))/(m gamma).
equal_input_baseline.equilibrium_fluctuation_method: Compute C(t)=(k_B T_b/m)exp(-gamma t); beta*C(t) and beta*integral_0^T C(s) ds reproduce the same impulse and step responses.
equal_input_baseline.outcome: Exact algebraic agreement for every admitted parameter and finite horizon; this is an internal matched calculation, not external validation.

data.falsifier: For any m,T_b,gamma>0, a disagreement between the direct first-order PDE solution and beta times the equilibrium velocity covariance under the same conventions falsifies the identity.

data.statement: At fixed m>0 and T_b>0, the homogeneous OU kinetic family has exact mean-zero spectral gap gamma and static current susceptibility chi_tilde_gamma(0)=1/(m gamma). Hence the zero-frequency response is not uniformly bounded over gamma>0 as the gap closes, although for each fixed gamma>0 the response kernel decays exponentially and every fixed-time step response is finite. This one-mode example is sharp because source and observable both occupy the slow first Hermite mode.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: Fix m,T_b>0 and let gamma range over all positive values.
Static susceptibility is the derivative of stationary mean velocity with respect to constant force, equivalently the zero-frequency causal response integral.
Finite-time response is evaluated at a fixed horizon independent of gamma. No uniform-in-gamma exponential-decay claim is made.
data.proof_pointer: RESULT.txt, sections 'Linear response and resolvent' and 'Gap-closing conclusion and sharpness'. For fixed T_f, |delta j(T_f)| <= |F_0|T_f/m, while chi_tilde_gamma(0)=1/(m gamma) diverges.

costs.model_size: One exact invariant Hermite mode; O(1) analytic expression.
costs.finite_time_acquisition: For empirical resolution of an epsilon-relative decay, the observation horizon scales at least gamma^(-1)log(1/epsilon).
costs.precision: Absolute precision for the parameter gamma must scale as epsilon*m*gamma^2 to guarantee absolute error epsilon in 1/(m gamma), locally.

data.equal_input_baseline: Direct current response and the equilibrium Green-Kubo/FDT integral use identical m,T_b,gamma and give exactly 1/(m gamma). At m=k_B T_b=F_0=T_f=1, gamma=1,0.1,0.01 give finite-horizon step responses approximately 0.6321206,0.9516258,0.9950166 and static values 1,10,100.
data.falsifier: The explicit resolvent formula would have to fail for some gamma>0, or a claimed gamma-uniform finite bound would have to coexist with 1/(m gamma) for arbitrarily small positive gamma.
data.scientific_boundary: This refutes a general inference from pointwise relaxation/finite-time boundedness to uniform dc control. It does not imply divergence for every gap-closing kinetic model; vanishing slow-mode overlap can change the outcome.
unresolved: Whether a specific non-OU kinetic model has nonvanishing overlap with its slow modes requires separate analysis.
No novelty or priority claim.

data.statement: For a reversible equilibrium generator L with discrete mean-zero spectral expansion L psi_k=-lambda_k psi_k, lambda_k>0, and a matched force-response source/observable A for which the FDT pairing holds and the inverse-generator quadratic form is finite, the zero-frequency response is beta*sum_k |<A,psi_k>|^2/lambda_k. A positive gap lower bound gives a norm-over-gap bound; closing gaps alone give no uniform bound unless the overlap weights on slow modes also suppress the inverse rates.
assumptions_and_quantifiers: L is self-adjoint and nonpositive on the mean-zero equilibrium Hilbert space.
The perturbation is conjugate to A so the response kernel is beta*<A,exp(tL)A>.
The spectral sum is interpreted by the spectral theorem and is finite for each model under consideration.
data.proof_pointer: Expand A in the orthonormal eigenbasis and integrate beta*sum_k |<A,psi_k>|^2 exp(-lambda_k t) termwise when the nonnegative integral is finite; monotone convergence gives the stated sum.

costs.information: Requires the equilibrium generator, observable/source overlap, and spectral measure; these are supplied in the conditional statement.
costs.precision: A finite truncation needs control of the omitted low-rate spectral mass; no uniform truncation algorithm or cost is claimed.

data.falsifier: A reversible model satisfying the stated FDT pairing and spectral assumptions but violating its spectral-resolvent sum would falsify the claim.
data.primary_prior_art: Kubo 1957 is the general response-correlation source; the spectral expansion here is a direct resolvent consequence under the explicit self-adjointness and overlap assumptions.
limits: Continuous spectral measures require the corresponding integral formulation.
Non-reversible systems may have non-normal resolvent growth not captured by eigenvalues alone.

data.claim: For every N, beta>=0, and h in R, the Curie-Weiss Ising Gibbs law on sigma in {-1,+1}^N has magnetization mass proportional to binom(N,(N+M)/2) exp(beta M^2/(2N)+hM), and its thermodynamic pressure is the supremum in RESULT.txt equation (2).
data.quantifiers: All positive integers N, all beta>=0, all h real; M ranges over {-N,-N+2,...,N}. For fixed beta,h, N^-1 log Z converges to sup_{|m|<=1}{log2-I(m)+beta*m^2/2+h*m}.
data.constants_costs: Exact finite law has N+1 terms. Recurrence computes weights in O(N) arithmetic operations and O(N) memory; no observations or oracle are required. This excludes physical Gibbs preparation and finite-bit costs.
data.evidence: Direct magnetization multiplicity count; standard thermodynamic variational limit. See RESULT.txt sections 1-2 and primary-source comparison.
data.falsifier: A finite-N configuration count contradicting the binomial multiplicity or a failure of the stated Laplace-principle pressure limit under these parameters.

data.claim: At beta=1,h=0, M_N/N^(3/4) converges to density proportional to exp(-x^4/12); Var(M_N)=(C2+o(1))N^(3/2), where C2=sqrt(12)Gamma(3/4)/Gamma(1/4)=1.1708286566..., and chi_N=Var(M_N)/N=(C2+o(1))sqrt(N).
data.quantifiers: As N tends to infinity through all integers; chi_N is dimensionless response to h as it appears in the Gibbs exponent. Moment asymptotics use uniform quartic-tail control, not weak convergence alone.
data.constants_costs: The limit law is one-dimensional and non-Gaussian; E[X^4]=3 and standardized kurtosis is 2.1884396152..., not 3. The exact finite-N baseline costs O(N) weight evaluations.
data.evidence: Primary critical limit and O(N^-1/2) Kolmogorov rate in Eichelsbacher-Lowe 2010, Theorem 1.3; gamma moments evaluated directly. See RESULT.txt section 4.
data.falsifier: An exact-binomial sequence whose scaled second moment fails to approach C2 or whose variance-normalized fourth moment fails to approach 2.1884396152... .

claims.claim: Under the stated repulsive GP scaling, energy and condensation assumptions, every fixed-k reduced density converges to the factorized solution of the cubic GP equation with coefficient 8*pi*a0.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed k and each fixed t in R; the source proves compact-time convergence in the fixed-k weak* metric.
claims.source: Annals 2010, Theorems 2.1 and 2.2; arXiv:math-ph/0606017 v3

claims.claim: The exact scattering rescaling gives coefficient 8*pi*a0: N V_N(x) f_N(x) converges distributionally to 8*pi*a0 delta_0.
claims.quantifiers: Fixed smooth compactly supported radial V; f_N(x)=f0(Nx); N tends to infinity.
claims.proof: Change variables y=Nx and use integral V(y)f0(y)dy=8*pi*a0.
claims.source: Annals 2010, equations (2.8)-(2.12), Section 3, and Section 7.

claims.claim: The cutoff H^k estimate supplies the hierarchy regularity needed for uniqueness.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed integer k, rho sufficiently small, ell >> N^(-1/2), and N >= N0(k,C0).
claims.estimate: <psi,(H_N+N)^k psi> >= C0^k N^k integral Theta_(k-1)^(k)|nabla_1...nabla_k psi|^2 plus nonnegative derivative and potential terms.
claims.cutoff_window: Choose N ell^2 -> infinity, N ell^3 -> 0, and N ell^(3-epsilon) -> 0; ell=N^(-2/5), epsilon=1/4 is admissible.
claims.limit_consequence: Tr product_j(1-Delta_j) gamma_infinity,t^(k) <= C1^k with C1 independent of k and t on fixed compact intervals.
claims.source: Annals 2010, Proposition 5.3, Proposition 6.3, equations (5.29)-(5.33) and (6.12)-(6.13); uniqueness: arXiv:math-ph/0508010 v3, Theorem 9.1.

claims.claim: The proof's cutoff estimate is a fixed-k limit and does not provide a prelimit bound uniform for k growing with N.
claims.quantifiers: The estimate has N0=N0(k,C0), cutoff exponent 2^k*ell^(-epsilon), and Prop. 6.3 takes N to infinity for each fixed k.
claims.consequence: Do not interchange the fixed-k limit with a supremum over 1<=k<=N.

claims.claim: At the matched weaker-interaction scaling 0<beta<1/2 with the same V and product initial state, the effective coefficient is integral V rather than 8*pi*a0.
claims.quantifiers: For each fixed beta in (0,1/2), under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.1 of the primary baseline source.
claims.source: Erdos-Schlein-Yau, arXiv:math-ph/0508010 v3, Theorem 1.1; Annals 2010, Section 2.

claims.claim: No universal algebraic fixed-k convergence rate follows from the qualitative initial condensation and O(N) energy assumptions of Theorem 2.2.
claims.quantifiers: There is no delta>0 and universal constant bounding all admissible one-body errors by O(N^(-delta)).
claims.counterexample: For orthonormal smooth compactly supported phi,chi, set phi_N=sqrt(1-epsilon_N^2)phi+epsilon_N chi and psi_N=phi_N tensor N, with epsilon_N=1/log(N+2). Then the energy is O(N), the fixed-k strong factorization holds, and the one-body trace-norm error at t=0 is exactly 2/log(N+2).

claims.claim: Uniform-in-k convergence over every 1<=k<=N is false even within the low-energy theorem's initial-data class.
claims.quantifiers: A single admissible sequence has sup_(1<=k<=N) trace-norm error bounded away from zero at t=0.
claims.counterexample: Use the same product family with epsilon_N=N^(-1/2). For k=N, the trace-norm distance from |phi tensor N><phi tensor N| is 2*sqrt(1-(1-1/N)^N), tending to 2*sqrt(1-e^(-1)).

falsifier.target_stronger_claims: A universal algebraic convergence rate from only qualitative condensation, or convergence uniformly over all k<=N.
falsifier.decisive_observation: Both failures occur at t=0 for the explicit smooth product sequences in C6 and C7, which satisfy the O(N) energy and fixed-k factorization assumptions.

data.claim: For N=3, B=Phi(|v-v_*|)b(cos(theta)), -3<gamma<=1, two-sided Phi(r)~r^gamma bounds, and two-sided angular bounds b(cos(theta))~theta^(-2-alpha) with 0<alpha<2, the linearized Boltzmann Dirichlet form around a fixed Maxwellian controls (i) the weighted L2 norm of h-P h from Theorem 1.1 and (ii) the local H^(alpha/2) norm of h-P h from Theorem 1.2. In particular b(theta)=a theta^(-2-2s), gamma=0, alpha=2s, 0<s<1 gives local H^s_v control for Maxwell molecules.
data.quantifiers_and_interface: For each admissible kernel B and every h in D(L_B), D_B(h)>=C_{gamma,alpha}||h-P h||^2_{H^(alpha/2)_loc(R^3)}. Precisely, for each fixed finite velocity ball B_R, this gives a positive c_R(B)>0 controlling the H^(alpha/2)(B_R) norm. P is the L2(M)-orthogonal projection onto span{1,v_1,v_2,v_3,|v|^2}. The theorem is velocity-only and has no spatial or time variable.
assumptions: N=3 and B=Phi(|v-v_*|)b(cos(theta))
-3<gamma<=1 and C_Phi r^gamma<=Phi(r)<=C'_Phi r^gamma for positive constants
0<alpha<2 and c_b theta^(-2-alpha)<=b(cos(theta))<=c'_b theta^(-2-alpha)
fixed homogeneous Maxwellian; source convention F=M(1+h), L2(M dv)
h belongs to the domain of the linearized operator
data.proof_evidence: Primary source theorem read directly. Its proof restricts velocities to B_R, uses Carleman representation to lower-bound the positive jump term by the fractional difference integral with kernel |v-v'|^(-3-alpha), controls the cancellation remainder by a second-order Taylor expansion, and closes the L2 error with the Maxwell-molecule spectral gap. Near grazing angles the remainder is finite because integral_0^1 theta^(1-alpha)dtheta<infinity.

acquired: proof mechanism and equilibrium rescaling from the source paper

data.constant_dependence: The primary source states constructive dependence on gamma, alpha, radial and angular kernel comparison constants, and N. For the exact angular multiplier a, D_a=a D_1, hence the best local coercivity constant scales exactly linearly with a. For a lower angular multiplier a_- and radial lower bound C_Phi, positivity gives a valid lower coefficient at least C_Phi*a_- times the reference-kernel coefficient. The cancellation remainder in the source proof contains an angular integral O((1-s)^(-1)) when alpha=2s, so that proof does not furnish a uniform endpoint bound as s approaches 1. No optimal asymptotic in s was extracted.
data.costs: Infinite-dimensional functional input, no oracle or sample acquisition, and no finite bit or runtime cost. The constant is constructive at fixed parameters but no numerical lower bound was extracted here. The proof reports local ball constants with possible exponential growth in R.
data.strongest_comparator: Gressman-Strain 2011 Lemma 2.5 gives a stronger global anisotropic geometric fractional coercivity estimate in N^(s,gamma), under a closely matching non-cutoff kernel class.
data.falsifier: For one admissible fixed kernel and fixed finite R, construct h_j in D(L_B) with P h_j=0 and D_B(h_j)/||h_j||^2_{H^s(B_R)} tending to zero. Such a sequence would contradict the stated theorem.

primary_sources.publication: Journal de Mathématiques Pures et Appliquées 87 (2007), 515-535; DOI 10.1016/j.matpur.2007.03.003

data.claim: For a fixed homogeneous Maxwellian and x-independent collision kernel on T_L^3, local velocity coercivity lifts mode by mode: for every fixed R, L^-3 integral_T D(h(x,.))dx >= c_R(s,a) sum_{m in Z^3} ||(I-P)h_hat_m||^2_{H^s(B_R)}. The constant is independent of L and the spatial mode m.
data.quantifiers_and_interface: Fix 0<s<1, a>0, R<infinity, and L>0. Let h belong to L2(T_L^3;D(L_B)) and let h_hat_m be its normalized Fourier coefficients at k_m=2 pi m/L. Then the displayed inequality holds, initially for finite Fourier sums and by density for the stated domain. The spatial measure is normalized by L^-3; with unnormalized measure both sides acquire L^3.
assumptions: same kernel and Maxwellian as the primary local coercivity theorem
collision operator acts only in v and is independent of x
fixed homogeneous equilibrium parameters rho,u,T
Fourier coefficients and D are in the domain needed for Parseval
data.proof: Since the collision form is local in x and quadratic, Parseval gives L^-3 integral D(h(x,.))dx=sum_m D(h_hat_m). Apply the primary source theorem to each coefficient; apply it separately to real and imaginary parts for complex modes. P acts only in v and is independent of m, so the sum of the mode inequalities is exactly the claim. No estimate of x derivatives is used.
data.constant_dependence: For B=a theta^(-2-2s) and gamma=0, c_R scales as a. Under Maxwellian M_{rho,u,T}, let lambda=sqrt(2T) and z=(v-u)/lambda. The source scaling is D_{rho,u,T}(h)=rho^2/pi^3 * lambda^gamma D_base(h(u+lambda z)); in z coordinates the coefficient for gamma=0 is rho^2/pi^3, independent of T and u. For physical v-patch norms, the L2 and homogeneous H^s pieces carry rho^2 lambda^(-3) and rho^2 lambda^(2s-3), respectively, on the patch B_{lambda R}(u). A positive lower density bound is necessary. The modewise c_R has no torus-length dependence.
data.costs: No new oracle, finite sample, or numerical computation. The derivation is one Parseval identity plus the source theorem; no arithmetic precision or conditioning cost is incurred. If the equilibrium parameters vary with x, Fourier modes couple and this corollary no longer follows as stated.
data.strongest_comparator: Gressman-Strain 2011 Lemma 2.5 controls a global anisotropic velocity norm and is stronger than the local isotropic H^s mode estimate. The current claim is useful only as an exact fixed-equilibrium Fourier lift.
data.falsifier: An admissible x-independent collision form for which Parseval fails to diagonalize the quadratic form, or a mode violating the source theorem, would refute the claim. For variable rho(x), u(x), or T(x), a counterexample to naive mode diagonalization is expected and that case is excluded.

streaming operator v dot grad_x
