data.title: Exact sequential Fock sampling for rational fermionic Gaussian states

scope.input: An n-mode fermionic Gaussian state supplied by an exact rational Majorana covariance; equivalently, a rational-complex BCS pair matrix with exact covariance construction.
scope.output: One occupation string distributed exactly according to the Born law; pure or mixed states, arbitrary phases, either fixed-parity sector.
scope.quantifiers: For every finite n and every valid rational covariance satisfying the Gaussian-state constraints.

data.statement: At each mode with covariance entry g=Gamma_(2j-1,2j), outcome s=2x_j-1 has conditional probability (1+s g)/2. For remaining indices a,b the conditional covariance is Gamma^s_ab=Gamma_ab-s(Gamma_ap Gamma_bq-Gamma_aq Gamma_bp)/(1+s g). Iteration samples the exact Fock law.
data.proof: Occupation projectors are single-mode Gaussian maps. The probability formula is their trace; Wick expansion of the conditioned two-point function gives the rank-two update. Gaussian closure and the Born chain rule prove the output distribution.

cost.arithmetic: O(n^3) rational operations and O(n^2) storage.
cost.bits: Polynomial in n and input height; a conservative prefix/Pfaffian bound is O(n^3 ell) bits for covariance-entry height ell. Exact rational branch probabilities avoid floating-point rare-prefix loss.
cost.randomness: Exact fair-bit Bernoulli draws terminate almost surely with expected polynomial random bits; worst-case coin flips are unbounded. K=ceil(log2(n/epsilon))-bit branch coins give a worst-case finite algorithm with TV error at most epsilon.
cost.energy: Classical sampler consumes no physical energy. Input-state preparation/encoding is separate.

data.strongest_baseline: Established fermionic linear-optics classical simulation, including Bravyi's Gaussian-map formalism and Terhal–DiVincenzo's noninteracting-fermion circuit simulation.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: A covariance supplied only as an unqualified noisy floating-point approximation is outside the exact-input theorem; a global interacting filter can make the conditional state non-Gaussian.
data.unresolved: The rational algorithm is derived but not implemented or proof-assistant checked. It does not solve completion sums for general quota or local filters.

data.title: Fixed-total-number BCS sampling by Pfaffian coefficient extraction

scope.input: An explicitly supplied rational pure fermionic Gaussian covariance or rational-complex pair matrix and a requested total particle number r.
scope.output: Exact occupation sample from the normalized r-particle sector, or exact detection that the sector has zero norm.
scope.quantifiers: For all finite mode counts n, all valid inputs, and all 0<=r<=n.

data.statement: For prefix h with k occupied bits, the completion mass in the r-particle sector is the coefficient [z^(r-k)]Q_h(z), where Q_h(z)=Tr[rho (product of prefix projectors)(product of remaining (Pi_0+z Pi_1))]. Wick's rule writes Q_h as one Pfaffian polynomial of degree at most n-|h|. Coefficient ratios give exact next-bit probabilities.
data.proof: Expand the diagonal generating operator as a sum over completion occupations. The coefficient is exactly the event mass. The Pfaffian minor identity evaluates this generating function from the Gaussian covariance. Child coefficients partition the parent mass, so the chain rule gives the sector-conditioned law.

cost.arithmetic: At most O(n^5) rational field operations by n+1 point evaluations/interpolation per prefix and cubic-time Pfaffians.
cost.bits: All evaluation/interpolation numerators and denominators have polynomial length in n and the pair-matrix encoding length; exact arithmetic has no inverse-sector-probability factor.
cost.energy: No physical postselection attempts are needed by the classical algorithm. A physical rejection implementation would cost 1/p_sector per accepted sample.

data.strongest_baseline: Grand-canonical Gaussian sampling followed by rejection, expected cost 1/p_sector; direct determinant identities give the unconditioned total-number partition polynomial.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: This fixes only total particle number. The no-double-occupancy constraint I intersect J=empty is an additional interacting filter and is not represented by this one-parameter coefficient.
data.unresolved: The interpolation sampler is a checkable derivation from Wick/Pfaffian identities, but has not been implemented or independently reviewed. Priority is not claimed.

data.title: Parity-sector probabilities contain binary-code coset weight enumerators

scope.input: A product Slater with one fermion in each disjoint two-mode block, followed by measurement conditioned on Hx=s over F_2.
scope.output: The exact parity-sector probability.
scope.quantifiers: Any finite binary matrix H, syndrome s, and rational site biases p_i; for strictly rational orbital entries the fixed-fugacity subfamily includes z=16/9 via orbital (3/5,4/5).

data.statement: Pr[Hx=s]=product_i(1-p_i) W_(H,s)(z), where z_i=p_i/(1-p_i) and W_(H,s)(z)=sum_(Hx=s) product_i z_i^(x_i). Exact zero-syndrome evaluation is #P-hard at any fixed rational z>0,z!=1 by the cited weight-enumerator result.
data.proof: The Slater determinant factors across disjoint orbital pairs, giving the independent Bernoulli law. The probability identity is direct summation over the code coset. Exact-hardness follows by the polynomial-time reduction to binary-code weight enumerators.

cost.input: n disjoint orbital pairs and a binary parity-check matrix; all orbital and filter encoding bits are charged.
cost.exact_count: A polynomial-time evaluator at a fixed nonunit fugacity would evaluate the cited #P-hard code weight enumerator.
cost.positive_cases: For graph-incidence zero syndrome and 0<=z<1, the Ising partition function has an FPRAS; bounded-treewidth Tanner graphs permit exact dynamic programming in 2^O(t) poly(n,L).
cost.energy: The Slater has exactly n fermions; postselection by physical repeated trials costs inverse sector probability.

data.strongest_baseline: At z=1, probability is exactly 2^(-rank H); graph-incidence zero-syndrome cases reduce to ferromagnetic Ising; bounded-treewidth checks are exactly solvable.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: At z=1 the claimed generic hardness does not apply; W(1)=2^(dim ker H). The reduction proves exact #P-hardness, not absence of an FPRAS for arbitrary parity constraints.
data.unresolved: No general relative-approximation hardness is proved for positive weighted code cosets. Nonzero-syndrome Ising FPRAS and arbitrary Tanner graphs remain outside the stated positive cases.

data.title: CNF-filtered occupation probability is #P-hard on block-product Slater and BCS states

scope.input: A supplied occupation distribution of a product Slater or BCS state and an explicitly listed CNF predicate on designated occupation bits.
scope.output: The exact accepted-event probability.
scope.quantifiers: For every CNF formula phi on m variables, the constructed instance has probability #SAT(phi)/2^m.

data.statement: Exact filtered-event evaluation is #P-hard under a one-query metric reduction. An FPRAS for this arbitrary-CNF-filter interface would yield an FPRAS for #SAT and hence NP=RP under the Jerrum–Valiant–Vazirani self-reduction.
data.proof: Each independent three-mode BCS block (or four-mode rational orthonormal Slater block) has four equiprobable configurations and a fair designated occupation bit. Filtering those m bits by phi yields exactly #SAT(phi)/2^m.

cost.encoding: BCS uses 3m modes with constant integer pair entries; Slater uses 4m modes and 2m particles with entries 0 or plus/minus 1/2; filter size is O(|phi|).
cost.approximation: Relative error is preserved by multiplication by 2^m; exact output has polynomial bit length.
cost.sampling: Unfiltered samples are trivial. Additive TV error must be below 2^-m to distinguish a single satisfying assignment from zero by event frequency.
cost.energy: No physical energy is required for a classical sample; a physical postselection implementation is charged by its accepted-event probability.

data.strongest_baseline: Independent block sampling exactly solves the unfiltered distribution.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: This uses an arbitrary CNF predicate. It does not prove hardness for the fixed local no-double-occupancy filter, fixed total number alone, or bare BCS sampling.
data.unresolved: The result is an interface reduction, not a complexity separation without NP!=RP; nearby constrained-DPP hardness is credited and novelty is not claimed.

data.title: Chen–Liu complementary log-concave FPRAS covers the N63 quota-filtered Slater count

scope.input: Explicit rational A in Q(i)^(m by r), mode blocks E_j, quotas q_j summing to r, and an acquired feasible quota support.
scope.output: Relative approximation and prefix probabilities for Z=sum_(S quotas) |det A_S|^2; coherent compiler is a separate extension.
scope.quantifiers: The transfer holds when the two homogeneous multiaffine nonnegative log-concave measures have supplied/computable rational value oracles, positive support starts, and polynomial-bit coefficient-range bounds.

data.statement: Cauchy–Binet gives f(x)=det(A*diag(x)A)=sum_|S|=r |det A_S|^2 x^S. With g(x)=product_j e_(|E_j|-q_j)(x_Ej), [x_all]fg=Z. The Chen–Liu Theorem 5.1 FPRAS therefore applies; prefix conditioning is by derivative/deletion and support is acquired by matroid intersection.
data.proof: Both factors are homogeneous, multiaffine, nonnegative and log-concave. Clearing denominators gives a polynomial-bit lower bound on positive determinant weights; a Hadamard bound gives a polynomial-bit upper range. Inclusion/exclusion preserves the class, and exact support routines provide zero branches and positive starts.

cost.count: One homogeneous count uses O(m^10 B^2 eta^(-2) log^2(2B/eta)) arithmetic/value-oracle operations, B=m+log(R_f R_g); N63's prefix coherent compiler has a larger O(m^13 B^2 epsilon^(-2) polylog) count component plus support, phase, reversible arithmetic, and gate synthesis.
cost.bits: Chen–Liu Remark A.4 caps exact rational random tapes to obtain a polynomial every-execution bit bound; all oracle outputs and range bounds must have polynomial bit encodings.
cost.energy: This is a classical count/coherent-preparation compiler, not a physical retry sampler; numeric energy cost is not part of this Slater interface.

data.strongest_baseline: Direct rejection from the original Slater has expected cost det(A*A)/Z and may be exponential. Support-only matroid intersection does not approximate Z.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: A condition-number-one block Slater can have quota probability 2^-r, refuting a generic polynomial-retry claim. The theorem does not automatically admit generic BCS Pfaffians, no-doublon filters, arbitrary sums or non-log-concave factors.
data.unresolved: Source theorem and finite-bit cap were audited at decisive sections but not proof-assistant certified; FPRAS, reversible count service, and coherent compiler are unimplemented and unexecuted.

data.title: All-size parity exchange proves support connectivity but not weighted mixing

scope.input: A nonnegative multiaffine right-half-plane Hurwitz-stable polynomial supported on one parity class.
scope.output: A sharp square-root coefficient-exchange inequality and support connectivity under pair flips.
scope.quantifiers: For every finite variable set and every supported S,T of the same parity, any pivot a in S symmetric-difference T satisfies the N84 inequality.

data.statement: sqrt(f(S)f(T)) is at most the sum over j in (S triangle T) without a of sqrt(f(S triangle {a,j})f(T triangle {a,j})); constant one is sharp.
data.proof: Full reciprocal twist by T preserves right-half-plane stability; zeroing outside the symmetric difference gives an even stable polynomial. Setting x_a=1 and x_j=w_j z yields an odd left-half-plane-rooted univariate polynomial. Its positive endpoints obey a0 ad<=a1 a_(d-1); optimize over positive w by Cauchy–Schwarz.

cost.combinatorial: Support graph diameter is at most |S triangle T|/2.
cost.numeric: No coefficient acquisition, bit-costed transition probabilities, or polynomial mixing bound follows from the inequality.
cost.energy: No microscopic transition-energy/Dirichlet cost is supplied.

data.strongest_baseline: N84 establishes aggregate support connectivity; N85 adds aggregate capacity/relocation under supplied balancing data.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: For the directed 2q-cycle pair matrix in fixed k=q, only two alternating pair-label supports survive; moves changing fewer than q labels disconnect. The two-mode F_t example has fixed support for all t!=0 but weights |t|^2 and 1.
data.unresolved: A computable microscopic two-replica energy/conductance bound or a more expressive positive coefficient representation remains missing; route-specific failures do not prove general hardness.

data.title: Small-loss output sampling for independent two-fermion blocks has quartic error

scope.input: Independent pure two-fermion Gaussian blocks, uniform per-mode vacuum survival eta_i, discarded loss record, followed by supplied Gaussian processing.
scope.output: A positive Gaussian-mixture surrogate sampler for the full final occupation/output law.
scope.quantifiers: For eta_i<1, each block has completion error delta_i<=eta_i^4/(2(1-eta_i)^2); joint TV is at most sum_i delta_i plus separate arithmetic/simulation error.

data.statement: An explicit finite phase average of pure Gaussian states reproduces the lossy vacuum, one-particle and two-particle sectors while adding only a higher-particle tail of mass delta_i. Tensor products and channel contractivity give the full-law TV bound.
data.proof: The phase average cancels cross-sector coherences. A scalar product polynomial fixes the vacuum/pair-sector weights; the remaining tail obeys delta_i<=b_i^2/(2a_i), a_i=(1-eta_i)^2, b_i=eta_i^2. Contractivity under later Gaussian processing gives the output bound.

cost.sampling: Polynomial time per sample after covariance acquisition; dense covariance update is O(M^3) arithmetic for M modes, plus finite mixture labels and separately charged precision.
cost.energy: With unit mode energy, expected surviving particles across blocks is 2 sum_i eta_i. No herald record is observed or rejected.
cost.precision: The analytic error is exact; a numeric root/phase implementation still needs a bit-precision bound. The archived float prototype is not certified.

data.strongest_baseline: Exact Gaussian simulation for eta=0 and the standard unobserved loss channel; the positive completion extends to a quantified small-loss regime.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Three-fermion blocks have an eta^3 obstruction; revealing a loss flag changes the local scale to eta^2. The bound is not uniform as eta_i approaches 1 and does not solve filtered-sector sampling.
data.unresolved: Completion proof is an internal candidate; source-reported diagnostics were not replayed. General mixed/high-particle blocks and certified numerical compilation remain open.

data.title: Conditional Gaussian-resource lower bound for preparing fermionic codes

scope.input: Independent lossy balanced four-mode magic blocks, Gaussian processing, and a target Majorana-distance codeword.
scope.output: A lower bound on the number of lossy blocks required for constant success/fidelity under the stated architecture.
scope.quantifiers: For a code with k>0, m physical modes, distance d_F>=3, and imported zero-non-Gaussian-gate Gaussian-overlap bound.

data.statement: At low per-mode survival loss parameter eta, fixed-target concentration costs Theta(eta^-4) blocks. The converse is p(1-epsilon)<= (1+R_eta)^L A^t, where R_eta=eta^4/[4(1-eta)^2], A=1-H_2^{-1}(k/m), and t=floor((d_F-1)/2).
data.proof: The balanced four-mode block has exact Gaussian robustness R_eta in the stated low-loss branch; multiplicative tensor domination and branchwise Gaussian-preserving monotonicity combine with Tang et al.'s Theorem 2 zero-gate overlap cap. Independent filters attain the exponent for fixed target 0<q<1.

cost.blocks: For fixed target and constant p, L=Omega(d_F/eta^4); the separable filter upper is O(eta^-4) for one fixed target block.
cost.energy: Each source block has expected surviving particle number 4 eta; physical ancillas and measurements for filtering are charged separately.
cost.precision: Filter s=eta(1-q)/(q(1-eta)); relative filter error xi gives explicit target shift and success-ratio change in leaf-08.

data.strongest_baseline: Independent Gaussian filters attain the fixed-target eta^-4 exponent; this is a resource-conversion bound, not a sampling-hardness claim.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: Imported code-overlap theorem is used only at zero extra non-Gaussian gates. No complexity separation, code-preparation achievability, arbitrary hardware, or q=1 claim follows.
data.unresolved: Tang's source theorem is not independently certified here; global experimental or fault-tolerant attainability and broader prior art remain open.

data.title: Exact determinant coefficient and paired-Gram representation of the fixed local filter

scope.input: Explicit A in Q(i)^(n by n), total rational input length L, and 0<=k<=floor(n/2).
scope.output: Exact fixed-filter normalizer Z_k(A)=sum_{|I|=|J|=k,I∩J=empty}|det A[I,J]|^2.
scope.filter: Only the intrinsic sitewise no-double-occupancy rule; no extra predicate.

data.statement: With X=diag(x), Y=diag(y), f=det(I+u X A Y A*) and g=product_i(x_i y_i+z x_i+z y_i), one has [x_1...x_n y_1...y_n u^k z^(2k)]fg=Z_k(A). Equivalently, for V=[I,A^T], G=V*V and P(S) selecting both columns for each site in S, Z_k(A)=sum_{|S|=k} det G[P(S),P(S)].
data.proof: Cauchy–Binet expands f as sum_{|I|=|J|}u^k|det A[I,J]|^2x^Iy^J. At every site, the local g factor completes the target squarefree monomial uniquely for occupancy patterns 00,10,01 and cannot complete 11, so exactly disjoint I,J survive. For the Gram form, Cauchy–Binet sums squared minors of V; the selected identity columns force rows S and the residual rows are a k-set in S^c.

cost.representation_size: O(n^2) rational entries plus O(n) variables; this is not an evaluation algorithm since direct summation still has binomial(n,k) terms.
cost.bits: After clearing entry denominators by D with log D<=L, nonzero Gaussian-integer minors have squared modulus at least 1 and Hadamard gives log coefficient range O(k(L+log n)); exact determinant and coefficient values have polynomial bit height.
cost.energy: This is a classical exact identity, so no physical energy is consumed. A physical postselection implementation separately pays W_k/Z_k attempts per success.

data.baseline: Unrestricted charge norm is a single coefficient of det(I+z A*A); the fixed no-double condition is the extra disjointness constraint.
data.boundary: The identity does not imply polynomial evaluation or sampling for arbitrary rank.
data.unresolved: External proof review and novelty are open. A legal polynomial-time coefficient service for the paired selector remains missing.

data.title: The two natural Chen–Liu complementary-coefficient lifts each fail one exact hypothesis

scope.input: The direct coefficient identity or the paired-Gram identity in FA2-01, in any nontrivial sector 1<=k<=floor(n/2).
scope.output: Exact route-specific log-concavity counterexamples; no universal impossibility claim.

data.statement: In the direct lift, A=[[0,1],[1,0]], k=1 gives minor factor F=x_1 y_2+x_2 y_1 with positive log-Hessian eigenvalue 1/2 at ones. In the Gram lift, the selector is e_(n-k)(x_(e_i)x_(f_i)); it fails log-concavity for every nontrivial k, since derivative/deletion reductions yield x_1x_2+x_3x_4, whose log-Hessian quadratic form on (1,1,-1,-1) at ones equals 2.
data.proof: Both are explicit Hessian computations. Differentiation in fixed paired variables and setting other paired variables to zero preserve multiaffine log-concavity; therefore the four-variable selector witness propagates to all nontrivial sector sizes.

cost.arithmetic: The witnesses use rational entries and exact integer Hessian data; no numerical tolerance is involved.
cost.representation: Chen–Liu's theorem has polynomial cost only if both complementary homogeneous factors are log-concave. The two factorizations meet degree, multiaffinity, bit-range, and oracle requirements but fail this load-bearing hypothesis.
cost.energy: No physical energy cost; this is an algebraic route audit.

data.baseline: Chen and Liu, arXiv:2610.06724v1, Theorem 5.1 and Remark A.4, give a conditional complementary-log-concave FPRAS.
data.boundary: These failures rule out only these two explicit factorizations and simple restriction-preserving lifts; different auxiliary-variable or Pfaffian representations remain possible.
data.unresolved: No general no-lift theorem is proved.

data.title: Exact bounded-rank algorithm and sampler for the fixed filter

scope.input: Rational-complex A of supplied or exactly detected rank d, fixed k, and sitewise no-double filter.
scope.output: Exact Z_k(A), exact zero-sector detection, and an exact classical sample from weights |det A[I,J]|^2/Z_k(A).
scope.quantifiers: All finite n,k,d; the runtime is fixed-parameter in d.

data.statement: Factor A=UV^T and transfer four exterior-algebra replicas over per-site states empty/up/down, never allowing both up and down at one site. The final degree-(k,k,k,k) diagonal contraction is exactly Z_k(A).
data.proof: Cauchy–Binet writes det A[I,J] as the inner product of the k-th exterior coordinates of U[I,:] and V[J,:]. Expanding the squared modulus introduces two replicas for each side. Exterior multiplication updates carry determinant signs; the three-state local update imposes I∩J=empty. Prefix completion masses from the same transfer give exact self-reduction sampling.

cost.normalizer: O(n d^2 16^d) rational-complex arithmetic operations and O(16^d) stored scalars when k>=d; replace 16^d by (sum_{j<=min(k,d)}binom(d,j))^4 for general k.
cost.sampler: A straightforward exact prefix sampler uses O(n^2 d^2 16^d) arithmetic operations.
cost.bits: Common-denominator integer factorization gives polynomial bit lengths in n,d,L; the leaf derives an explicit conservative DP bit-height bound and exact rational branch masses. Exact fair-bit draws have expected polynomial randomness but unbounded worst-case coin flips; a capped version incurs an explicit TV abort probability.
cost.energy: The classical DP uses no physical energy. Physical preparation followed by hard postselection costs exactly W_k/Z_k attempts per accepted output, which can remain exponential.

data.baseline: Direct enumeration costs binomial(n,k) times polynomial determinant work; unrestricted Gaussian covariance sampling does not include the local filter.
data.boundary: The 16^d dependence is exponential for unbounded rank; this does not solve arbitrary A or coherent state preparation.
data.unresolved: Mathematical proof is internal and no runtime implementation or external review was performed.

data.title: Exact bounded-block algorithm, with physical success probability charged separately

scope.input: A rational-complex pair matrix block diagonal under a supplied site partition of maximum block width w.
scope.output: Exact filtered and unfiltered fixed-k norms, an exact filtered Born sampler, and the exact physical no-double success probability.

data.statement: If u_b(x) and d_b(x) are block-local unfiltered and no-double charge polynomials, then W_k=[x^k]product_b u_b and Z_k=[x^k]product_b d_b. Local enumeration and coefficient DP give exact values and exact samples.
data.proof: For a block-diagonal matrix, every nonzero selected minor has equal row and column counts in each block, and its determinant factors into the block determinants. Disjointness is also blockwise. Convolution over block charge therefore gives the two identities and sequential completion-mass sampling.

cost.bit_time: O(s 4^w poly(w,L)+s k w poly(n,L)) bit operations for s blocks and input length L; polynomial for fixed or logarithmic w.
cost.sampling: Exact rational suffix masses; polynomial bit height, expected polynomial fair-bit cost and an optional explicit finite cap.
cost.conditioning: Classical runtime has no inverse-success factor. Physical retries have E[N]=W_k/Z_k and expected charged energy (E_p+sum_t e_t p_{t-1})/(Z_k/W_k).
cost.example: For s unitary swap blocks A_b=[[0,1],[1,0]], n=2s,k=s, W_k=binom(2s,s), Z_k=2^s, so p_G=2^s/binom(2s,s)~sqrt(pi s)2^-s despite condition number 1.

data.baseline: General dense exact enumeration has binomial(n,k) support terms; monomial/permutation matrices also have cycle-transfer algorithms from N89.
data.boundary: A sparse support graph alone is not a block-diagonal decomposition; arbitrary couplings between blocks are not covered.
data.unresolved: External proof review and practical runtime validation remain open.

data.title: Proposal-specific rejection, walk, Gaussian, and loss routes have exponential or algebraic barriers

scope.input: Only the explicitly named proposal algorithms and examples in the evidence files.
scope.output: Counterexamples to generic guarantees for those proposals, not a lower bound against all algorithms.

data.statement: There are condition-number-one block instances with exponentially small physical or Gaussian rejection acceptance; rational bounded-entry near-cycle matrices with exponentially slow mixing for one-label Metropolis walks; the local no-double projector is not one Gaussian occupation/parity branch; and N100 quartic loss completion conditioned on a k>=2 synthetic-tail event gives no useful conditional sampler guarantee.
data.proof: Exact formulas are given in the leaf results: block acceptance 2^s/binom(2s,s); a two-heavy-state cycle cut with bridge weight O(poly(n)2^-n); local projector rank 3 per site versus power-of-two rank for a single Gaussian occupation/parity branch plus a Wick-violating two-site state; and a four-site loss example where the postselected completion probability is about 3.07e-5 at eta=0.1 despite p_G=1.

cost.precision: All example matrices are rational with polynomial input bit length; small probabilities are exactly representable with polynomially many bits.
cost.energy: Physical retries are inverse acceptance. The examples do not prove a lower bound on direct classical algorithms.
cost.scope: Metropolis conductance applies only to the specified bounded-radius exchange chain.

data.baseline: Bounded-rank or bounded-block DPs can solve some examples directly, so proposal failure is not target hardness.
data.unresolved: No proposal-specific obstruction has been promoted to a general sampling lower bound.

data.title: Perfect-matching reduction proves exact #P-hardness of the fixed-filter normalizer

scope.input: A general graph H with even vertex count and a perfect-matching counting oracle for Z_k on rational matrices.
scope.output: Candidate exact #P-hardness and approximation-preserving transfer for the fixed no-double filter.
scope.filter: The target side uses exactly Z_k(A), with no additional event predicate.

data.statement: Exact Z_k is #P-hard under one-query metric reductions, already for k=n/2 and real rational A. After clearing denominators, Q^(2k)Z_k(A) is in #P, so the scaled integer-valued problem is #P-complete under metric reductions. An FPRAS for Z_k would imply an FPRAS for perfect matchings in general graphs.
data.proof: Start with a general graph H on even m vertices and E>=1 edges. If E<m, add a forced leaf edge uv and connect u to every old vertex; this preserves #PM and ensures E' >= m'. Let D=E-m and N=E+D=2E-m. In Q^N, make a pair (e_u,e_v) for every graph edge and D dummy pairs on private coordinates. At half filling, a nonzero N-column paired minor must include every dummy pair and m/2 graph-edge pairs; those vectors are a basis exactly for perfect matchings, with determinant ±1. Thus R(0)=#PM(H) for R(epsilon)=Σ_|S|=N/2 det([B+epsilon I,C]_{P(S)})^2. Every column of B is a coordinate vector, so its nonzero eigenvalues are roots of unity and B+epsilon I is invertible for rational 0<epsilon<1. Set A_epsilon^T=(B+epsilon I)^(-1)C; then R(epsilon)=|det(B+epsilon I)|^2 Z_(N/2)(A_epsilon). R has degree at most N and polynomial-bit rational coefficients/inputs, so N+1 evaluations interpolate #PM exactly. More strongly, a coordinate-vector column expansion gives |R(epsilon)-R(0)|<=8(N/2)2^N epsilon for N epsilon<=1/2; epsilon=2^-O(N+log N) makes the error <1/4, so one exact target query, exact scaling, and nearest-integer rounding recovers #PM. For membership, with Q clearing all denominators, Q^(2k)Z is a nonnegative integer sum over disjoint I,J; a #P machine guesses I,J and an integer below the squared Gaussian-integer minor modulus. Use #PM>=1 and choose epsilon from that lower bound and the requested tolerance, without knowing the count; a polynomial matching-existence test handles zero instances. An FPRAS estimate for Z, multiplied by the exact chart determinant square, then approximates #PM in one call.

cost.exact: N+1 rational target queries suffice by interpolation; alternatively one exact target query suffices with epsilon=2^-O(N+log N) and exact rounding. The dense rational chart has polynomial input bit length: each inverse-chart numerator/denominator has O(N(q+log N)) bits for q=log2(1/epsilon), so total encoding remains polynomial.
cost.approximation: For positive #PM, use the known lower bound #PM>=1 and choose epsilon with O(N+log(1/delta)) bits so the additive perturbation is at most delta/16, without knowing the count. Multiplying a delta/4 FPRAS estimate by the exact determinant scale gives the desired relative approximation in one call. This transfers the open general-graph #PM FPRAS problem; it is not an inapproximability theorem.
cost.energy: The reduction is classical. Physical hard-filter preparation has success Z_k(A)/W_k(A), expected attempts W_k/Z_k, and expected attempt energy E_try W_k/Z_k. These probabilities are exactly computable determinants but are not promised inverse-polynomial; no physical energy lower bound or efficient circuit synthesis follows.
cost.conditioning: For epsilon<=1/2, ||B+epsilon I||2<=2sqrt(N) and |det(B+epsilon I)|>=epsilon^N, giving kappa2(B+epsilon I)<=(2sqrt(N))^N epsilon^(-N). With q=O(N+log N), this is at most 2^O(N^2). The exact reduction uses rational arithmetic; no floating-point inversion or bounded-condition-number claim is needed. The chart A can be rank deficient, so its ordinary condition number may be infinite.
cost.sampling: The normalized paired-set law differs from the uniform perfect-matching law by TV at most Delta/(P-Delta), where Delta<=8K2^N epsilon and P=#PM>=1. A target TV sampler plus validity checking and edge-exposure self-reduction yields an FPRAS for general-graph perfect matchings; full confidence/sample accounting is in outputs/research/sol_fermionic_filter/RESULT.txt.

data.baseline: Valiant's permanent theorem gives #P-hardness of bipartite perfect-matching counts. An FPRAS for perfect matchings in general graphs remains open in Stefankovic–Vigoda–Wilmes (2017).
data.boundary: The FPRAS transfer reaches the open general-graph perfect-matching approximation problem; it gives no NP=RP implication and proves no absence of an FPRAS. A TV sampler for Z also transfers to an almost-uniform general-graph perfect-matching generator by the explicit normalized-law TV bound and validity rejection; edge-exposure self-reduction then gives an FPRAS. Neither consequence is an all-sampler lower bound. The exact reduction is metric, not parsimonious. Physical postselection success is not promised inverse-polynomial.
data.unresolved: External specialist proof review and priority/novelty audit remain open; Matoya–Oki 2019 §3.4 contains related graph-to-parity encodings. The direct reduction is not a physical-energy bound, and general arbitrary-rank FPRAS/sampling remains UNKNOWN.

data.title: Exact polynomial counting and sampling for the fixed filter on path and cycle nearest-neighbour matrices

scope.input: Explicit rational-complex n by n matrix A with zero diagonal and support contained in the two directed nearest-neighbour entries of each edge of one path or simple cycle; 0<=k<=floor(n/2).
scope.output: Exact Z_k(A) and an exact classical sample from the fixed-filter weights, when Z_k(A)>0.

data.statement: For a path, and for a cycle except the even half-filled sector described below, Z_k is the size-k weighted matching partition function on the underlying path/cycle with edge activity w_e=|A_ij|^2+|A_ji|^2. For an even cycle at k=n/2, the same DP plus two explicit interference corrections computes Z_k. All these cases have polynomial exact bit complexity and exact sampling.
data.proof: A square minor det A[I,J] is a signed sum over perfect matchings of the bipartite double-cover support graph induced by row set I and column set J. In a path this double cover is a forest, so it has at most one perfect matching. In an odd cycle it is a single 2n-cycle; selecting its entire cycle would require I=J=[n], forbidden by disjointness. In an even cycle it is two n-cycles. A multiple-term minor requires selecting an entire component, which under disjointness is possible only at k=n/2 for (I,J)=(Even,Odd) or (Odd,Even). Every other directed edge matching has a unique minor term. Summing the two orientations of each selected undirected edge yields activity w_e and the usual path/cycle matching DP. At the two exceptional outcomes, subtract the two alternating matching-term squared moduli from the base DP and add the exact squared two-term determinant. For sampling, use the DP self-reduction off the exceptional outcomes; at the exceptional even-cycle sector remove the four oriented matching atoms with a constant-state prefix DP tracking equality to the two forbidden parity orientations, then mix the residual mass with the two corrected exceptional outcomes.

cost.arithmetic: The matching coefficient and suffix completion masses use O(nk) exact rational arithmetic operations; cycle corrections use O(n) products and additions once edge order is fixed.
cost.bits: For total input bit length L and a common denominator D with log D<=L, k-edge weights share denominator D^(2k); the configuration count contributes O(n) further bits. All DP values therefore have O(kL+n) bits, giving O(nk poly(n,L)) bit complexity with standard integer arithmetic.
cost.sampling: Suffix self-reduction gives an exact classical sample with expected polynomial fair-coin cost; capping exact rational draws adds an explicitly chargeable abort-TV budget.
cost.energy: Classical DP has no energy cost. Physical preparation plus hard filtering still costs W_k/Z_k expected attempts and can be exponential.

data.baseline: General dense exact enumeration has binomial(n,k)^2 minor candidates. N89 gives exact transfer for monomial/permutation matrices; this path/cycle result allows two directed entries per site but only nearest-neighbour support.
data.boundary: No result is proved for branched sparse graphs, dense matrices, or general BCS pairing. For cycles the only interference correction is even length at half filling; the no-double condition is essential to that classification.
data.unresolved: The combinatorial proof is internally derived; external proof review and novelty audit remain open. An independently assigned leaf is finishing a targeted derivation and exact diagnostic.

data.claim: For gamma_L=L(4J+V_L)=-kappa/L, V_L=-4J-kappa/L^2, beta=tau L^2 and bounded lambda, the coherent profile theta gives liminf L^-1 log Z_L >= tau Gamma(theta), where Gamma=kappa int sin^4(theta/2)+lambda int sin^2(theta/2)-(J/2)int|theta prime|^2. If the supremum Phi_coh is positive, the full Gibbs particle number is macroscopic: for some epsilon>0, P(N>=epsilon L)->1 exponentially.
data.proof: LEAD_SUPPLEMENT.txt §A. The product state gives the Riemann-sum lower bound. In sector m, Hcrit>=Hneu and W<=m yield Z_{L,m}<=A^m from the reflecting-exclusion heat trace Tr_m exp(-tau L^2 Hneu)<=(e C_tau)^m; compare the low-number sum with the exponential partition lower bound.
data.costs: Trial preparation has L-1 local rotations and O(L) evaluations; angle precision O(log L) bits per site suffices for O(1) exponent error. The result is asymptotic and is not a Gibbs sampler. Failure probability for N<epsilon L is exp[-(tau Phi_coh-epsilon log A)L+o(L)].
data.baseline: A pure coherent trial proves only a partition lower bound without the sector heat estimate; the latter upgrades it to a high-probability density statement.
data.boundary: Phi_coh positivity is sufficient only. Equality of the speed-L free-energy limit with tau Phi_coh and the true transition are UNKNOWN.

data.claim: Let C_tau=1+2 sum_{r>=1}exp(-8J tau r^2). For gamma_L=-kappa/L, full-Fock particle number is uniformly tight if e C_tau exp(tau(kappa+lambda))<1. For every gamma_L>=0, including arbitrary gamma_L->0+, the full-Fock number is uniformly tight if e C_tau exp(tau lambda)<1.
data.proof: LEAD_SUPPLEMENT.txt §B. Use the exact graph-form inequality Hcrit,m>=Hneu,m, the operator bounds W<=m and gamma_L L W>=0, min-max, and the all-m reflecting-exclusion heat trace estimate (5.5) in outputs/research/sol_attractive_critical/proof.txt. The resulting sector weights are bounded by a summable geometric sequence.
data.costs: Uniform analytic tail P(N>K)<=r^(K+1)/(1-r); C_tau has a Gaussian series with O(sqrt(log(1/delta))) terms for additive precision delta. The condition is conservative and provides no preparation algorithm.
data.baseline: This is a sufficient tightness region, not the sharp Bose/GP chemical-potential threshold.
data.boundary: Outside the displayed low-lambda regime the bound does not decide tightness. It gives no matching speed-L free-energy upper.

data.claim: For S=L-1, the marginal XXZ target H_L equals C_L I - J Hdiag(Delta_L,Delta_L,Delta_L) + b_L sum_i Z_i with Delta_L=1+kappa/(4JL^2), b_L=(kappa+lambda)/(2L^2), and the stated exact scalar C_L. Equivalently H_L=4J Delta_L H^1_{[1,S]}-(kappa+lambda)N/L^2 in the open ferromagnetic XXZ droplet convention.
data.scope: Every L>=2, J>0, kappa>=0, real lambda; both endpoint fields retained, including both terms on the same site at L=2.
data.proof_evidence: Direct Pauli expansion; exact Fraction matrix checker for L=2,...,7.
data.limitations: No novelty claim; not a finite-bit Bethe solver and not a proof of Bethe-root completeness in the isotropic singular limit.

data.claim: Under the FA2-SA1 compact-gap assumptions, D(rho_{L,V}||rho_{L,0}) tends to zero uniformly in tau, lambda, and V; Pinsker gives trace distance convergence of the interacting state to the finite-L free reference.

data.claim: Uniform convergence D(rho_{L,V_L}||rho_{L,V=0})->0 over every bounded sequence V_L>-4J with g_L=L(4J+V_L)->infinity.
data.counterexample: At lambda=0 choose finite g_j->infinity with f_infinity(g_j)->f_TG, d_j=f_infinity(g_j)-f_infinity(g_j+1)>0. Fixed-g LL partition convergence, free partition convergence, and convexity give thresholds L_j so -f'_L(g_j)>=d_j/2 and both relevant partition functions are within 1/j of their limits for every L>=L_j. Increase L_j so L_j d_j>=j, 4J L_j>=2g_j, and g_j/L_j<=1/j. Set g_L=g_j on [L_j,L_{j+1}) and V_L=-4J+g_L/L. Then g_L->infinity and V_L->-4J, so FA2-SA3 gives trace-norm convergence to Tonks, but the exact Gibbs identity gives D>=Jj-3/j on block j; hence relative entropy diverges.
data.audit: Independently checked by /root/sol_kls_consequences on 2026-10-08. The strict decrease d_j>0 follows because the finite-g two-particle ground state has nonzero contact trace; all other sector eigenvalues are nondecreasing in g. This is an existential diagonal sequence, not an effective finite-bit schedule.
data.supplied_inputs: The internally proved fixed-g finite-chain-to-Lieb-Liniger partition convergence, free XX partition convergence, monotone g-to-infinity form limit, and trace theorem FA2-SA3.
data.costs: No effective thresholds/rate are supplied; existence is sufficient to disprove uniform KL convergence. The sequence has V_L->-4J but g_L->infinity, with no claim on the optimal growth threshold for KL divergence.
data.baseline: Trace distance convergence does hold along the counterexample sequence. The result demonstrates that trace norm does not control this relative entropy under the changing reference Gibbs energy observable.
data.falsifier: A flaw in strict finite-g contact monotonicity, the fixed-g partition convergence, or the exact Gibbs identity; the independent audit found none under those dependencies.

data.claim: For the open L-1-site hard-core chain with H_L=Hcrit+(g_L/L)W-(lambda/L^2)N, beta=tau L^2, fixed J,tau>0, |lambda|<=B, and g_L->g<0, the full-Fock partition function satisfies L^(-2) log Z_L -> tau|g|. For every fixed K, P(N<=K)->0, in fact at most exp(-tau|g|L^2+o(L^2)); each fixed-m canonical sector contribution is O_m(1).
data.proof: ../negative_scaled_coupling/RESULT.txt §§1-4. The exact open-endpoint graph form gives Hcrit>=0. A product state with a width floor(sqrt(L)) spin-coherent boundary ramp has exact expectations <Hcrit>=2Jw(1-cos(pi/w)), <N>=L-w-2, and <W>=L-(3/2)w-2+(w/4)cos(pi/w). Gibbs variational principle gives the lower free-energy rate; Hcrit>=0, W<=L-2 and N<=L-1 give the matching upper bound. For fixed m, a contraction to the labeled cube, an orbit-counting collision bound, a one-dimensional discrete diagonal trace inequality, and the reflecting-exclusion heat-kernel estimate give a uniform O_m(1) sector bound. The independent audit found a missing L^2 factor in the written kinetic consequence; it has been corrected in equations (9)-(11), and the constants then imply (12).
data.supplied_inputs: Open chain, fixed J,tau, bounded lambda, and a convergent bounded sequence g_L->g<0. No particle-number cutoff or eigenbasis is supplied.
data.acquired_inputs: Finite-sector comparison and reflecting-exclusion heat-trace bound are proved in the result. The finite-g attractive Lieb-Liniger form is only noted as lower bounded and trace class; lattice-to-attractive-LL convergence is not claimed.
data.costs: The trial has L-1 qubits and O(L) single-qubit rotations, with O(L) observable evaluations. A conservative total state error delta requires O(log(L/delta)) angle bits per rotation; delta=O(L^-3) controls the variational exponent at O(1) under the stated operator scale. Full partition evaluation still has dimension 2^(L-1). No sampler or sampler lower bound follows. Exact algebra checks pass for three boundary ramps; they are finite evidence only.
data.baseline: The fixed-m attractive Lieb-Liniger contact operator is lower bounded and has finite heat trace; this does not bound the grand-canonical lattice tail. The coherent ramp supplies a macroscopic-occupation trial with subleading critical-gradient cost.
data.falsifier: An error in the exact endpoint-inclusive form identity or ramp expectations, failure of the variational upper/lower matching, or a counterexample to the corrected fixed-m trace estimate. A scoped independent audit checked the fixed-m constants after the L^2 correction.

data.claim: Commuting-operator threshold parallel repetition
data.statement: For a finite two-player game G with commuting value v<1, finite answer-product d, minimum question-pair resampling gap sigma across support components, every k>=1 and 0<delta<1-v, every arbitrary-dimensional commuting strategy satisfies Pr[W_k >= ceil((v+delta)k)] <= exp(-sigma*delta^3*k/(2048*(1+ln d))). The denominator improves to 1024*(1+ln d) for connected pair support.
data.inputs_and_costs: The question law, finite alphabets, predicate, and resampling gaps are supplied. No tensor-product representation, finite strategy dimension, or optimizer is assumed. The theorem's exponent is explicit; acquiring sigma for a succinct sampler remains a separate cost.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Independent reconstruction covers zero-spectrum resolvent transport, commuting POVM dilation, mixed exposure, component barycenter, Poincare, and ceiling rounding; no internal counterexample found. External/formal proof review is still required. A counterexample to the exposure inequality or a conditional transported POVM leaving its same amplified algebra would falsify the proof route.
data.limits: Truth status is separate from novelty/priority, which is UNKNOWN. No finite-dimensional representation, local Hamiltonian, QPCP theorem, or tensor/commuting value equality follows.

data.claim: One-sided erasure acquires a constant question-chain gap for a named verifier
data.statement: Erasing Alice's question with probability 1/4 yields omega_skip=1/4+3*omega/4, connected question support, and resampling gap at least (2-sqrt(3))/4>1/15. For Lin's source-reported coRE-complete family this changes no value <=1/2 to <=5/8. Conditional on GH-01, all-wins repetition has value <=exp(-27*k/(7864320*(1+ln d))) in the no case, where d=(|A|+1)|B|.
data.inputs_and_costs: Adds two random bits and one Alice question tag per copy. k-fold randomness, wires, and predicate time scale linearly in k. For base answers of a bits, 1+ln d<=2a+2 (or <=2a+3 under common fixed-length padding); polynomial target exponent needs k=ceil(7864320*(2a+2)*L/27).
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Wrapper value and maximal-correlation calculation were independently checked. Repetition conclusion inherits GH-01 validation status. Exact certificate 4*13^2>3*15^2 verifies the rational lower bound 1/15. A mismatch in branch law or a failure of the projection/maximal-correlation lemma would falsify the acquisition proof.
data.limits: The wrapper appears in the supplied prior proof; this is an independent audit/application, not a novelty claim. Polynomially small soundness does not lift MIPco beyond coRE. No Hamiltonian locality follows.
data.evidence: work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/02_lin_wrapper.txt; work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/12_gap_certificate.txt

data.claim: Generic coRE-complete commuting-game acceptance cannot be uniformly compiled to finite computable separated-threshold matrices
data.statement: Assuming Lin's MIPco=coRE theorem, no total computable compiler on every instance of its promised coRE-complete family can output a finite effectively approximable Hermitian matrix with effectively certified separated minimum-eigenvalue thresholds for yes and no cases. No polynomial dimension/runtime assumption is needed.
data.inputs_and_costs: A hypothetical compiler plus effective entry precision and finite dimension lets one approximate the matrix in operator norm and decide a coRE-complete language. This is a uniform-family argument; it does not need L02 if one starts from the source family, and the claimed exponential repetition element remains an infinite-algebra object.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: The computability reduction is direct. Its external premise is Lin's source theorem, not independently re-proved here. A purported compiler must escape by restricting the family, losing effective finite dimension/entry access, or losing a certified threshold separation.
data.limits: Does not exclude a compiler for decidable QMA/local-Hamiltonian instances, does not refute quantum PCP, and does not say a particular game has no finite-dimensional near-optimal strategy.

data.claim: Positive local syndrome testing has a sharp r/t bound
data.statement: For one fixed auxiliary Hilbert space, K_x=sum_a w_a E_{a,x|S_a}, w_a>=0, sum_a w_a=1, 0<=E<=I, x-independent weights and |S_a|<=r, if inf spec(K_0)<=eta and K_x>=cI for every nonzero x in {0,1}^t, then c<=eta+(r/t)(1-eta). Under total positive term-norm budget L, the sharp bound is c<=eta+(r/t)(L-eta).
data.inputs_and_costs: No commutation or finite auxiliary dimension is required. The proof uses a near-ground vector at zero and averages singleton syndromes. It assumes all singleton sectors and an all-state lower bound in the same auxiliary space.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Short dimension-free variational proof reconstructed, including continuous-spectrum infimum handling; exact scalar examples attain equality. Finite rational script checks fixtures only. A counterexample must violate one of the fixed-space, fixed-weight, positivity-budget, local-support, or all-state premises.
data.limits: Not a no-go for globally positive sparse matrices, signed cancellation, off-diagonal sector coupling, x-dependent auxiliary encodings, or all QPCP reductions. Priority/novelty is UNKNOWN.

data.claim: Global positivity and low signed degree do not imply the positive local-budget barrier
data.statement: The rational t=4 polynomial p(x)=(3/5)sum_i x_i-(3/10)sum_{i<j}x_i*x_j is a contraction on [0,1]^4, p(0)=0, and p(x)>=3/5 for every nonzero Boolean x, despite signed degree 2. The Chebyshev approximate-OR family gives constant Boolean gap and degree O(sqrt(t)) while remaining globally between 0 and 1 on the real cube.
data.inputs_and_costs: These are tests on supplied syndrome bits. The t=4 signed coefficient l1 norm is 21/5; any positive degree-2 term realization with the same gap requires total positive budget at least 6/5. For the asymptotic Chebyshev family signed l1 is Omega(t), and N26 requires positive budget Omega(sqrt(t)); a complete monomial expansion need not be polynomial-size, though the diagonal matrix is 1-sparse with an entry oracle.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Exact algebraic derivations are in the leaf; 221 Boolean Chebyshev fixtures and the t=4 rational example were checked by the included standard-library script. The analytic family proof is not replaced by finite enumeration. A flaw in the real-cube Chebyshev bound or Boolean minimum would falsify the construction.
data.limits: This is not an encoding of the actual overlapping five-qubit hard Hamiltonian and does not refute GH-04. It proves that positive total norm alone cannot substitute for a positive local decomposition budget.
data.evidence: work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/06_beyond_positive_budget.txt; outputs/research/games_hamiltonians/verify_exact_checks.py

data.claim: Current qLTC/HDX sources do not provide the required energy gap or common positive sparse encoding
data.statement: BNZ Theorem 9.3 amplifies combinatorial support soundness and its constant-cap case assumes both a robust single-shot decoder and an O(1)-depth error suppressor. The two fresh qLTC preprints state code parameters but not that package. Their code-check inequalities give normalized code-Hamiltonian gap on the order of 1/N; bounded incidence also gives an O(1/N) single-site upper bound. Independently, an explicit normalized 1-local family has combinatorial violation fraction exactly 1/2 and ground energy Theta(4^-n), so support soundness alone gives no inverse-polynomial energy floor. The BNZ output theorem does not state ordinary expectation-energy soundness or the common V,C,B encoding interface.
data.inputs_and_costs: Results and theorem interfaces were read from cited arXiv v1 primary sources; their long proofs were not independently audited here. A route to L02 would additionally need an actual two-question pair law equal to an expanding HDX walk plus a predicate and value separation. A route to N11 needs one common efficiently represented isometry, positive sparse invalid-space penalty, and compressed logical-energy comparison.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Source-reported theorem claims plus independently checked toy counterexamples. A decoder/suppressor construction satisfying the exact BNZ assumptions, or a quantitative amplitude-to-support conversion, would change the conclusion. An HDX walk gap alone does not provide a verifier predicate.
data.limits: This is a scope/conversion finding, not a refutation of qLTCs, BNZ amplification, quantum PCP, or existence of a different positive sparse encoding.
data.evidence: work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/20_qtc_hdx_l02.txt; work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/21_hdx_energy_gap.txt; work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/23_hdx_prior_art.txt; work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/24_hdx_gap_certificate.txt

data.claim: Reversible expanding walks transfer to endpoint-pair resampling gap, conditional on using that pair law
data.statement: For finite reversible R with stationary pi, the endpoint law mu(u,v)=pi(u)R(u,v) has maximal correlation ||R|| on mean-zero L2(pi), and its two-coordinate resampling gap is at least (1-||R||)/2. Thus a certified ||R||<=beta<1 gives sigma_question>=(1-beta)/2.
data.inputs_and_costs: A finite exact certificate may provide rational R and an LDL^T witness that B^T(beta I-R)B is positive semidefinite on the mean-zero subspace. For N states and dense witness, size O(N^2) and verification O(N^3 poly(bit length)); sparse transition acquisition is O(N Delta). Fixed-bit sampling additionally charges relative approximation and total-variation loss.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: The projection/maximal-correlation transfer proof is direct and recorded. No particular BNZ HDX matrix, rational beta, LDL witness, two-prover predicate, or game-value theorem was acquired. A counterexample to the endpoint-law operator-norm identity or a wrong pair law would falsify an application.
data.limits: The source-reported routing walk does not itself define a game. Its asymptotic alpha/poly(d)lambda presentation needs explicit constants or a finite witness before it is a numerical named-verifier certificate.
data.evidence: work/programmes/games_hamiltonians/leaves/24_hdx_gap_certificate.txt

data.claim: The cubic sigma*delta^3 repetition exponent is not shown tight or removable

This demonstrates instance-wise looseness but neither refutes the uniform commuting bound nor proves sigma removable. Existing odd-cycle and Feige-Verbitsky controls do not force the cubic dependence or full logarithmic alphabet term.
data.inputs_and_costs: Finite game and explicit repeated strategy; details and source records are in the leaf. The small-gap sampler and examples do not yield a counterexample to the theorem quantifiers.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Exact example calculations reported; the sharp uniform exponent problem remains open in this programme. A family of commuting strategies matching or violating the uniform dependence is needed.
data.limits: Do not infer a uniform improvement from an individual game's binomial control.

data.statement: For the specified two-branch isometry built from a pair of five-qubit seed bases with relative non-monomial Clifford coherence mu<=1/sqrt(2), every nonzero exact row of an image enforcer has support at least 1+2^(t/2).

data.claim: Exact BMVZ seed-pair occurrence in a hardness-preserving augmented family
data.statement: Starting from a constant-color bounded-degree 5-local QMA-hard layered family H_base=sum_chi v_chi H_chi, add the two BJSW five-qubit seed projectors P_phi and P_psi on fresh ancillas as separate singleton colors of weight 1/4 each, scaling the original color weights by 1/2. Then H_aug=(1/2)H_base tensor I+(1/4)P_phi+(1/4)P_psi and lambda_min(H_aug)=lambda_min(H_base)/2. BMVZ Definition 1.6 allows positive layer weights and its small-layer rule repeats singleton clauses, so the exact repeated clauses Q_(v,T)=I-(I-|v><v|)^{tensor T} occur at every iteration. This does not establish membership in the particular unmodified canonical BJSW term table.
data.inputs_and_costs: The original family, its bounded-degree coloring, and the BMVZ weighted layered/path interface are supplied. The augmentation adds only 5 fresh qubits and two 5-local projectors; each new seed qubit has incidence two. Color count stays constant and minimum color weight stays bounded below. The QMA promise thresholds scale by exactly 1/2.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: The common kernel of the two rank-one seed projectors has dimension at least 30, so the minimum energy of their sum is zero and the tensor-sum minimum separates. A failure of the source's positive layer-weight/small-layer rule or of the stated color interface would falsify the BMVZ membership step.
data.limits: The abstract BMVZ definition does not certify the pair in an unmodified input or adjacency list. This is a constructed augmented family. It is not an encoding theorem or novelty claim.
data.evidence: bmvz_bjsw_source_audit.md; positive_encoding_cycle2.md; bmvz_bjsw_seed_pair_test.py

data.claim: Pair-only repeated seed has a constant-comparison sparse logical lift and a reversible-cube gap tradeoff
data.statement: For T repeated BJSW seed blocks, V|psi>=2^(-T/2)sum_x|x>U_x|psi>, with U_x=tensor_i U_(x_i), and B=I_branch tensor [I-tensor_i(I-|0^5><0^5|_i)] give a positive diagonal 1-row-sparse operator whose compression E=I-tensor_i(I-Q_i), Q_i=(P_phi+P_psi)/2, obeys q_-H_pair<=E<=q_-^(-1)H_pair, where H_pair=(Q_(phi,T)+Q_(psi,T))/2 and q_-=(1-1/(2sqrt(2)))/2>0.32. Every reversible uniform-cube kernel with jumps of at most q coordinates has Poincare gap at most 2q/T. Its Clifford-covariant connector has gap at most q/T and row support at most 1+s*8^q for degree s. Thus polynomial row support forces gap O(log(T)/T) within this connector class.
data.inputs_and_costs: The T-bit branch register and T five-qubit data blocks have polynomial size. V is a product controlled-Clifford circuit; B has diagonal 0/1 entries and an O(T)-time row/entry procedure. For a degree-s connector with maximum jump q, the row bound is 1+s*8^q. The bit-flip walk has row support at most 1+8T and connector gap 1/T.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: The compression follows by averaging independent branch bits. The local nonzero eigenvalues of Q_i are q_- and 1-q_-; product principal cosines bound the pair Hamiltonian on the complement of its common kernel. For the gap bound, signed coordinate sums have variance T and sign-averaged Dirichlet form at most 2q. data.claim: Direct branch frames with branch-dependent pure workspaces require a wide exact enforcer row

If there are at least two classes, every matrix C with ker C=ran V has a computational-basis row with at least ceil(1+1/mu) nonzeros. For the two repeated BJSW frames, mu=2^(-3T/2), giving ceil(1+2^(3T/2)) even with arbitrary branch-dependent pure workspaces.
data.inputs_and_costs: Finite-dimensional logical and workspace registers are arbitrary in size. The branch amplitudes and pure workspace states are arbitrary. The theorem needs exact kernel equality but not C positivity or a quantitative gap; the target positive-gap condition implies its kernel premise.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Collapse each enforcer row by branch workspace amplitudes. Rank comparison forces a nonzero dependence among at least two representative frame rows; Gershgorin's criterion makes every set of fewer than ceil(1+1/mu) such rows independent. An explicit direct-frame counterexample with a narrower exact enforcer would falsify the lemma.
data.limits: This exact bound is for the two seed branches. It is not an exponential-row lower bound for the whole BMVZ list: the maximum coherence across all path branches may remain constant, and one branch per color does not encode the within-color path average. Data-dependent workspaces and active isometries are outside the theorem.

data.claim: Whole-list path-history encoding achieves exact constant logical comparison but only an inverse-polynomial image gap
data.statement: For an explicit polynomial-size BMVZ clause list flattened to R fixed-k local algebraic projectors, with exact local diagonalizers U_i and diagonal projectors D_i, a polynomial clock-history isometry V and positive contractions B,C exist with ker C=ran V, V*BV=(Q/K)H where 1/4<Q/K<=1, row support at most 1 for B and 9 for C, and C>=[(1-cos(pi/K))/2](I-VV*). The relative decoder factors across R disjoint blocks; each factor acts on at most 2k qubits and has a constant-size exact one-/two-qubit algebraic decomposition. K is polynomial in the clause count, transition-gate count and common weight denominator, so the gap is Theta(K^-2), not constant.
data.inputs_and_costs: The exact local term-matrix representation is part of the input interface and is polynomial-bit algebraic. The output has n'+log_2 K qubits. V has a polynomial-size controlled local-gate circuit. B has a polynomial-time diagonal entry oracle; C has at most 9 entries per row and a polynomial-time row/entry oracle. C terms act on the full log_2 K clock plus at most 2 data qubits; B's D_j can be global on the data. Hence constant locality is not established. Exact local diagonalization and two-qubit gate synthesis are polynomial in bit height for fixed k; C coefficients have polynomial bit height and constant algebraic degree under the stated input model.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: The clock positions repeat each clause decoder for q_j=Qw_j tail positions and insert relative local gates between tails. Each C edge is positive. Gauge conjugation gives one quarter of the path Laplacian, yielding the stated exact kernel and gap; averaging B over tails gives (Q/K)H. A matrix entry, kernel, or compression counterexample to these identities would falsify the construction.
data.limits: This is a complete positive sparse-row lift under the explicit exact local algebraic-matrix representation; approximate-entry-only inputs need an additional perturbation proof. It reaches only inverse-polynomial gap and growing clock locality. It does not meet constant gap, constant locality, or quantum-PCP requirements.

data.claim: Any positive sparse enforcer of the fixed full-list history image has a repetition-dependent gap upper bound
data.statement: Let P be the exact kernel projection of a finite positive contraction C<=I with first positive eigenvalue gamma and maximum row support s. If a row i has projection mass at least m on J and each squared entry on J is at most a, then for D=log(m/(2a))/log(s+1)>1, gamma <= [log(8/m)/(4(D-1))]^2. For the augmented BMVZ singleton seed tails in the banked full-list uniform-history image, chosen Clifford decoders give (m,a)=(q/K^2,1/(K^2*8^T)) with q=Q/4. More generally, for any factorwise decoders across the T seed copies, the fixed overlap |<phi,psi>|^2=1/8 gives a selected row with every squared relative entry <=(7/8)^T, hence (m,a)=(q/K^2,(7/8)^T/K^2). This yields gamma <= [log(8K^2/q)log(s+1)/(4(log(q*(8/7)^T/2)-log(s+1)))]^2 whenever D>1. The result also covers decoders that mix the full base data copy, provided endpoints factor across copies and diagonalize P_phi tensor I and P_psi tensor I. For T dominating log K+log s the bound is O((log K log(s+1)/T)^2); it tends to zero when T>>log K log(s+1), in particular for K,s<=n^b and T>=n^c with fixed positive exponents.
data.inputs_and_costs: Finite-dimensional positive contraction, exact kernel projector, row support s, and the stated projector-row mass/entry bound. The application uses the explicitly augmented two singleton seed layers, history length K, repeated seed count T, and exact BMVZ seed overlap. No decomposition of C, row oracle, reversibility, covariance, or locality assumption is needed. The arbitrary-decoder extension needs factorwise endpoint decoders across T copies; they may act on the entire base data copy. It excludes constant all-state gap for polynomial row support on these fixed uniform-history images, including basis-injective monomial classical workspace recodings.
data.proof_status_and_falsifier: Degree-l Chebyshev filtering approximates P in operator norm by 2 exp(-2l sqrt(gamma)); a degree-l polynomial in C has row support at most (s+1)^l. Any omitted target projection-row mass bounds approximation error below. Choosing l=ceil(log(8/m)/(4sqrt(gamma))) yields the formula. For arbitrary factorwise decoders, the selected phi row has one entry of square 1/8 by the seed overlap and unit row norm, so every entry square is at most 7/8; tensoring yields (7/8)^T. For a full-base-copy decoder the identity P_phi P_psi P_phi=(1/8)P_phi gives the same row cap. An exact sparse positive contraction for the same image with a gap violating the bound, or a failure of the seed-tail projector-row data, would falsify the claim.
data.limits: The no-go applies only to the exact uniform-history image with factorwise endpoint decoders across T copies, and survives basis-injective monomial recodings. It does not cover a global decoder of the amplified OR projector, coherent quantum workspace maps, or redesigned isometries; it does not constrain logical B and does not imply a quantum PCP result. The separate Clifford stabilizer construction has a constant-gap enforcer, so this cannot be generalized to all Clifford images. External proof validation and novelty remain UNKNOWN.

data.title: Finite global torus rank obstruction at the coefficient-4 endpoint
data.theorem: There exists a smooth complete proper metric g on R×S² with λ4≥2 and λa=−∞ for every real a<4, where Qa(φ)=∫(a|dφ|²+Rgφ²). For every fixed finite k and globally smooth diagonal torus warps p1,…,pk, inf R(g+Σe^(2pi)dθi²)=−∞.

Dip tests ζ/f have bounded Q4 and gradient energy ≥1/(72δj), forcing λa=−∞ below 4. The finite-warp scalar formula reduces any lower bound to a positive supersolution for coefficient ak=4k/(k+1)<4.

data.title: Pure-symbol reconstruction for relative height-one field pairs

data.title: Relative p-rank two hypothesis is sharp
data.theorem: For every prime p, the pairs (Fp(t),Fp(t)^p) and (Fp²(u),Fp²(u)^p) are nonisomorphic rank-one field pairs but have isomorphic countably infinite V spaces and identically vanishing pure-symbol predicates.

data.title: Shifted simultaneous power-free polynomial values are recurrence parameters exactly at good shifts
data.theorem: For fixed k>=2 and a finite family F=(f_i) of nonzero integer polynomials, each separable over Q with every nonconstant irreducible factor of degree at most k+2, assume the joint local condition |Omega_p|<p^k for every prime p. Conditional on the pinned 2026 power-free density Corollary 1.3, for every integer r the shifted set A_{F,r}={n>=1:n+r is a simultaneous k-power-free input for F} is an averaging set of polynomial multiple recurrence iff every f_i(r) is k-power-free.
data.assumptions: The number-theoretic positive-density Euler-product theorem is imported from OpenAI Math Release preprint 020, Corollary 1.3 (24 Sep 2026), and is not externally validated here. The dynamics implication uses Bergelson-Kulaga-Przymus-Lemanczyk-Richter, Definition 1.1 and Theorem 1.4.
data.proof_mechanism: Finite-prime truncations are periodic and converge to 1_A_F in Besicovitch density because their densities converge to the Euler product; fixed translates preserve this property. For every u, affine dilation f_i(x)->f_i(ux+r) preserves the hypotheses if all f_i(r) are k-free: primes dividing u have no bad residues, and primes coprime to u act bijectively modulo p^k. The density theorem then makes A_{F,r} divisible, hence averaging. If q^k divides any f_i(r), A_{F,r} misses qN and the q-cycle with polynomial t gives zero return average.
data.supplied_vs_acquired: Supplied: F, k, joint local condition, the cited density theorem, and the established rational-set recurrence theorem. Acquired: periodic approximation, dilation invariance of the local interface, exact iff proof.
data.costs: Qualitative only. The imported density theorem states an asymptotic but provides no numerical onset in this package; the rationality proof is Cesaro/Besicovitch and the recurrence theorem supplies no effective finite-pattern threshold.
data.baseline: The source theorem supplies density but not this recurrence criterion. The closest direct dynamics input is Theorem 1.4 for rational positive-density sets.
data.falsifier: A family meeting all hypotheses and all f_i(r) k-free at a fixed shift r whose translated set fails divisibility, or a family with one non-k-free f_i(r) that is nevertheless averaging, would falsify the iff. The proof reduces either failure to a directly checkable density or cyclic-system calculation.
data.unresolved: External validation of the 2026 density input, proof-priority review of this transfer corollary, and effective recurrence rates.

data.title: Same-local-admissibility positive-density quartic family can fail recurrence
data.theorem: For k=2 the family (x^4+18,x^4+5) is jointly locally admissible at every prime and has positive density of simultaneous squarefree values conditional on preprint 020, Corollary 1.3, yet its parameter set omits 3N and is not an averaging set of polynomial multiple recurrence.
data.assumptions: The density conclusion is conditional on the same imported power-free-value theorem. Eisenstein irreducibility and the modular obstruction are exact elementary facts.
data.proof_mechanism: The local conditions are checked symbolically by separating p=2,3,5 and using at most four simple roots per component for p>=7. If 3|n then 9|n^4+18. On the 3-cycle with the singleton set at zero and polynomial t, every parameter correlation is zero.
data.supplied_vs_acquired: Exact family and imported density theorem supplied; modular root analysis and the cyclic nonrecurrence witness acquired.
data.costs: A finite exact modular checker covers selected primes; the all-prime condition follows from the symbolic case split in RESULT.txt, not from the checker.
data.baseline: Positive density alone, and even positive density plus the joint local admissibility condition, do not imply polynomial recurrence.
data.falsifier: A residue calculation showing a prime p with all classes in Omega_p, or a q-cycle return at a parameter n not divisible by q, would falsify the record.
data.unresolved: The 2026 density input remains a preprint premise; no external validation or novelty claim is made.

data.title: Irrational polynomial phases are Cesaro-orthogonal to the shifted power-free set
data.theorem: Under GN2-01's density hypotheses, for any fixed good shift r and any fixed real polynomials Q_1,...,Q_m such that every nonzero integer combination has an irrational nonconstant coefficient, the normalized sum N^{-1} sum_{n<=N, n in A_{F,r}} exp(2 pi i sum_j h_j Q_j(n)) tends to zero for every nonzero h in Z^m.
data.assumptions: The power-free family is Besicovitch rational conditional on the pinned density Corollary 1.3. Weyl equidistribution for each fixed irrational polynomial phase is imported standard input.
data.proof_mechanism: Replace the indicator by a fixed periodic approximant. Split into residue classes modulo its period and apply Weyl to each affine-substituted phase; then let the Besicovitch approximation error tend to zero.
data.supplied_vs_acquired: Supplied: density theorem and Weyl criterion. Acquired: the periodic-weight transfer for this family of polynomial-value sets.
data.costs: Qualitative Cesaro convergence only; no uniformity in the phase coefficients, shrinking Bohr sets, or finite-prefix onset.
data.baseline: A direct consequence of Besicovitch rationality and Weyl equidistribution; the theorem is a scoped application, not a new equidistribution principle.
data.falsifier: A fixed phase vector meeting the Weyl irrationality condition with nonzero Cesaro correlation against a good-shift indicator would falsify the record.
data.unresolved: External verification of the 2026 density input and any effective uniform phase-distribution rate.

data.claim: A group admitting a faithful normalized-Hilbert-Schmidt ultraproduct model by monomial unitary matrices with phases in one fixed finite cyclic group is sofic.
data.quantifiers: Fix k>=1. For every finite F and tolerance eta>0, an injective HS-ultraproduct homomorphism into monomial U(D) matrices over mu_k admits a finite permutation (F,eta)-approximation on a lifted set of size kD followed by a finite m-fold product.
data.proof: Lift each monomial Ue_j=omega^{a(j)}e_{sigma(j)} to the permutation Pi_k(U)(j,s)=(sigma(j),s+a(j)) on [D]xZ/k. The lift is a homomorphism. Columnwise phase gap c_k=min{2,4sin^2(pi/k)} gives d_H(Pi(U),Pi(V))<=||U-V||_2^2/c_k and ||U-I||_2^2<=4d_H(Pi(U),id). For finite F, faithfulness gives a positive minimum HS separation gamma_F>0 among distinct elements in the ultraproduct; a coordinate stage separates each pair by at least gamma_F/2, hence the lifts by at least gamma_F^2/16. An m-fold product makes fixed-point fraction at most (1-gamma_F^2/16)^m. If relation HS errors are e, lifted Hamming defects are at most e^2/c_k and the product defects at most m e^2/c_k. Choose m and then e to meet eta. This yields a sofic approximation.

data.claim: Every group with a faithful normalized-Hilbert-Schmidt unitary metric-ultraproduct embedding admits another faithful such embedding whose induced trace on group elements is the canonical group trace.
data.quantifiers: For every group G hyperlinear and every original faithful HS metric-ultraproduct embedding, there exists a re-embedding with trace 1 at the identity and 0 on every nonidentity element.
data.proof: Add a trivial block so a nonidentity normalized trace t becomes (1+t)/2, which has modulus strictly below 1 because faithfulness forces t != 1. The conjugation representation U -> U tensor conjugate(U) is a homomorphism with normalized trace |tr(U)|^2. After k iterations, the trace is |(1+t)/2|^(2^k), tending to zero. The outer ultraproduct over k preserves exact group multiplication and yields pairwise orthogonal group unitaries. Linear extension to C[G] is injective because the canonical trace gives ||sum c_g g||_2^2=sum |c_g|^2.

data.claim: A group admitting an injective rank-metric ultraproduct representation over finite fields of one fixed characteristic p has stably finite group algebra over every coefficient field of characteristic p.
data.quantifiers: For every prime p, countable group G, ultrafilter omega, finite fields F_i with char(F_i)=p on an omega-large set, dimensions n_i tending to infinity along omega, and injective homomorphism G -> prod_omega GL_n_i(F_i)/d_omega; for every field K with char(K)=p, K[G] is stably finite.
data.proof: For each finite k0=F_{p^d}, extend coordinate fields to L_i containing both F_i and k0, then restrict scalars to k0. Normalized rank is preserved exactly. Apply Arzhantseva-Paunescu Theorem 7.4 to embed k0[G] in a rank ultraproduct and Proposition 2.8 for stable finiteness. A hypothetical matrix one-sided inverse over arbitrary K gives a finite polynomial system over F_p, augmented by Z times one nonzero group coefficient of BA-I equal to 1. A maximal ideal of its nonzero finite-type coordinate algebra has finite residue field by Zariski's lemma, contradicting stable finiteness over that finite extension k0.

The resulting finite-type coordinate algebra is nonzero because K supplies a solution. A maximal ideal has finite residue field over F_p by Zariski's lemma, and the residue classes give the same one-sided inverse witness.

data.claim: A fixed finite complex rank model reduces to a finite field of prescribed characteristic p while preserving a finite list of ranks whenever the product c of selected nonzero maximal minors is not nilpotent modulo pR.

data.proof: The condition c not in sqrt(pR) says (R/pR)[1/c] is nonzero. A maximal ideal of this finite-type F_p algebra yields a finite residue field; the rank minors selected remain nonzero while all larger minors vanish identically in R. Including inverse entries preserves invertibility after reduction.

data.claim: Each fixed finite complex rank-model stage over a characteristic-zero finite-type domain is p-safe for all but finitely many primes, but this stagewise fact does not guarantee one prime is safe eventually along a sequence.
data.proof: For a fixed stage, R[1/c] is a nonzero finite-type domain over Z. The image of Spec(R[1/c]) -> Spec(Z) is constructible and contains the generic point, hence contains all but finitely many prime points. The exact Z model theta_k(m)=diag(P_k^m,...,P_k^{km}) for P_k the product of the first k primes has coefficient ring Z[1/P_k]; each fixed prime is a unit at every sufficiently late stage, so no coordinate reduction to that fixed characteristic exists there.
data.quantifiers: The cofinite assertion is per fixed stage. The sequence counterexample is a selected model of Z, not a statement that Z lacks models in any characteristic.
data.falsifier: A fixed finite-type characteristic-zero domain with nonzero c whose fibers c!=0 are empty for infinitely many prime characteristics would contradict constructibility of the dominant image.
data.scope: Z is sofic and has another rank model over every F_p via prime-length permutation cycles; the counterexample is to model-specific specialization only.
