data.title: Posterior-regret trace-cap converse for blind quantum or hybrid archives
data.theorem: Let X have law mu, let a blind encoder map x to a state rho_x on a D-dimensional Hilbert space, and let a fixed query decoder use a POVM M(dy) with bounded regret 0<=R(x,y)<=L. For a measurable chart C of mass m and V(u)=sup_y mu({x in C:R(x,y)<=u}), E R(X,Y)>=integral_0^L [m-D V(u)]_+ du. For direct-sum hybrid memory D=sum_j d_j. Independent public seeds are allowed if every seed uses dimension at most D.
data.proof: rho_x<=I_D implies integral_{C_y}rho_x dmu<=V(u)I_D. Integrating against the POVM gives Pr[X in C,R<=u]<=D V(u); integrate the complementary tail in u.
data.costs: D counts all quantum blocks and all dephased classical labels; bits are log2(D). Decoder/runtime, precision and output costs are outside the inequality and must be reported separately.
data.baseline: A classical quantizer has the same trace-cap upper bound; equality requires a separate positive reference-preserving codec.
data.falsifier: A finite-dimensional blind code violating the displayed integrated bound under the stated POVM interface.
data.unresolved_gate: External proof and priority review; determine when a matching positive codec exists for a specified family.

data.title: Independent later queries pay a sum of scalar rate-distortion costs
data.theorem: For independent classical features X_1,...,X_d encoded before the query into one D-dimensional quantum/hybrid memory M, if query i may use its own POVM and guarantees distortion at most delta_i, then ln D >= sum_i R_i(delta_i), where R_i is the scalar Shannon rate-distortion function under that query's distortion.
data.proof: For each i, measurement data processing gives I(X_i;Y_i)<=I(X_i;M). Independence and strong subadditivity give sum_i I(X_i;M)<=I(X_1...X_d;M)<=ln D. Since R_i(delta_i)<=I(X_i;Y_i), sum the inequalities. No joint measurement of incompatible query outputs is assumed.
data.costs: All hybrid branch dimensions are charged through D. Query descriptions and measurements are external; charge their communication/runtime if the application requires it.
data.baseline: Classical product rate-distortion code with the same feature priors and distortions.
data.falsifier: A counterexample to conditional-entropy subadditivity/Holevo under this finite-dimensional interface or an archive beating the Shannon lower bound.
data.unresolved_gate: The source-derived N36/N66 specializations need external proof review; the theorem does not apply to dependent features or encoder-known queries.

data.title: Fisher information alone cannot determine one-shot archive cost
data.theorem: On theta in [pi/3,2pi/3], X~N(theta,1) and X~Bernoulli(sin^2(theta/2)) have identical Fisher information 1 for every theta. The Bernoulli observation is stored exactly with D=2; D=1 has worst-case TV error at least 1/4. Under the source-derived N07 Gaussian rate for affine dimension one, e_D=Theta(D^-2), so D_min(epsilon)=Theta(epsilon^-1/2).
data.proof: For Bernoulli, p'(theta)^2/(p(1-p))=1. The endpoints have Bernoulli TV distance 1/2, so one fixed output law has radius at least 1/4. Store the observed bit for exact reconstruction. The Gaussian conclusion is N07's affine-dimension-one theorem, not independently externally validated here.
supplied_inputs: known scalar family and parameter interval

data.title: Known-spectrum near-tracial qudit orbit has a partial-collision leading profile
data.theorem: Fix d and known sorted p_n in [1/(2d),3/(2d)]^d with p_n->I/d. Set B_n=product_{i<j}(1+n(p_{n,i}-p_{n,j})^2), H_n=log2(B_n), and delta_n=1-product_{i<j}(p_{n,j}/p_{n,i}). A total hybrid memory D=sum_j d_j that reconstructs the entire n-copy state with half-trace error <=1/8 has D>=c_d B_n. A candidate classical archive has D<=C_d eta^{-2(d^2-1)}B_n and error <=delta_n+eta. If H_n->infinity, vanishing-error leading cost is H_n+o(H_n). For prescribed epsilon_n, the upper is certified if epsilon_n>delta_n eventually and log2(1/(epsilon_n-delta_n))=o(H_n); this is sufficient, not known necessary.
data.proof: The independent lower uses only the one-sided closed-chamber orbital-integral bound, a maximal Frobenius net, fixed informationally complete tomography with O_d(1/n) risk, and the total-hybrid trace cap; it proves D>=c_{d,e}B_n for every fixed error e<1. The upper's Schur/coherent likelihood, weighted-flag chart and positive code are reconstructed from an earlier internal candidate package; those analytic steps have not been externally certified.
acquired_inputs: none; spectrum and model are supplied
data.costs: All hybrid branches count via D=sum_j d_j. The theorem is information-theoretic; gates, runtime, source acquisition, precision, decoder randomness and fresh n-qudit output are separate.

data.falsifier: A code below c_d B_n at error <=1/8, or a counterexample to the weighted-flag upper within the stated band.

data.title: Collision product is not a complete law at critical precision or uniformly in growing d
data.theorem: The all-accuracy extension D=Theta(B_n) for every vanishing-error sequence is false: for n=k^2 and qubit spectrum (1/2+3/(2k),1/2-3/(2k)), B_n=10 but every archive with bounded total hybrid dimension along a subsequence has error bounded away from zero. A dimension-uniform extension is also false: for d=n and p=(1-eta,eta/(d-1),...), eta=epsilon/(16n), a symmetric-subspace archive uses D=binom(n+d-1,n) with error <=epsilon/8, while log2 B_n=(n-1)log2(n)+O(1) and log2 D<=2n-1.
data.proof: The critical-qubit lower forms m=D0^2+1 distinct phase queries and a Vandermonde matrix of true expectations whose limiting matrix has full rank m; every decoded expectation matrix through D0-dimensional memory has rank at most D0^2. The growing-d upper projects onto Sym^n(C^d); the n-copy state is within trace distance <=n eta of the dominant pure orbit, which this subspace reconstructs exactly. The pure symmetric dimension is binom(n+d-1,n).

data.title: Pure rank boundary removes one counted cutoff factor
data.theorem: For N23's local qubit family at known lambda=0, fixed R, blind total-hybrid dimension D=sum_j d_j, and uniform half-trace reconstruction error epsilon, a Dicke cutoff gives D<=O_R(1+min(n,h_epsilon)), h_epsilon=ln(1/epsilon)/ln ln(1/epsilon), with no epsilon*n restriction. Hence a square lower bound uniform over lambda>=0 is false. The matching two-sided pure-face optimum is only SOURCE-REPORTED via N22.
data.proof: The Dicke excitation B is binomial with n p<=R^2. For m>=1, E[(B)_m]<=(R^2)^m and P(B>=m)<=(R^2)^m/m!. A good m-dimensional quantum branch plus one charged failure label has trace error <=sqrt(t)+t; when m>n, store the exact n+1-dimensional symmetric block.

When i is known before storage, a scalar positive-hat code costs (1/2)log2(r/epsilon)+O(1) bits. data.title: Fixed-reference QLAN covers unitary-orbit degeneracies but not moving collisions
data.theorem: Yamaguchi--Tajima arXiv:2609.11926v2, Part III, gives strong two-way trace-norm QLAN for the unitary orbit of one fixed finite-d density matrix, allowing repeated positive eigenvalues and rank deficiency. It treats horizontal rotations between distinct spectral blocks and has a remainder O(n^(-1/2+kappa)) in its stated local parameter range, with constants depending on the fixed reference spectrum/gaps.

It contains no unknown within-block splitting coordinates and no uniform triangular-gap estimate.
data.costs: This is an experiment-equivalence theorem, not by itself a finite-bit archive rate. QLAN map construction costs, spectrum acquisition, and finite-n decoder costs are not covered here.

data.title: Common-eigenbasis spectral perturbations have an explicit n-copy stability bound
data.theorem: For fixed d, parameter set Theta_n, common unitary U_{n,theta}, spectra p_{n,theta},q_{n,theta} with supp(p) subset supp(q), and Xi_n=sup_theta sum_{i:q_i>0}(p_i-q_i)^2/q_i, the n-copy trace distance is uniformly at most r_n=min{1,sqrt(n Xi_n/2)}. For the same later-query archive interface, |e_D(E_n^p)-e_D(E_n^q)|<=2r_n. A transfer of the N08 bridge requires eta_n+2r_n=o(epsilon_n).
data.proof: Quantum relative entropy is invariant under the common U and additive on tensor powers: D(rho_p^tensor n||rho_q^tensor n)=nD(p||q). The classical inequality D(p||q)<=chi^2(p||q), followed by quantum Pinsker, gives the state bound. Contractivity moves both the decoded output and target output, giving 2r_n for the archive risk curve.
supplied_inputs: same known or unknown unitary parameter U in both models
p support contained in q support

data.title: A shrinking unknown rare-rank interval inherits the pure-face memory order

A pure-face archive at tolerance epsilon_n/2 gives D=O_R(1+min(n,h_{epsilon_n/2})); the lambda=0 subfamily gives the matching order lower through N22, whose detailed lower proof is source-reported rather than independently replayed. Its overlap with the tensor-power state is (1-lambda/n)^n, so the pure-target half-trace distance is exactly 1-(1-lambda/n)^n<=lambda<=Lambda_n. Compose with the pure-face archive and use the triangle inequality. Restricting to lambda=0 imports N22 lower.

data.title: Critical iid-qubit orbits have a sharp-order EB reconstruction floor
data.theorem: Fix 0<c0<=c1<infinity. For known 0<r<=1/2 with c0<=r*sqrt(n)<=c1 and unknown v in S^2, require full n-qubit density reconstruction in worst-case half trace distance. Every entanglement-breaking channel, including arbitrary outcome spaces and arbitrary input/output Schur-sector transitions, has error e>=c(c0,c1)r. A coherent measure-and-prepare channel has e<=2r and can be made finite with all labels charged. Hence the optimum EB error is Theta_(c0,c1)(r)=Theta_(c0,c1)(n^(-1/2)).
data.proof: The exact Schur reduction gives known sector probabilities P_L and thermal spin states tau_(L,v). For spin j=L/2, the covariant first-harmonic identity bounds the norm of every measurement posterior direction by a_L=Tr(tau_(L,z)J_z)/(j+1). A bounded quadratic score F_K(v)=a_K(v.J_K/j_K)-a_K^2 I/2 has global interval [-3/2,1/2] using a_K<=1. For any input posterior sector L and prepared output sector K, completing the square gives decoded score <=a_L^2/2, whereas the target score is a_L^2/2+a_L^2/j_L. Haar averaging and half-trace duality yield e>=sum_L P_L a_L^2/L. A uniform positive critical mass window 2/r<=L<=B/r has a_L>=1/3, giving e>=c r. The coherent EB channel gives e<=2r.
supplied_inputs: unknown full SU(2) orbit direction v
full-state reconstruction and worst-case half-trace metric
data.costs: The converse covers all classical outcome spaces and therefore all EB alphabets. A finite coherent implementation has a finite label count. The theorem concerns EB error, not optimal total hybrid dimension or minimum quantum branch size. Decoder runtime, precision, gates, and fresh output preparation remain separate.
data.baseline: The same full-orbit family with known r; coherent EB reconstruction is the matching order upper baseline.
data.falsifier: An EB reconstruction channel within the stated interface with worst-case half-trace error o(r) along a critical sequence, or a failure of the posterior-score inequality under an allowed sector-changing output.

data.title: Critical qubit full-state error trades inversely with maximum quantum branch dimension
data.theorem: For known 0<r<=1/2 with c0<=r*sqrt(n)<=c1 and unknown v in S^2, let e_Q be the minimax worst-case half-trace error for full reconstruction of rho_(r,v)^tensor n by a dephased hybrid memory whose every quantum branch has dimension at most Q; classical outcomes are unrestricted in the converse. There are constants c,C>0 depending only on c0,c1 such that c*r/Q<=e_Q<=C*r/Q for integers 1<=Q<=1/(32r), for sufficiently small r. The same radius-independent encoder gives worst-case error O(c1/(sqrt(n)Q)) on the unknown-radius ball ||b||<=c1/sqrt(n), and restriction to a fixed critical sphere gives a matching lower for Q up to a constant times sqrt(n).
data.proof: Exact Schur reduction gives direct_sum_j P_j tau_(j,v). Every decoded branch factors through dimension Q, so its Kraus operators and Choi vectors have rank/Schmidt number at most Q. A covariant spin-score argument plus a Schmidt-rank projector/energy bound yields e>=c*r/Q, including arbitrary output-sector transitions. For the upper, on spin j use F=diag((1-k/Q)_+) in occupation k=j-m, s=Tr F^2=(Q+1)(2Q+1)/(6Q), and Phi_j(X)=(2j+1)/s integral (U F U*)X(U F U*) dU. Its commutator energy is E=Q^-2 sum_(k=1)^Q k(2j-k+1), so E/s<=6j/Q and 1-lambda_1=E/[2s*j*(j+1)]. The full trace-norm thermal-series double-commutator estimate gives T(Phi_j(tau_(j,v)),tau_(j,v))<=3/(2Q)*(beta+beta^2*j/3)*exp(beta*j), beta=2 atanh(r). Exact Schur-weight bounds and unbiased-binomial moments average this to O(c1*r/Q). Finite Euler/Gauss quadrature realizes the Haar channel with O(n^3) total classical outcomes.
supplied_inputs: n and known radius r, or public radius envelope c1/sqrt(n)
whole-state density reconstruction in worst-case half trace
maximum branch dimension Q; every retained input-dependent register is charged
data.costs: The lower allows arbitrarily many classical labels but limits each quantum branch to Q. The explicit upper has O(n^3) finite classical outcomes, at most Q quantum dimension per outcome, and total direct-sum dimension D<=O(Q*n^3). This does not optimize D. Exact algebraic quadrature, gates, runtime, Schur implementation, finite control precision and fresh output preparation are separate.
data.baseline: At Q=1 this recovers the EB Theta(r) floor. The exact Schur-cutoff code has a smaller total-D upper at a specified epsilon but does not give a branch-dimension optimum.
data.falsifier: A fixed-Q full-state code with e=o(r), an allowed rank-Q channel violating the Choi score converse, a sign/factor error in the spin flip, or a failure of the full trace-norm thermal-series bound.
data.proof_location: outputs/research/sol_collision_precision/quantum_branch.txt, sections 1-11; independent audit outputs/research/memory_information/quantum_branch_upper_audit.txt; exact taper fixtures outputs/research/memory_information/evidence/quantum_branch_upper_audit/check_taper.py

data.claim: Mode-selective additive-noise stability of the N81 postselection obstruction
data.theorem: For the N81 rational centered pure-Gaussian family with m=Theta(R), uniform pure loss eta=1/R, h=O(R), and post-loss herald lower bound p>=w>=2^(-s), s=O(R^2 log R), apply rational Gaussian displacement noise after the known passive network and before loss: nu_H=2^(-[2s+ceil(log2(20000m))]) on herald modes and nu_S=R^(-a), a fixed positive constant, on all unheralded detector modes including retained outputs. The resulting input is full rank; its conditional output law is o(1)-close to the ideal N81 law for each fixed a>0.
data.proof: The H-noise global trace bound is delta_H<=sqrt(2m nu_H)<=w/100. With p>=w, conditioning gives TV<=delta_H/(p-delta_H)<=1/99. The S-noise channel is local to the unmeasured output subsystem, preserves the herald mass, commutes through uniform loss with variance scaled by eta, and satisfies T(rho,A_tau(rho))<=sqrt(tau(2E+m_S)). Since eta=1/R, conditional post-loss energy E<=eta(h+0.01), and m_S=O(R), S-noise contributes at most sqrt(nu_S O(1)).
data.cost: nu_H requires O(R^2 log R) denominator bits; nu_S=R^(-a) has O(log R) bits. Added numerical energy is O(m nu_S)<=O(R). Numerical m,h,1/eta, energy, input bits, epsilon^-1, and s=log2(1/w) are polynomial in R. The bound charges no inverse physical success probability.
data.baseline: Generic all-state trace-distance continuity certifies a fixed conditional error only for globally isotropic nu<=gamma^2 w^2/[2m(1+gamma)^2], exponentially small in R^2 log R. The mode-selective construction improves robustness only on the unheralded subsystem.
data.falsifier: An error in the N81 post-loss mass bound, the Weyl displacement-channel inequality, or the output-partition locality would invalidate the extension. If noise is applied before a mixing network without pulling back the covariance correctly, the herald can change.
sources: Optical postselection prior: Knill-Laflamme-Milburn, Nature 409 (2001), https://doi.org/10.1038/35051009
data.open_gate: Independent replay of the N81 rational optical compiler, source rounding, false-herald filter, and post-loss probability bound. Uniform inverse-polynomial noise on all modes erases this compiled conditional statistic by PC-03/PC-14, so the class-collapse implication applies only to the stated mode-selective family.
data.scope: Mathematical bounds are internally derived. The family-specific class implication is separately recorded as conditional in PC-02. No PP != BPP separation or runtime lower bound follows.

data.claim: A polynomial-bit sampler for the mode-selectively perturbed family would imply PP=BPP
data.theorem: Assuming the N81/N82 source/compiler candidate and its encoded-bit conditional gap, any uniform classical sampler with constant conditional-TV error for the full-rank mixed family in PC-01 and runtime polynomial in finite description length, numerical m,h,E,1/eta, epsilon^-1, and log(1/w) yields PP subseteq BPP, hence PP=BPP. The corresponding quantum sampling implication is PP=BQP.
data.proof: The H perturbation costs at most 1/99 conditionally; for fixed a>0, S perturbation tends to zero; a 0.01 sampler error and inherited compiler/filter error below 0.02 leave the N81 constant decision gap positive. A constant number of conditional samples and majority amplification decides each PP language.
data.cost: The numeric herald count and inverse loss are O(R); log inverse herald lower bound is s=O(R^2 log R); all rational perturbation descriptions have polynomial bit length. There is no physical rejection step.
data.baseline: Physical unconditional rejection costs expected 1/p and is not the abstract conditional sampling interface. The implication only excludes runtimes polynomial in log(1/p), not runtimes polynomial in 1/p.
data.falsifier: Independent replay that disproves the N81 optical compilation, post-loss lower bound, or final conditional gap blocks this consequence. The claim does not assert a separation.
sources: N81-N83 source/status cards and proof page work/astra_prior/web/pages/d-f3b89d44c7a3e836.html

data.scope: Conditional consequence; source-reported inherited reduction, not external validation.

data.claim: Uniform inverse-polynomial all-mode noise erases the N81 compiled conditional statistic
data.theorem: For the N81 centered pure-Gaussian family with rational detector-plane B, ||B||<=g=2^(-ell), ell>=R, d=Theta(R), binary herald h,h0=O(R), uniform loss eta=1/R, and any fixed integer a>=1, add isotropic displacement noise nu=R^(-a) to all detector modes before loss. The complete retained two-mode count law conditioned on the herald is TV-o(1) from vacuum, erasing the encoded constant-TV amplification; subleading probabilities may still encode information. The actual herald mass is p_ref(1+o(1)), p_ref=t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0), t=eta nu, with log(1/p_ref)=O(R log R).
data.evidence: After all-mode additive noise the state has a positive Gaussian P representation because nu>g/(1-g). Its post-loss latent quadrature covariance is t(I+E), ||E||<=delta=g/((1-g)nu). Under the B=0 reference posterior conditioned on the binary herald, the standardized squared radius S has an explicit gamma moment-generating function. The Gaussian prior likelihood ratio r obeys |log r|<=C delta(2d+S), giving conditional latent chi-square <=exp(Cd delta)-1 and output TV O(sqrt(d delta)) by data processing. Since d delta=O(R^(a+1)2^(-R))->0, and the reference retained thermal modes have mean t->0, the retained law tends to vacuum. Full derivation: outputs/research/photonic_complexity/all_mode_noise_n81_proof.txt.
data.cost: d,h,h0,1/eta=O(R); nu=R^(-a) has O(log R) bits for fixed integer a; added input energy is d nu=O(R^(1-a)); the herald log inverse is O(R log R). The conditional comparison has no 1/p_ref loss.
data.baseline: The direct pure-source trace distance is at most g*sqrt(d/[2(1-g^2)]), and dividing it by p_ref is not sufficient when h is linear in R. The posterior positive-P comparison avoids this failure. This erases the N81 constant-TV encoded amplification on the supplied family; subleading probabilities may still encode information. It is not a sampler for arbitrary noisy Gaussian inputs.
data.falsifier: A covariance-convention error, failure of the positive-P threshold, incorrect herald-conditioned gamma law, or a failure of the likelihood-ratio chi-square bound would invalidate the candidate. Noise must be isotropic in the detector-mode basis before uniform loss.
data.open_gate: Independent review of the posterior covariance proof and replay of the inherited N81/N82 optical compiler; do not infer hardness/easiness for other noisy instances.
data.scope: Family-specific conditional-law erasure, not PP != BPP, a general noisy sampler, or a no-noise hardness refutation.

data.theorem: For a supplied finite-bit physical Gaussian density kernel with real entrywise nonnegative K and ell in a supplied number-preserving phase gauge and the required physical structure, the N42 source claims a sampler for the complete remaining photon-count vector conditioned on an exact herald. The claimed running time is polynomial in input bits, mode count, numerical herald count h, numerical mean energy E, and epsilon^-1, with no 1/p_H factor.

data.claim: Integer-weighted edge to simple-unweighted perfect-matching gadget
data.theorem: For every positive integer W with k=ceil(log2(W+1)), a simple bipartite graph with O(k) vertices and O(k^2) edges has a two-port matching signature (1,W,0,0): one completion when neither port is used, W when both are used, and zero when exactly one is used.
data.proof: Build a DAG with vertices s,x_0,...,x_(k-1),t; add x_i->t and x_i->x_j for j<i; add s->x_i iff bit i of W is one. The number of x_i-to-t paths obeys P_i=1+sum_(j<i)P_j=2^i, so the s-to-t path count is W. Split each DAG vertex into L_v,R_v; add L_v-R_v and L_u-R_v for each arc u->v. The full graph has the unique all-loop perfect matching. Deleting ports L_t,R_s yields one completion per s-to-t path. Parity makes exactly-one-port use impossible.
data.cost: O(log W) vertices and O(log^2 W) simple edges. If weights are rational, clearing denominators charges their bit lengths.
data.baseline: A vague appeal to standard weighted matching gadgets would leave the weighted-to-unweighted reduction as a gap. This construction makes the elementary gadget explicit; it does not establish the OA113 FPRAS.
data.falsifier: A path-count error, unintended directed cycle, or port-signature mismatch disproves the gadget. Exact enumeration was performed for W=1,...,20 and matched the claimed signature.
sources: OA113 theorem page work/astra_prior/web/pages/d-f92e4f610d78fe0a.html for the separate unweighted counting service

data.scope: Proof is internally reconstructed; finite enumeration is a sanity check only.

data.claim: Exact coefficient-positivity criterion for centered gauge-invariant Gaussian states
data.theorem: For N>=0, Q=N(I+N)^(-1), and Bargmann density kernel det(I-Q) exp(z^T Q bar(w)), all coefficients in a fixed detector phase frame are real nonnegative iff every Q_ij is real nonnegative. Under local phase gauges, such a gauge exists iff all cycle phase products on the nonzero-entry graph equal one.
data.proof: Expand the exponential for sufficiency. The coefficient of z_i bar(w_j), divided by the constant coefficient, equals Q_ij, proving necessity. The cycle-product condition is the standard vertex rephasing consistency condition.
data.cost: Exact rational covariance inversion and phase-certificate acquisition are charged by the input representation; this is a representation test, not a sampler runtime theorem.
data.baseline: Positive covariance and positive P representation alone do not imply coefficient positivity. The thermal path matrix N=[[2,1,0],[1,2,1],[0,1,2]] has Q_13<0 after any eta>0 and a negative gauge-invariant triangle product, although unconditional counts have an easy Gaussian-Poisson sampler.
data.falsifier: A coefficient expansion with a negative coefficient despite all Q entries nonnegative, or a balanced-cycle graph with no nonnegative rephasing, would contradict the algebraic proof.
data.open_gate: Whether other positive representations efficiently sample frustrated-cycle or general mixed/displaced rare heralds remains UNKNOWN.
data.scope: Exact criterion within the centered gauge-invariant subclass, not a complexity boundary.

data.claim: A full variable-cardinality doubled-graph sampler does not automatically yield a fixed herald-sector sampler
data.theorem: For G consisting of m disjoint edges and c=1/2 in the graph-GBS law proportional to c^(2|S|) PM_G(S)^2, the feasible sector |S|=2 has exact mass (m/16)(16/17)^m. Thus rejection from the full law is exponential even though the sector is easy to sample directly.
data.proof: Feasible sets are unions of j edges, each with matching count one and weight 16^-j. The partition function is (17/16)^m, and the j=1 mass is the stated expression. In G square K2 the sector fixes a vertical-edge count; the full-law sampler controls perfectness, not this color count.
data.cost: Expected rejection count is (16/m)(17/16)^m. Direct conditional sampling is O(log m) random bits up to representation costs.
data.baseline: Anand et al. (2025/2026) give a polynomial-TV sampler for the complete variable-cardinality law; this exact example blocks a general inference by postselection/rejection.
data.falsifier: Direct binomial expansion or the exact doubled-graph identity would expose an arithmetic mistake. The calculation is exact.
data.open_gate: Direct colored-sector relative counting/sampling or certified coefficient extraction with polynomial conditioning.
data.scope: Counterexample to a generic reduction strategy only; no hardness claim.

data.claim: Conditional-TV amplification and sample-only rare-event lower bound
data.theorem: If two full flagged laws have TV delta and herald masses p,p'>0, their conditional laws obey TV<=3delta/[2 min(p,p')]; when p=p', TV<=delta/p. In the sample-only Bernoulli-herald black-box model, T unconditional samples that must identify an unknown postselected bit to error epsilon<1/2 satisfy T>=log(1/(2epsilon))/[-log(1-p)]=Omega(p^-1 log(1/epsilon)) for p<=1/2.
data.proof: Restrict the full-law L1 difference to the herald event, then account for normalization by the difference |p-p'|. For the lower bound couple the two black boxes on shared flags and coins; transcripts can differ only if at least one of T trials heralds.
data.cost: Physical rejection has mean 1/p and capped failure (1-p)^T. These lower bounds apply to black-box unconditional samples, not structured optical descriptions.
data.baseline: An N42-style relative branch-count algorithm can exploit a supplied optical description and avoid 1/p; N81's class implication only rules out polynomial log(1/p) dependence under its conditions.
data.falsifier: A pair of conditional distributions with equal herald masses violating delta/p, or a sample-only decision algorithm violating the coupling bound, would falsify the proof.
data.open_gate: None for the stated information-theoretic interface; structured-description complexity is a separate question.
data.scope: Proved for black-box samples; not a lower bound against all classical algorithms.

data.claim: Equal energy and herald probability do not determine the conditional optical law
data.theorem: A two-mode squeezed source and a product thermal source can be parameterized to have equal input energy and exactly equal herald probability under the same uniform loss, while conditioning on a herald count h=s^2 yields conditional outputs converging respectively to Poisson(1) and vacuum, with TV tending to 1-exp(-1). The common success probability is approximately s^(-6s^2).
data.proof: The leaf derives the exact geometric/thermal herald law and takes the s->infinity limit. The state pair has rational parameters of O(log s) bits while the numeric herald count is s^2.
data.cost: Physical rejection is superpolynomial; description-based samplers remain easy for both examples. Numeric herald count must be charged, so binary bit length alone hides a large output parameter.
data.baseline: Energy-only or success-probability-only covariance resets cannot control the conditioned output law.
data.falsifier: Exact normalization and the limiting probability laws are checkable from the two generating functions.
sources: Jerrum-Sinclair-Vigoda FPRAS source cited in the leaf
data.open_gate: No hardness claim; use as an adversarial control in any resource or conditioning theorem.
data.scope: Exact family-specific counterexample, not a sampler lower bound.

data.claim: Phase-twirled bipartite herald law admits a scoped positive latent sampler
data.theorem: Under the leaf's weighted phase-orthogonality and phase-independent-normalization assumptions for a bipartite centered pure Gaussian herald, the phase-twirled complete conditional count law, including collisions, can be sampled from a log-concave simplex latent law without inverse-herald rejection.
data.proof: Phase averaging removes cross monomials by weighted orthogonality; the surviving nonnegative sector weights define the simplex latent measure, whose normalized count draws generate the twirled conditional law.
data.cost: Exact theorem is algebraic; finite-bit sampling of the latent distribution and rational implementation costs remain unresolved. An l1-envelope rejection proposal has cost (5/4)^k on the leaf's k-copy fixture.
data.baseline: The leaf's result covers a phase-twirled ensemble, not a supplied fixed-phase instance. N81 blocks a uniform arbitrary-phase conditional sampler under its inherited collapse assumptions.
data.falsifier: A surviving cross-term under the stated orthogonality condition, or phase-dependent herald normalization, invalidates the factorization.
data.open_gate: Finite-bit sampler with certified TV and cost; general fixed-phase extension.
data.scope: Scoped ensemble theorem candidate; not externally reviewed.

data.claim: Spectrum-sensitive rank compression for unconditional lossy sampling
data.theorem: For passive channel singular values sigma_i and discarded-mode energy W_k=sum_(i>k) sigma_i^2 <n_(v_i)>, the leaf derives TV(P_T,P_Tk)<=sqrt(1-(1-W_k)_+^2), and composes it with N71 to control retained sixth-power spectral mass.
data.proof: The note bounds the discarded-mode vacuum overlap and converts it to trace/TV distance, then applies the inherited N71 reset sampler to the retained subspace.
data.cost: Nine one-mode loss fixtures and vacuum/thermal generating-function checks passed. Combined finite-bit sampler is unverified because the N73 high-precision engine was not executed.
data.baseline: N71/N73 unconditional reset sampling is the relevant comparator; neither is a specified rare-herald conditional sampler.
data.falsifier: A state/channel pair violating the discarded-mode vacuum-overlap inequality or any exact fixture mismatch.
data.open_gate: Independent proof review, finite-bit sampler execution, and extension to noncommuting channels.
data.scope: Candidate unconditional compression result; finite evidence only for fixtures.

data.claim: Universal all-mode inverse-polynomial-noise stability of rare-herald conditional laws is false
data.theorem: For R=4^k, lambda=2^(-R^2), fixed integer a>=1, nu=R^(-a), eta=1/R, a two-mode squeezed-vacuum source with rational Walsh-Hadamard fanout of the idler into R herald modes has ideal conditional signal law tending in TV to Poisson(1), while after uniform additive Gaussian noise on all R+1 modes before loss the conditional signal law tends in TV to vacuum. The conditional-law TV gap tends to 1-exp(-1).
data.proof: The ideal source pair number N is geometric. N<R cannot herald; the N=R branch has herald probability q_R=eta^R R!/R^R=R!/R^(2R). The conditional mass above R is at most lambda^2/[(1-lambda^2)q_R], which tends to zero, so the retained signal is Bin(R,1/R)+o_TV(1), hence Poisson(1). The TMSV pure-state trace distance from global vacuum is exactly lambda. Channel contractivity makes the full noisy output law lambda-close to the vacuum-plus-noise reference, which is product thermal with per-mode mean t=eta nu. Its all-one herald probability is p0=[t/(1+t)^2]^R. Since lambda/p0 tends to zero, the noisy conditional signal is o_TV(1) from the independent thermal law of mean t, which tends to vacuum.
data.cost: Rational input covariance has O(R^2) squeezing bits; fixed-a noise and loss have O(log R) bits; Walsh-Hadamard has R^2 rational dyadic entries and O(R^2 log R) bits. m=R+1, numeric h=R, 1/eta=R, input energy is O(R nu+lambda^2)<=O(R), noisy log inverse herald probability is Theta(R log R), and ideal log inverse herald probability is Theta(R^3). Retained conditional means tend respectively to 1 and 0.
data.baseline: A universal claim that inverse-polynomial noise preserves every rare-herald conditional law is false. This does not decide N81-specific noisy sampling complexity; both distributions in this witness are easy to sample.
data.falsifier: An error in the TMSV-vacuum trace distance, exact thermal reference herald mass, conditional-TV normalization, uniform fanout probability, or ideal tail bound invalidates the construction.
sources: Self-contained derivation in RESULT.txt, section 1, all-mode noise counterfamily
Gaussian optical event framework: Hamilton et al. (2016/2017), https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.01199
data.open_gate: Independent audit of the proof and exact rational optical interface; no hardness or sampler-complexity implication follows.
data.scope: Universal conditional-law stability is refuted at an internally derived candidate level. Does not automatically refute or prove robustness for N81 instances.

data.claim: Uniform inverse-polynomial noise creates an N81 herald-vacuum branch larger than its entire ideal herald
data.theorem: For N81's detector-plane uniform additive noise nu=R^(-a), eta=1/R, and herald with h ones and h0 zero targets, the input herald-vacuum block contributes at least p_floor=(1/2)t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0), t=eta nu. The ideal pure herald mass obeys p_id<=(2g)^h(4/3)^(d/2). With N82's g=2^(-ell), ell>=(q+10)/2, q>=R ceil(log2R), and d,h,h0=O(R), p_floor/p_id diverges for every fixed a>0.
data.proof: The N81 mean energy E<=2dg^2 implies source probability of vacuum on all herald modes at least 1-E>=1/2. Phase-covariant additive noise, vacuum loss, and PNR detection give the exact-pattern probability t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0) from this block. For the ideal pure source, G(x)=E[x^(N_total)]=sqrt(det(I-BB*)/det(I-x^2 BB*)); set x=1/(2g) so beta_j<=g implies G(x)<=(4/3)^(d/2). The event detects h photons and requires N_total>=h, hence p_id<=x^(-h)G(x). The exponent h log2(t/(2g)) dominates the O(R) determinant cost and the o(1) monitor penalty.
data.cost: Detector mode count d=O(R), numerical herald h=O(R), 1/eta=R, noise rational bits O(log R), and the existing N81 lower-bound bit size is O(R^2 log R).
data.baseline: This branch alone does not bound the full noisy conditional law; the conditioned positive-P posterior comparison is the stronger result in PC-03/PC-14.
data.falsifier: A failure of the vacuum-block herald probability, N81 energy/vacuum-mass bound, total-number generating function, or tail-Markov inequality invalidates the comparison.
data.open_gate: Independent audit of the branch estimate and PC-14 posterior comparison. Nonvacuum source branches are controlled by the full likelihood-ratio argument, not this floor alone.
data.scope: Shows a noise-generated herald branch larger than the entire ideal herald. The full N81 noisy conditional law is separately shown TV-o(1) from vacuum in PC-03/PC-14; no general hardness or sampler conclusion follows.

data.claim: Binary-herald posterior stability for weak centered Gaussians under dominant isotropic noise
data.theorem: Let a centered pure Gaussian on d modes have rational B with ||B||<=g<1/4. Add isotropic displacement noise nu>g/(1-g) to all modes and pure loss eta>0. For any binary PNR herald on H (h one-targets, h0 zero-targets, h<=|H|<=d), put t=eta nu and delta=g/[(1-g)nu]. If delta<=1/4 and d delta<=c, the complete unheralded count law conditioned on the herald is within O(sqrt(d delta)) TV of the same heralded law for the noise-only B=0 reference. The actual herald probability is p_ref exp(O(d delta)), p_ref=t^h/(1+t)^(2h+h0).
data.proof: The pure-state quadrature covariance obeys ||V_B-I/2||<=g/(1-g), so noise yields positive P covariance nu I+(V_B-I/2); after loss this is t(I+E), ||E||<=delta. Standardize reference latent quadratures to y~N(0,I). The reference posterior has independent radii with exact mgf E exp(theta||y||^2)=(1-2theta)^(-(d-|H|))(1-2theta/(1+t))^-(|H|+h). The Gaussian prior RN derivative r satisfies |log r(y)|<=C delta(2d+||y||^2), whence Z=E[r]=exp(O(d delta)), E[r^2]<=exp(O(d delta)), conditional chi-square<=exp(O(d delta))-1, and TV<=O(sqrt(d delta)). Photon counts are a common Poisson-mixture channel, so data processing preserves the bound.
data.cost: The bound depends on numerical dimension d and binary target count h through O(d delta); no inverse herald probability appears. For N81, d=O(R), g<=2^-R, nu=R^-a for fixed integer a>=1, so d delta=O(R^(a+1)2^-R).
data.baseline: Generic full-state trace continuity followed by conditioning incurs 1/p_ref and may fail. Posterior comparison works because each herald count is at most one, so the conditioned reference latent norm remains O(d).
data.falsifier: Check the exact coherent-quadrature convention, P covariance under additive noise and loss, gamma posterior law, and the likelihood-ratio second moment. The result as stated uses isotropic noise, a centered input, and binary herald targets.
data.open_gate: Independent proof review; extension to nonbinary herald counts, displacements, or nonisotropic noise requires a separate posterior-moment bound.
data.scope: Mathematical conditional-law candidate for weak centered Gaussian sources; not an efficient sampler theorem or complexity lower bound.

data.claim: Near-isotropic centered positive-P Gaussian optics admits a finite-bit approximate exact conditional PNR sampler without inverse-herald cost
data.theorem: Given rational t>0 and centered post-loss quadrature P covariance C=tA on d modes, a rational PSD certificate (1-eps_bar)I<=A<=(1+eps_bar)I with 0<=eps_bar<=1/4, and a PNR pattern k_j on s herald modes, the exact-real sampler based on N(0,ctI) conditioned on the same herald and rejection exp(-y^T[A^-1-c^-1I]y/2), c=1+eps_bar, samples the target conditional count law exactly. Its expected proposal trials are <=exp(C(d+kappa)eps_bar), independent of 1/p_H, where kappa=sum k_j is charged numerically. A dyadic finite-bit implementation has output-law TV <=eps_out+xi and worst-case time polynomial in rational input length L, d, numeric kappa, M_out=tT/2, eps_out^-1, log(xi^-1), and Lambda>=exp(C(d+kappa)eps_bar). A polynomial-in-L corollary additionally requires numeric kappa, M_out, eps_out^-1, and log(xi^-1) to be polynomially bounded in L; no such claim is made when the rational scale t makes M_out exponentially large in its bit length.
data.proof: The isotropic proposal posterior factorizes into independent uniform phases and Gamma radii: shape k_j+1, scale 2ct/(1+ct) on herald modes and shape 1, scale 2ct otherwise. In y=x/sqrt(t), f_A/f_c=M exp(-y^TDy/2), M=c^d/sqrt(det A), D=A^-1-c^-1I>=0. The determinant envelope cancels in conditional normalization; accepting with exp(-y^TDy/2) gives exactly the target P posterior. Under the proposal E||Y||^2<=2c(d+kappa), ||D||<=2eps_bar/(1-eps_bar^2), and Jensen implies alpha>=exp(-C(d+kappa)eps_bar). For finite bits, truncate the Gamma sum at T=4c[K log 2+log(8/rho)], K=d+kappa, couple dyadic uniforms/phases to Euclidean error O(rho/[1+sqrt(eps_bar)+sqrt(t)]), approximate acceptance and rational-rate Poisson kernels to O(rho), with rho=eps_out/(C Lambda); normalization costs at most Lambda and an O(Lambda log(1/xi)) attempt cap bounds timeout. Exact rational LDL/fraction-free arithmetic validates the certificate and computes D.
data.cost: Certificate validation, rational inverse, quadratic forms, interval arithmetic, and Poisson truncation are polynomial in d and exact matrix/noise/loss bit length L. Total numerical PNR count kappa is separately charged: the stated Gamma construction uses O(d+kappa) exponential variates and is not asserted polynomial in the binary length of an arbitrarily large herald number. The explicit output Poisson cutoff is Q=O(M_out+log(1/rho)), M_out=tT/2. No log(1/p_H) enters the algorithm. Physically generating and discarding failed optical trials still costs expected 1/p_H. Three rational diagonal two-mode fixtures exactly match the integrated acceptance and p_H/(M q_H) formulas; a 60-digit numerical check confirms Jensen on those fixtures only. A polynomial-in-L corollary also requires numeric kappa and M_out=tT/2, together with eps_out^-1 and log(xi^-1), polynomially bounded in L; rational t can make M_out exponential in its bit length. N81 satisfies these extra bounds.
data.baseline: Quesada–Arrazola arXiv:1908.08068 explicitly samples sequentially from Gaussian marginal probabilities by conditional ratios; by inference, a fixed-herald-prefix adaptation samples the remaining law without an inherent 1/p_H rejection factor, but costs O(m N^3 2^N) after N detected photons. Quesada et al. arXiv:1905.07011 compute heralded-state matrix elements and success probabilities via loop hafnians, with exponential mode/occupation costs. Positive-quasiprobability output samplers and Oh et al. arXiv:2306.03709 target full output distributions; the latter notes postselected state preparation only as a possible application. The exact-real proposal overhead is polynomial when (d+kappa)eps_bar=O(log L). A polynomial-bit runtime in L also requires numeric kappa, M_out, and the requested accuracy budgets to be polynomially bounded. This is not a claim that no direct conditional algorithm exists.
data.falsifier: An incorrect Gamma posterior or density ratio, failure of D>=0 under the certified interval, an acceptance probability below the Jensen bound, or a finite-bit coupling/count-kernel error exceeding the stated budget falsifies the result.
data.open_gate: Independent proof review of finite-bit coupling after conditional normalization; independent check of the inferred fixed-herald-prefix adaptation of the Quesada–Arrazola sequential sampler has the stated exp-in-photons cost and no hidden 1/p_H loss; and a primary-literature priority search. Extend beyond centered near-isotropic P covariances only with a separately proved posterior-moment and domination bound.
data.scope: Applies to centered rational positive-P Gaussian states with a supplied near-isotropy covariance certificate. The N81 specialization has eps_bar=g/((1-g)nu), d,kappa=O(R), nu=R^-a, g<=2^-R, so expected trials are 1+o(1); it samples the all-mode-noisy conditional law, which is vacuum-like and has lost the constant-TV amplification; subleading probabilities may still encode information. No general mixed/displaced boundary, hardness conclusion, or physical herald rate improvement follows.

data.claim: Gaussian exponential tilting and positive-count marginalization yield a conditional sampler with rejection cost controlled by total herald photons times tilted-marginal anisotropy
data.theorem: Let C be a rational strictly positive definite centered coherent-quadrature P covariance; let H be a PNR herald, H_+ its m positive-count modes, kappa the numerical total target count, and U the remaining modes. Put C°=(C^{-1}+P_H)^{-1}, S=C°_{H_+,H_+}, K=C°_{U,H_+}S^{-1}, V=C°_{U,U}-KSK^T. If (1-eps)bI<=S<=(1+eps)bI for rational b>0 and 0<=eps<=1/4, the exact conditional output-count law is sampled by q(x)=phi_{(1+eps)bI}(x)W(x)/( (1+eps)b)^kappa, acceptance exp[-x^T(S^{-1}-((1+eps)b)^{-1}I)x/2], then X_U|X_+=x~N(Kx,V) and independent Poisson counts of rates ||X_u||^2/2. Its expected proposal count is at most exp(2(1+eps)eps(m+kappa)/(1-eps^2))<=exp(6 kappa eps), independent of unheralded dimension, zero-target herald count, and 1/p_H. For kappa=0 the Gaussian tilt alone is exact.
data.proof: The herald likelihood factors as exp(-X^T P_H X/2)W(X_+). Gaussian completion of the square gives phi_C exp(-X^T P_H X/2)=z_H phi_{C°}; marginalization gives pi_+(x)=phi_S(x)W(x)/Z_S. Under the isotropic proposal, each positive herald radius has squared radius/2 distributed Gamma(k_j+1, scale cb), and Z_q=(cb)^kappa. With D=S^{-1}-(cb)^{-1}I>=0, the target/proposal ratio is a constant times exp(-x^TDx/2), so acceptance produces exactly pi_+ without computing Z_S or p_H. The certificate gives ||D||<=2eps/[b(1-eps^2)]; E_q||X||^2=2cb(m+kappa); Jensen yields the bound. Conditional Gaussian regression and Poisson mixing produce the requested law.
data.cost: Exact rational inverse/Schur/LDL preprocessing and certificate checks are polynomial in d and rational input bit length L. The Gamma proposal uses O(m+kappa) exponential variables, so numerical kappa is charged; this is not polynomial in the binary length of an arbitrary huge herald count. Physical optical repetition still costs 1/p_H. Under C=tA with (1-eps_bar)I<=A<=(1+eps_bar)I, the tilted positive-count block has eps_eff=eps_bar/[1+t(1-eps_bar)]<=eps_bar, giving proposal exponent O(kappa eps_eff).
data.baseline: Quesada-Arrazola arXiv:1908.08068 gives sequential Gaussian-boson conditional probability ratios with exponential dependence on detected photons; fixing the herald as a prefix is an inferred conditional adaptation. Quesada et al. arXiv:1905.07011 give loop-hafnian heralded-state matrix elements. Neither establishes this positive-P near-isotropic rejection bound.
data.falsifier: A sign or determinant error in the Gaussian tilt, a wrong Gamma shape/scale or factorial normalizer, failure of D>=0, or an accepted density other than phi_S W/Z_S invalidates the result. Exact-rational fixtures check correlated three-mode and all-zero cases but are not proof validation.
data.open_gate: Independent external proof review and novelty/priority search. The theorem is restricted to centered strictly positive-P inputs with a supplied rational near-isotropy certificate on S; displaced/non-positive-P and arbitrary anisotropic cases remain open.
data.scope: An exact-real abstract conditional sampler; not finite-bit implementation by itself, not physical herald production, not a hardness or complexity lower bound, and not a general mixed/displaced Gaussian boundary.

data.claim: The marginalized positive-P herald sampler admits a finite-bit approximate implementation with explicit rejection, Gaussian precision, output-rate, and photon-count costs
data.theorem: Under PC-16 and its supplied rational covariance certificate, for rational 0<delta,xi<1 there is a bounded-random-bit sampler with output-law TV<=delta+xi. Its worst-case bit and randomness cost is polynomial in d, rational input length L, numerical kappa, dyadic Lambda>=exp(6 kappa eps), explicit numeric M_out, delta^{-1}, log(xi^{-1}), and exact rational factorization/certificate bit lengths. A polynomial-in-L corollary requires numerical kappa, Lambda, M_out, delta^{-1}, and log(xi^{-1}) polynomially bounded in L. No p_H or log(1/p_H) factor occurs; physical optical repetition remains 1/p_H.
data.proof: Finite dyadic proposal, acceptance, and normal uniforms are coupled cellwise to exact uniforms. Proposal exponential sums have tail <=delta/(256Lambda); off this tail and the small-uniform event, the finite proposal is within Euclidean tau of the exact proposal. The acceptance function has Lipschitz constant sqrt(||D||/e), and a normalized rejection-coupling lemma loses at most O(Lambda) times the one-trial mismatch, yielding accepted-core coupling failure <=delta/16. The finite one-trial success probability is >=1/(2Lambda), so its uncapped expected proposal count is <=2Lambda (the exact-real expectation is <=Lambda). Exact rational LDL V=R diag(v)R^T and absolute dyadic square-root intervals give Lhat without relative precision for tiny pivots. The normal CDF is computed by integrating a bounded Taylor polynomial for exp(-x^2/2), with rational Machin intervals for pi; certified inverse-CDF bisection couples latent normals in Euclidean norm except for the explicit Gaussian-tail and endpoint bands. The product-Poisson Hellinger bound TV(Pois_x,Pois_y)<=||x-y||/sqrt(2) transfers amplitude coupling into count-law TV. A rational cap M_out bounds every finite sampled total rate; cutoff Q=O(M_out+log(1/delta)) and rational interval probabilities implement Poisson/multinomial draws. The deterministic rejection cap is O(Lambda log(1/xi)). No discrete-versus-continuous Gaussian TV assertion is used.
data.cost: See the full construction and constants in outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_finite_bit_theorem.txt. For kappa>0, K0=m+kappa, T=8(1+eps)b(K0+ceil(log2(256Lambda/delta))), B=ceil(sqrt(T)), r=2|U|, Rz=2ceil(log2(512r/delta)), and M_out=1/2[K_*ceil(sqrt(2m))B+(L_*+gamma_L)ceil(sqrt(r))(Rz+1)]^2. The Poisson cutoff is Q=ceil(16(M_out+ceil(log2(64/delta)))). For the all-zero herald, omit rejection and use the U marginal of C° with its analogous Gaussian output cap.
data.baseline: Direct Gaussian hafnian simulation and heralded-state loop-hafnian methods have exponential detected-photon/occupation costs in the cited formulations. PC-17 is a finite-bit implementation of PC-16 only on the positive-P near-isotropic certificate class; it does not dominate direct methods outside that interface.
data.falsifier: The proof fails if cellwise uniform coupling, the acceptance normalization lemma, the conditional LDL Gaussian coupling, the Poisson Hellinger normalization, or the finite Poisson tail/interval budget is invalid. In particular, a discretized Gaussian is not claimed TV-close to its continuous law.
sources: Internal root analytic and sibling-leaf adversarial audit: outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_finite_bit_audit.txt
data.open_gate: Root analytic audit and a fresh sibling-leaf adversarial audit found no fatal gap; the full internal audit note is linked in sources. External proof validation, priority, and independent replay of the inherited N81 compiler remain open.
data.scope: Applies to centered rational strictly positive-P Gaussian inputs with a supplied certificate for the tilted positive-count herald marginal. The N81 all-mode-noise specialization has numerical kappa=O(R), bounded Lambda, and polynomial M_out; its noisy conditional law is separately TV-o(1) from vacuum. This does not alter ideal N81 hardness, sample rare physical heralds, establish a universal noisy-input sampler, or exclude subleading encoded information.

data.claim: A modewise relative-covariance certificate extends conditional positive-P Gaussian herald sampling beyond one-scale near-isotropy
data.theorem: Let C be rational strictly positive definite, C°=(C^(-1)+P_H)^(-1), S=C°_(H_+,H_+), K=C°_(U,H_+)S^(-1), V=C°_(U,U)-KSK^T, with m=|H_+|>0 and numerical kappa=sum k_j. For rational D0=direct_sum_(j in H_+) b_j I2, b_j>0, and supplied exact PSD certificates 0<s_-D0<=S<=s_+D0, set rho=s_+/s_-, K0=m+kappa, and q=phi_(s_+D0)W/Z_q with Z_q=product_j(s_+b_j)^k_j. Accept q at x with probability exp[-x^T(S^(-1)-(s_+D0)^(-1))x/2]. This samples the exact conditional count law after Gaussian regression and Poisson mixing, with expected proposals <=exp[K0(rho-1)]. A dyadic bounded-bit implementation follows the PC-17 latent-coupling proof, with worst-case bit/randomness cost polynomial in d, rational input/certificate length, numerical kappa, Lambda=2^ceil(2K0(rho-1)), explicit numeric M_out, delta^(-1), log(xi^(-1)), and exact factorization bit lengths. Polynomiality in binary input length alone requires those numeric parameters to be polynomially bounded. No p_H or log(1/p_H) factor occurs in conditional sampling; physical herald generation still costs 1/p_H.
data.proof: Whiten with S′=D0^(-1/2) S D0^(-1/2). Its eigenvalues lie in [s_-,s_+], and D0^(1/2)[S^(-1)-(s_+D0)^(-1)]D0^(1/2)=S′^(-1)-s_+^(-1)I is PSD with operator norm at most 1/s_- -1/s_+. Under q, whitened mode radii are independent Gamma(k_j+1, scale s_+) and phases uniform, so E||D0^(-1/2)X||^2=2s_+K0. Jensen gives acceptance alpha>=exp[-K0(rho-1)]; the dyadic Lambda is an envelope since ln2>1/2. The finite-bit proof replaces the common scale in PC-17 by modewise scales; radial coupling uses b_max, the precision-gap Lipschitz bound uses the rational entrywise norm envelope, and the output Gaussian/Poisson smoothing is unchanged. The exact rational fixture checks a heterogeneous correlated two-mode core, its zero-tilt covariance reconstruction, normalizer, acceptance and energy bound.
data.cost: The full constants and finite-bit adaptation are in outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_modewise_preconditioner.txt. Set J=ceil(log2(256Lambda/delta)), T_Y=8s_+(K0+J), B_X=ceil(sqrt(b_max T_Y)), tau=delta/[512Lambda(1+Lbar_Delta+K_*)], and M_out=1/2[K_*ceil(sqrt(2m))B_X+(L_*+gamma_L)ceil(sqrt(r))(R_z+1)]^2. The attempt cap is O(Lambda log(1/xi)); Poisson inversion is polynomial in M_out. Covariance acquisition, exact rational sandwich checks, K,V, and LDL are charged. Numerical kappa,Lambda,M_out and delta^-1 are explicit; physical repeat-until-herald still costs 1/p_H.
data.baseline: PC-16/17 use a single scalar variance certificate. PC-18 permits arbitrary heterogeneity of the positive-herald mode scales when a rational relative Loewner sandwich controls standardized correlations. It still requires centered strictly positive-P input and a supplied certificate; it does not cover arbitrary anisotropic or displaced covariances, and no direct hafnian algorithm is dominated outside this certified class.
data.falsifier: A wrong modewise proposal normalizer, a sign error in the whitened precision gap, failure of the Gamma radial scale, an invalid Jensen bound, a missing b_max or dimension factor in the finite-bit coordinate coupling, or an uncharged M_out/accuracy cost would falsify the claim. The fixture is finite evidence only.
data.open_gate: Sibling-leaf adversarial review found no fatal gap; the internal audit note is linked in sources. External proof validation, priority search, and novelty remain open. Verify numerical cost conditions in every application; no claim extends to displaced/non-positive-P or general anisotropic covariances.
data.scope: Internally proved candidate conditional sampler for a centered rational strictly positive-P Gaussian with a supplied modewise relative covariance certificate. No hardness refutation, universal noisy-input result, or physical herald-rate improvement follows.

data.claim: A local-matrix covariance certificate removes within-mode anisotropy from conditional Gaussian-herald rejection cost
data.theorem: Let C be a rational strictly positive definite centered coherent-quadrature P covariance, H an exact photon-number herald with counts k_j>=0, H_+ its positive-count modes, U the retained unheralded modes, m=|H_+|>0, and numerical kappa=sum_j k_j. Define C°=(C^(-1)+P_H)^(-1), S=C°_(H_+,H_+), K=C°_(U,H_+)S^(-1), V=C°_(U,U)-KSK^T. Let B=direct_sum_(j in H_+) B_j have rational SPD 2x2 blocks and suppose supplied exact rational PSD certificates 0<s_-B<=S<=s_+B. Put rho=s_+/s_-, K0=m+kappa, W(x)=product_j (||x_j||^2/2)^(k_j)/k_j!, and q(x)=phi_(s_+B)(x)W(x)/Z_q with Z_q=product_j s_+^(k_j) mu_(j,k_j), mu_(j,k)=E_(u uniform S1)(u^T B_j u)^k. The exact-real rejection sampler accepts q at x with probability exp[-x^T(S^(-1)-(s_+B)^(-1))x/2], then uses N(Kx,V) and independent Poisson intensities ||u_j||^2/2. It samples the complete conditional count record with expected proposals <=exp[K0(rho-1)]. For its bounded-bit implementation whiten y=B^(-1/2)x, set A=K B^(1/2), G=B^(1/2)(S^(-1)-(s_+B)^(-1))B^(1/2), and charge the output stage through a certified rational A_*>=||A|| rather than ||K||. With Lambda=2^ceil(2K0(rho-1)), the implementation has TV error <=delta+xi, finite uncapped mean proposals <=2Lambda, and attempt cap ceil(4Lambda ceil(log2(2/xi))). Its bit/randomness time is polynomial in d, rational input/certificate length L, numeric kappa, Lambda, numeric M_out=1/2[(A_*+gamma_A)Ymax+(L_*+gamma_L)c_r(Rz+1)]^2, delta^(-1), log(xi^(-1)), and exact rational/algebraic interval and factorization costs. Polynomiality in L alone requires numeric kappa,Lambda,M_out,delta^(-1) to be polynomially bounded. There is no p_H or log(1/p_H) in abstract conditional-record sampling; physical herald generation still costs 1/p_H.
data.proof: The proposal normalizer factors across modes. In an eigenbasis of B_j, with T=cos^2(theta)~Beta(1/2,1/2), expansion of (lambda_-+(lambda_+-lambda_-)T)^k gives the nonnegative mixture weights binom(k,l)lambda_-^(k-l)(lambda_+-lambda_-)^l binom(2l,l)/4^l and components Beta(l+1/2,1/2); the radial variable is Gamma(k_j+1,1). The angular moment mu_(j,k) is the exact rational even-cosine sum in the linked proof. Accepting q by the displayed precision-gap exponential gives density proportional to phi_S W. With Y=B^(-1/2)X, the transformed gap G is PSD and ||G||<=s_-^(-1)-s_+^(-1); E_q||Y||^2=2s_+K0, so Jensen gives alpha>=exp[-K0(rho-1)]. For finite bits the same proposal coupling is implemented in Y, with the explicit Gamma/Beta/normal-CDF schedules in the proof. A rational A_* is certified from algebraic intervals for A=K B^(1/2), the Gaussian output is factored by exact rational LDL and absolute-precision square roots, and latent Euclidean error is transferred to count TV by the product-Poisson Hellinger bound. This avoids any claim of TV closeness between a discrete Gaussian grid and a continuous Gaussian. The exact fixture verifies the covariance and output formulas for a constant-output, rare-herald, high-anisotropy family.
data.cost: See outputs/research/photonic_complexity/conditional_gaussian_local_anisotropic_sampler.txt, Sections 5-7. For J=ceil(log2(2048Lambda/delta)), T_Z=8(K0+J), Ymax=ceil sqrt(s_+T_Z), Lbar_a=1+1/s_-, and tau=delta/[512Lambda(1+Lbar_a+A_*)], the core is coupled in whitened coordinates to radius error tau with failure budget delta/(128Lambda). Beta-denominator, normal-tail, algebraic-eigenbasis, and categorical-mixture precision costs are explicit; mixture normalization uses mu_(j,k)>=(det B_j/tr B_j)^k and O(kL+log(k/epsilon_mix)) interval bits. Output uses exact rational LDL V=R diag(v) R^T, absolute precision for sqrt(v_i), inverse-normal Taylor/Machin intervals, and gamma_A,gamma_L,gamma_Z budgets. The finite Poisson cutoff is Q=ceil(16(M_out+ceil(log2(64/delta)))); numerical kappa,Lambda,M_out,delta^-1 and log(xi^-1) are charged. PC-19 does not pay 1/p_H abstractly; actual optical herald generation retains that cost.
data.baseline: PC-18 uses one scalar variance per herald mode; PC-19 uses a rational full 2x2 local block and removes its condition number from the rejection exponent, while still requiring a supplied useful standardized inter-mode sandwich. In the revised Section 8 family, local-matrix acceptance is one but every isotropic scalar proposal has acceptance <=sqrt(a)(1+a)/2=Theta(2^-n). This proves a weakness of that scalar proposal only: the two-mode k=1 family also admits a direct sampler using the same Gamma/Beta-mixture core law, a two-dimensional Gaussian, and one Poisson draw, and its generic low-herald-count hafnian baseline is easy. No general all-algorithm lower bound or quantum/classical separation follows.
data.falsifier: An incorrect angular mixture coefficient or Beta shape, failure of the rational angular normalizer, invalid supplied Loewner sandwich, loss of PSD for the precision gap, an omitted factor in the whitened finite coupling, an uncertified A_* or output-rate cap, a missing normal-CDF/small-denominator event, hidden numeric kappa/Lambda/M_out dependence, or an uncharged physical 1/p_H would falsify the corresponding claim. The explicit family additionally depends on positive definiteness of T^(-1)-P_H, exact C° reconstruction, the determinant p_H formula, and the output vacuum formula.

data.claim: For a finite stochastic mass-action network with a strictly positive complex-balanced equilibrium c, the product-Poisson law is invariant, its total mean jump flux is the finite sum of reaction fluxes, the chain is nonexplosive from every state, and each irreducible closed class is positive recurrent.
data.quantifiers_and_interface: Finite species/reaction set; integer nonnegative complexes; fixed positive rate constants; standard falling-factorial propensities; complex balance at c in R_{>0}^d. The Poisson law is positive on all lattice states. Nonexplosion follows from the finite-stationary-flux theorem; classwise recurrence follows by restricting the invariant law to a closed irreducible class.
data.proof_or_evidence: For each source y, pi_c(x)(x)_y=c^y pi_c(x-y); complex balance equates coefficients in the forward equations. E_pi[(X)_y]=c^y, so sum_x pi_c(x)q(x)=sum_r k_r c^{y_r}<infinity. Apply the cited CTMC finite-flux theorem, then standard irreducible countable-state recurrence theory.
data.inputs_and_costs: Supplied finite network, rates, and positive equilibrium c; no acquired samples or unbounded-state oracle. Balance and flux checking are finite channel-level calculations. No uniform mixing time or cross-class tightness bound follows.
data.strongest_baseline: Anderson-Craciun-Kurtz product-form theorem and Anderson-Cappelletti-Koyama-Kurtz finite-flux nonexplosion theorem.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: A counterexample satisfying the stated interface would refute established source claims. If c has a zero coordinate, full lattice support and every-start nonexplosion do not follow from this argument. Infinite stationary flux in a generic CTMC is inconclusive.

data.claim: The unit-rate network (0,1,3)->(0,2,2)->(1,3,1)->(0,1,3) has infinitely many finite closed irreducible stochastic classes Gamma_n={(n,1,3),(n,2,2),(n+1,3,1)}, n>=1, all inside the same positive deterministic stoichiometric class B+C=4. The normalized product-Poisson law restricted to Gamma_n is stationary and supported on A>=n. Thus each class is positive recurrent but the stationary family is not uniformly tight, despite convergence of the complex-balanced ODE in this deterministic class to c=(1,2,2).
data.quantifiers_and_interface: Exactly three species and three irreversible reactions forming one directed linkage class; all rate constants 1; standard stochastic mass action. The stoichiometric subspace has rank two and the conserved linear functional is B+C. For each integer n>=1, Gamma_n is a finite class; this claim only concerns this displayed family, not a complete classification of all CTMC classes in the plane.
data.proof_or_evidence: The three states transition only to the next displayed state with rates 6, 4, 6(n+1), respectively. At c=(1,2,2), complex flux is 16 on each complex. Product-Poisson state weights on Gamma_n are proportional to (1,3/2,1/(n+1)); multiplying by rates yields equal directed flux 6 after a common normalization. Gamma_n is a finite irreducible cycle and hence positive recurrent. Since A>=n, any finite compact subset of N^3 is missed by all sufficiently large n. The equilibrium c lies in the sole positive stoichiometric class B+C=4; complex-balanced ODE convergence is established by the Global Attractor Theorem.
data.inputs_and_costs: Network/rates supplied. All transitions, fluxes, invariant B+C, and stationary weights are exact rational/factorial computations. No limit simulation is used. The output script checks n=0..40; proof for all n is the displayed algebra.
data.strongest_baseline: Complex-balanced product-Poisson stationary laws and the established global attractor theorem; N77's supplied 4-species example provided the initial obstruction, while this run's leaf17 gives a three-species positive-state version.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: An extra enabled transition from any Gamma_n state or unequal stationary edge flux would break the construction. The result refutes cross-component uniform tightness and common deterministic attraction implying such tightness; it does not refute tightness of each law, recurrence within each class, or the existence of a tight global mixture.

data.claim: Astra P/N33 claims that every finite ordinary-endotactic actual power-law diagram with source exponent equal to its reaction source, on the positive orthant, and with arbitrary measurable rate paths in one fixed interval [kappa,K] with 0<kappa<=K<infinity, has for each positive stoichiometric class P a common compact convex positive forward-invariant absorber K_P contained in P. Every initial point enters K_P in finite time independent of the rate path; no uniform entry time over an unbounded class is claimed.
data.quantifiers_and_interface: Finite diagram; real source exponents, including negative exponents, are allowed because the state remains positive; edges that are tangent/self-loops are treated by the essential-edge convention. No unrelated kinetic orders, vanishing rates, unbounded rates, or stochastic jump processes are included.
data.proof_or_evidence: The inherited affine-minimum lemma produces a fixed finite family with active slopes close to exponent vectors at small scale. A finite set D of coordinate and reaction/source difference vectors yields a positive gap H. Endotacticity in direction -r gives a positive lowest-tier projected edge; all negative projected terms come from faster-decaying higher sources. If K L h^H<=kappa H, the active-slope drift is positive outside S-perp. Compact plateau and finite scale/box iteration give a classwise invariant absorber. Independent Luna and Sol reconstructions found no gap in the affine compactness/gluing, weighted drift, measurable-rate chain rule, or absorption steps.

No useful family-size, precision, numerical h_P, or entry-time bound is established. An online O(|Lambda|d) label evaluation count excludes acquiring/precomputing coefficients.

data.claim: Given a supplied strict-inward buffered molecular certificate and predictable bounded rate control, the N35 estimate controls exit through a specified finite time; integrating it gives a mean-exit lower bound. If a finite-state recurrent setup also supplies a mean return-time bound M to the protected region, the regenerative stationary occupation of the complement is bounded in terms of M and the exit-time lower bound.
data.quantifiers_and_interface: Integer molecular network and volume V; exact factorial correction and buffer; controlled propensities with rate values in a fixed positive interval. The return-time premise is additional and not furnished by N35. The result is not infinite-time pathwise permanence.
data.proof_or_evidence: From P(tau_Q<=T)<=alpha_V+beta_V T, integrate the survival bound to obtain E tau_Q >= (1-alpha_V)^2/(2 beta_V) for the chosen range. A cycle decomposition with each outside excursion followed by return mean <=M bounds stationary outside occupation by M/(L+M). Exact N35's 2A/2B finite chain supplies infinitely many exits a.s., showing the finite-horizon guarantee does not imply all-time survival.
data.inputs_and_costs: Certificate, control bounds, molecular volume, and any return-time bound must be acquired. N35 pays for the lattice collar, factorial correction, rate envelope, and time horizon. No general M or quasipotential is computed.
data.strongest_baseline: Agazzi-Dembo-Eckmann stochastic permanence/exponential exit frameworks and the supplied N35 certificate; exact details and comparison are recorded in leaf12/leaf13.
data.falsifier_or_boundary: A violation of the stopped supermartingale estimate invalidates the exit bound. Without the return premise, the conditional stationary occupation conclusion does not apply. The 2A/2B chain shows exits occur infinitely often despite long finite-horizon safety.

The final range is class/network/rate-box dependent; the finite waiting time also depends on domain, diffusion and initial profile.

data.statement: For a weakly reversible finite mass-action network with one linkage class and fixed positive rate constants, if every proper tier sequence of the CTMC has highest stochastic tier contained in highest deterministic tier, then the CTMC is positive recurrent from each specified initial state. The paper's total-rate lower bound on every nonabsorbing class converts the embedded-chain argument to physical-time nonexplosion and positive recurrence; absorbing states are trivial.
data.interface_and_quantifiers: Complexes C subset N_0^d and finite reaction set R are supplied; propensities are kappa_(y->y') product_i (x_i)_(y_i) 1{x_i>=y_i}, with all kappa strictly positive. The tier premise quantifies over proper sequences in the reachable state space from the initial state. One linkage class and weak reversibility are required.
data.proof_evidence: Anderson-Cappelletti-Kim, Theorem 6.1 and Lemma 6.5 use a bounded-length favorable reaction word and a fixed-step embedded-chain Foster argument. Theorem 3.1 plus Lemma 3.2 establishes the physical-time conclusion.
data.cost: The source theorem gives existence, not a quantitative return-time, mixing, stationary-tail, or finite-precision bound. The path probabilities depend on the fixed rates.
data.strongest_baseline: Complex balance gives an all-order product-form stationary law and nonexplosion on its subclass. Anderson-Kim 2018, Corollary 4.3 is a separate general one-step tier/Foster sufficient condition.
data.falsifier: A counterexample satisfying the exact single-linkage, weak-reversibility, positive-rate, and all-proper-sequence tier-inclusion hypotheses but failing classwise positive recurrence would contradict the cited theorem.
data.novelty_boundary: No new recurrence theorem is claimed; this is the external theorem used as the baseline for an internally derived finite recognizer.
data.unresolved: The premise is sufficient, not necessary, and its failure does not decide recurrence. General higher-dimensional WR recurrence remains UNKNOWN in the sources audited.

data.statement: For any finite complex set C in N_0^d, the network-wide condition that every lattice proper sequence has stochastic top tier contained in deterministic top tier can be reduced to finitely many exact rational linear-feasibility tests. Acceptance certifies the tier premise of ACK Theorem 6.1 for every reachable class of a supplied one-linkage WR graph on C.
data.interface_and_quantifiers: The finite integer exponent vectors C are supplied. The checker ranges over every nonempty set I of diverging coordinates and every bounded-coordinate threshold pattern that changes the enabled-source set. This is stronger than checking sequences reachable in one fixed class. Rate constants are not checker inputs beyond the theorem's positivity requirement.
data.proof_evidence: After subsequence extraction each coordinate is fixed or diverges. Falling factorial propensities have the same log-monomial order as the diverging-coordinate exponents on enabled sources. A bounded projection removes finite log-ratio offsets among tied stochastic-top sources while preserving strict divergent gaps. A failure must have a disabled source strictly above an enabled stochastic-top source: enabled sources have the same stochastic and deterministic ordering. Every strict violation is represented by positive rational weights; rational weights realize a violating sequence by floor(n^w). Each violation is exactly a bounded LP with a common positive margin delta. Threshold values {0} union source exponents produce finitely many strata.
data.cost: At most sum_(nonempty I subset [d]) (m+1)^(d-|I|) strata and at most m^2 LPs per stratum, with |I|+1 variables and O(m) constraints for m complexes. The delivered code uses exact Fraction vertex enumeration, with combinatorial dimension/constraint cost and potentially large rational intermediates. It has no useful general runtime bound and no complexity/precision analysis beyond this accounting.
data.strongest_baseline: The cited ACK and Anderson-Kim papers state the stochastic tier criteria and recurrence implications but do not supply this exact all-sequence LP compilation. General exact rational LP algorithms provide a more scalable implementation route but do not remove the proof/reduction obligation.
data.falsifier: A tier violation not representable by one of the finite strata/LP witnesses, or an LP acceptance despite an explicit lattice sequence with stochastic top outside deterministic top, would refute the reduction or implementation.
data.novelty_boundary: This run's candidate contribution is the reduction and exact fixture compiler, not the recurrence theorem. Novelty and priority have not been externally checked.
data.unresolved: The written proof is not machine-verified; the script is a small internal implementation. A failed test returns a tier-condition counterexample candidate, not a recurrence counterexample.

assumptions: Every included catalyst-substrate edge has all four reversible substrate/autocatalysis reactions with positive finite rates and finite k_ji>=1.
Every catalyst has positive finite 0->A_j and A_j->0 rates.
Isolated substrate coordinates are fixed within a communicating class.
data.proof_object: Separate file SPARSE_EXTENSION.txt. The proposed V uses R_i^b_i(1+epsilon_i 1_{all neighbors of i absent}) so immigration turns a large inactive-substrate weight down, while last-neighbor death turns it up. The latter is dominated at large b_i by the matched q_ji a_j b_i R_i^b_i term. A mixed-escape subsequence argument also uses the chi_j margin at zero adjacent substrate and reverse factorial terms at fixed positive adjacent substrate.
data.class_and_invariants: Each isolated B_i count is conserved. Within each fixed vector of isolated counts, immigration/death and the paired edge reactions connect all remaining nonnegative coordinates; if there are no isolated substrates, the full lattice is one class.
data.scope_limit: This is separate from the complete-pair theorem and has not received independent review. validate_sparse.py checks the exact switching generator on a finite box but does not validate the all-state escape argument. No uniform stationary tightness over varying parameters is proved. Missing reverse edges, zero rates, or non-mass-action rates are outside scope.

data.claim: For each fixed finite sparse bipartite support E, fixed finite k_ji>=1, and fixed positive finite rate vector, the paired network 0<->A_j, A_j<->A_j+B_i, A_j+B_i<->(k_ji+1)A_j+B_i is irreducible, nonexplosive in physical time, and positive recurrent on each class obtained by fixing isolated-substrate counts.
data.quantifiers: Fix finite J,I,E and all k_ji. For every fixed rate vector with all six rates positive and finite on each catalyst and included edge, every fixed isolated-substrate label class has one closed irreducible active-coordinate chain with a unique invariant probability.
data.limits: Family-specific. Isolated substrates are frozen labels. Does not cover missing reverse channels, zero rates, arbitrary propensities, or general weakly reversible networks. The proof is internal and has no external validation or priority status.

data.claim: For each fixed finite sparse paired-edge structure and compact rectangular rate box with strictly positive lower and finite upper endpoints, there exist one class-relative support-corrected exponential V and common C,c>0 such that L_theta V<=C-cV for every active state and every rate vector in the box.
data.quantifiers: The constants and V are independent of theta and of isolated-substrate labels after projection to active coordinates. V is norm-like on every fixed label class; if no isolated substrates exist it is norm-like on the full lattice.
data.proof_object: outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_geometric_drift/ROOT_AUDIT.txt; explicit rational alternative in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_certificate_effectivity/REPORT.txt; independent adversarial audit in outputs/research/reaction_dynamics/cycle4/leaves/sparse_switch_adversarial/AUDIT.txt.
data.mechanism: High inactive B_i counts receive negative local-neighbor immigration switch drift. High active B_i counts receive q-removal drift; each sole-neighbor death surcharge is paired with the same active edge. Catalysts with no high adjacent substrate are controlled by the strict R-near-one death margin when all adjacent B counts are zero, or by a reverse falling-factorial term when some bounded adjacent count is positive.
data.limits: Uniformity is not claimed as rate lower endpoints approach zero or R approaches one. It is not a complete recurrence recognition theorem and does not cover arbitrary weakly reversible networks. Independent external proof review and novelty remain open.

data.claim: Under the sparse common geometric drift on a compact positive rate box, every active quotient skeleton has a common finite drift set and common one-step minorization to the active origin. Standard drift/minorization therefore gives V-geometric convergence with common constants over rate vectors and isolated-substrate labels.
data.quantifiers: There are M'<infinity and gamma>0, common to theta and label z, with ||P_t^(theta,z)(x,.)-pi_(theta,z)||_V<=M' V(x) exp(-gamma t) for every t>=0 and x in the class. The prefactor scales with V(x); uniform convergence over all initial states in ordinary total variation is not claimed.

data.statement: The channel Phi0(X)=sum_m Tr(P_m X) omega_m^0, which measures M and prepares the free canonical M-sector state, is parameter independent and exact on rho0(lambda), and satisfies ||Phi0(rho_W(lambda))-rho_W(lambda)||_1 <= 4 sqrt(a_L)+2 sqrt(2G_L). An overflow encoder with d exact counts and one overflow label has reconstruction error <=3 delta_L+2 P_0(M>=d), where delta_L=2sqrt(a_L)+sqrt(2G_L) and P_0(M>=d)<=exp(-sd) product_{k>=1}[1+exp(s+tau B-8tauJk^2)]. Choosing s=2tauJd^2 gives O(log log(1/epsilon)) bits for fixed target epsilon once L is large enough. It is an unextended-state entanglement-breaking reverse channel; for n copies, errors grow at most n-fold.

free conditional state can be prepared as a mathematical CPTP map

data.statement: Fix d>=1, J,tau>0, B>=0 and a finite displacement set Z. On spinless fermion Fock space over Λ_L={1,...,L−1}^d, let K=dΓ(4Jd I−2J A_D), M=Σ_x n_x, H0=K−lambda M/L², beta=tau L², |lambda|<=B. Let P forbid any occupied pair at displacements Z. For every finite W_L>=0 with W_L P=0, define c0=e^(tau B)Σ_{k∈N^d}e^(−8tauJ|k|²), c2=e^(tauB)Σ|k|²e^(−8tauJ|k|²), A=2·4^d·pi² c0 c2 Σ_z|z|², a=A/L^(d+2), S=(L−1)^d and G=[h2(a)+a+(2+c0)a log S+tau a(2J pi²c2+8JdL²(2+c0)+B(2+2c0))]/(1−a). When a<=1/2, the proof candidate gives D(rho_W||rho_0)<=G and ||rho_W−rho_0||_1<=sqrt(2G)=O(L^(−d/2)); otherwise use the trivial trace bound 2. Uniformity is over lambda and all such W, including arbitrarily large finite strengths and W not commuting with M. This is a d-D fermion Fock statement, not a d-D local-spin/Jordan–Wigner result. For a physical fermion Hamiltonian one can impose parity conservation on W; the mathematical statement does not require it.

falsifiers_or_counterexamples: A violation of the wedge estimate, DPP collision/weighted collision bounds, entropy bound, kinetic compression bound or min-max partition squeeze under the stated model falsifies the proof.
Indefinite/attractive W and generic positive W that acts nontrivially on P are outside scope.
