The measure-prepare channel that measures only T=Σ_i M_i and prepares the free n-copy Gibbs state conditioned on T fixes the free family for all lambda and reconstructs the interacting family with trace error <=2sqrt(2nG_L). It applies even if W does not conserve number. Error vanishes for n=o(L^d). Truncating T at t*=ceil((n c0+log(1/delta))/log2)+1 uses O(log(n+2)+log(2+log(1/delta))) classical archive bits independent of L and adds at most 2delta error.

data.statement: Assume public 0<tau_-<=tau<=tau_+<infinity and |lambda|<=B, with common unknown tau,lambda for n product copies and the same W>=0, W P=0 family. Uniform constants c0*,c2*,A*,G*_L are obtained by replacing tau in Gaussian tails with tau_- and tau in prefactors with tau_+. Then for all sufficiently large L with a*_L<=1/2, D(rho_{tau,lambda,W}||rho_{tau,lambda,0})<=G*_L=O(L^-d); smaller boxes use the trivial trace bound. Measure total T=ΣM_i and a bin of total E=ΣL²K_i of width h; conditionally lambda cancels and the free conditional state differs from a fixed reference-temperature conditional state by at most exp((tau_+-tau_-)h)-1. Number and energy cutoffs t*,R=O(n+log(1/delta)) yield an EB archive with error <=2sqrt(2nG*_L)+exp((tau_+-tau_-)h)-1+2delta and O(log(n+2)+log(2+log(1/delta))+log(1/epsilon)) classical bits for shape error epsilon, independent of L. A finite-energy mode-subset DP gives explicit sampler cost in PROOF.txt §7. The displayed expression is the ideal exact-bin/conditional-state channel; a quantized-bin implementation replaces the shape term by exp((tau_+−tau_-)(h+2t_*zeta))-1 and adds the quantized-weight term exp(2 tau_ref t_*zeta)-1, 2 eta_DP (for sampler total variation eta_DP), and eta_gate (gate synthesis). The full finite-channel bound is 2sqrt(2nG*_L)+2delta plus these four implementation terms, allocated within the requested epsilon. Certified lower rounding ensures tilde_E>R_g implies E>R_g, so the energy Chernoff overflow bound is preserved; rational grid labels require no equality oracle for transcendental energies.

data.claim: For an open path hard-core-boson chain at hopping -2J and saturation 4JM, any nonnegative density interaction supported on a fixed lattice range R has the same fixed-m scaled continuum form as the free Tonks-Girardeau/fermion Dirichlet Laplacian under beta=tau(N+1)^2 and field detuning lambda/(N+1)^2.
data.quantifiers: For every fixed integer R, m>=0, J,tau>0, and every sequence of finite nonnegative, possibly inhomogeneous V^(N)_(i,r) supported on 1<=r<=R (no common upper bound required), the embedded m-sector closed forms Mosco-converge as N->infinity. Ordered eigenvalues converge with multiplicity; isolated spectral-cluster projectors converge.
acquired_inputs: unknown lambda in [-B,B]; no query, estimate, or side register
data.proof: Jordan-Wigner identifies the hard-core sector with an antisymmetric wedge. In the common sine embedding, the free energies are a_(L,k)=4JL^2(1-cos(pi k/L))->2Jpi^2 k^2. For liminf, drop the nonnegative interaction form and exhaust finite Slater-coordinate sets. For recovery, sample C_c^infinity on the ordered continuum simplex; its support stays a positive distance from all collision walls, so the lattice recovery vector has W_N psi=0 exactly for large N regardless of coupling size. Finite differences converge to the Dirichlet kinetic form. The lower bound a_(L,k)>=8Jk^2 gives compactness.
data.costs: Mathematical form/eigenvalue statement; no solver or parameter acquisition. Range R is fixed. No explicit convergence rate for low-energy eigenprojections is proved.
data.strongest_equally_informed_baseline: The exact free-fermion sector spectrum with the same J,tau and unknown lambda; the theorem shows nonnegative fixed-range V does not alter this continuum experiment.
data.falsifier: A range-R nonnegative array sequence violating the liminf or collision-free recovery argument, or an explicit low-sector eigenvalue cluster that fails compact Mosco convergence.

data.claim: After the parameter-independent Jordan-Wigner/sine Fock embedding, the entire normalized Gibbs state converges in trace distance, uniformly for lambda in a compact interval and uniformly over all nonnegative range-R interaction arrays, to the free-fermion/Tonks-Girardeau Fock Gibbs state with one-particle energies 2Jpi^2 k^2.

data.proof: Fixed-m trace-norm heat-semigroup convergence follows from compact Mosco convergence and a uniform summable heat-trace tail. Positivity gives Tr exp(-tau A_(N,m)^V)<=Tr exp(-tau A_(N,m)^0). The uniform cubic particle-number tail controls the direct-sum remainder. A parameter-independent isometry embeds the finite state; its CPTP reverse projects onto the embedded subspace and sends the orthogonal complement to vacuum.

data.claim: For every L-site open hard-core chain with K_L=J sum_{i=0}^L (b_{i+1}-b_i)^*(b_{i+1}-b_i), b_0=b_{L+1}=0, J in [J_-,J_+], tau in [tau_-,tau_+] with J_-,tau_->0, |lambda|<=B, beta=tau L^2, and W_L=sum_{nonempty X:diam(X)<=R} V_X prod_{i in X}n_i with V_X>=0 and fixed finite R, the normalized Gibbs state of K_L+W_L-lambda M/L^2 obeys Pr(M>=d)<=C_geo exp[-(4/3)tau J d^3+C_2 d^2] for every 1<=d<=L, with constants depending only on the public compact ranges and not on L,R, or W. For d>L the tail is zero.
assumptions: Open hard-core path with shifted Dirichlet Laplacian normalization and positive J.
W is finite, positive semidefinite, and number preserving; the stated density form with V_X>=0 suffices. Empty-set scalar terms are removed.
beta=tau L^2; the field term is -lambda M/L^2 in the Hamiltonian, so its Gibbs factor is exp(tau lambda M).
tau,J lie in fixed compact subsets bounded away from zero and |lambda|<=B.
data.proof: Within each M sector W>=0 implies ordered eigenvalues of K+W dominate K by min-max, hence Z_M(W)<=Z_M(0), without assuming [K,W]=0. The vacuum has weight one in the full partition function. Jordan-Wigner and the open sine transform give e_k=4J sin^2(pi k/(2(L+1))); sin x>=2x/pi gives e_k>=4Jk^2/(L+1)^2. Distinct occupied modes and k_i=i+s_i yield Z_M(0)<=exp[-a_L sum_{i<=M}i^2](1-exp[-2a_*])^{-M}, where a_L=4tau J L^2/(L+1)^2>=a_*=tau_-J_-; a geometric sum over M>=d gives the stated cubic exponent and finite-size O(d^2) correction. Full derivation is derivation.txt.
data.explicit_constants: Let a_*=tau_-J_-, C_*=tau_+B-log(1-exp(-2a_*)). Choose integer d_*>=1 with a_*(d_*+1)^2>=C_*+a_*/2; C_geo=(1-exp(-a_*/2))^-1 and C_2=(8/3)tau_+J_++C_* work for d>=d_*. Enlarge C_2 by (4/3)tau_+J_+d_* to cover 1<=d<d_*.
data.supplied_vs_acquired: Supplied: L, J, tau, lambda range, open hopping model and nonnegative density coefficients. Acquired: exact one-body spectrum, canonical free-sector representation, min-max comparison and tail summation. No oracle or measured data.
data.cost: D-symbol classical sector map stores ceil(log2 D) bits. With cutoff d=D-1, overflow probability is Pr(M>=d); for target epsilon, D=O((1+log(1/epsilon))^(1/3)) symbols at fixed public constants, hence O(log log(1/epsilon)) stored bits. Measurement, circuit time, classical aggregation time, energy and hardware costs are not included.
data.error_convention: For 2<=D<=L, the exact parameter-independent map records M=0,...,D-2 and an overflow flag for M>=D-1; overflow probability is the stated error. If overflow is decoded to a fixed M value, the induced M-marginal TV error is at most the overflow probability. At D=L+1, map all M=0,...,L exactly with no overflow. The map discards within-sector quantum information and is not a whole-state trace-norm archive.
data.strongest_comparator: Exact unnormalized sector-by-sector canonical trace domination Z_M(W)<=Z_M(0), followed by the vacuum lower bound Z>=1 and the parameter-matched free XX canonical partition tail. Normalized stochastic domination of the free M distribution is not asserted because normalizers differ.
data.falsifier: Any allowed positive number-preserving W violating the explicit finite-L tail inequality would falsify the claim. The proof rules this out under the listed assumptions. Attractive/indefinite interactions, number-changing terms, unbounded field scaling and different kinetic normalization are outside scope.
data.unresolved_gate: The parent programme must choose whether it seeks only the classical sector statistic or a full quantum-state archive; this result proves only the former. Independent proof review and archive novelty/priority remain open. Open/nonuniform and many-body range-R nonintegrability are not covered by the cited periodic pairwise theorem.

data.claim: For the periodic, shift-invariant, inversion-symmetric pairwise spin chain with nonzero NNN ZZ and nonzero NN XX exchange, Shiraishi (2025) Theorem 6 excludes k-support conserved quantities for 4<=k<=L/2 in its defined sense. The uniform t-V-V' model with nonzero NN hopping and V'>0 maps into this rank-one case after Jordan-Wigner, with a uniform longitudinal field and scalar terms. This does not cover open-edge, site-dependent, or multi-body finite-range interactions.

For B>0, the minimax no-message error tends 1/2 while the two-label error tends 0.

data.claim: For the same open-chain model and fixed parameters, the full interacting Gibbs state is within trace distance delta_L=sqrt(tau V C_*/(2L)) of the free XX Gibbs state, uniformly in lambda, where C_*=32pi^2 exp(2tau B) sum_{k<ell}(k^2+ell^2)exp[-8tauJ(k^2+ell^2)]. data.proof: The relative entropy identity and convexity of s->log Tr exp[-beta(K0+sW-lambda M/L^2)] give D(rho_V||rho_0)<=beta<W>_0. Free-fermion Wick expansion expresses <n_i n_{i+2}> as the squared two-mode sine-function determinant; a derivative bound gives determinant magnitude <=4pi(k+ell)/L^2. Summing modes and O(L) bonds yields <W>_0<=VC_*/L^3. Pinsker gives delta_L. The block relative-entropy chain rule over M, followed by conditional Pinsker and Jensen, bounds the q_V-weighted conditional-state distance by the same delta_L. Add the overflow probability.

Explicit parameter dependence of C_* is given in RESULT.txt.

data.claim: For the open spin-1/2 chain S=L-1 with both endpoint fields, lambda_c=2J*pi^2, fixed J,tau>0, and Xi_L=Tr exp[-tau(L^2 Hcrit-kappa W-lambda_c N)], one has log Xi_L >= (1/2)log L-(1/2)loglog L-O(1) for each fixed 0<=kappa<lambda_c/3, and log Xi_L >= (2/3)log L-(1/2)loglog L-O(1) at kappa=lambda_c/3.
data.quantifiers: For each fixed J>0,tau>0 and fixed kappa in the stated range, the inequalities hold for all sufficiently large integer L; constants and onset may depend on J,tau,kappa.
supplied: Open-chain Hamiltonian and both endpoint fields
data.proof: Use theta_i=a sin(pi i/L) coherent product states. Their exact factorized expectation has quartic term ((lambda_c-3kappa)/128)L a^4; at equality the quartic cancels and the sextic term is (lambda_c/1152)L a^6. Since mean occupation u=La^2/8+O(La^4), choose u~sqrt(L) below equality and u~L^(2/3) at equality to keep the trial energy O(1). Dephase in total N, select K~sqrt(M/log L) means in [M/4,M/2] separated by 3Delta, Delta=C sqrt(M log L), and condition each state on its disjoint number window. Bernstein gives discarded probability <=L^-12. The Bernoulli variance is >=cM; Fourier inversion gives maximum sector atom <=C/sqrt(M). Conditioning changes this by at most 1+o(1). The equal mixture has orthogonal window supports and entropy >=log K+(1/2)log M-O(1)=log M-(1/2)loglog L-O(1). Since ||B_L||=O(L^3), conditioning changes energy by o(1). Gibbs variational principle gives log Xi_L>=S-tau Tr(rho B_L), yielding the two lower bounds.
data.costs: Analytic finite-chain trial-state argument; no oracle acquisition or state-preparation runtime is claimed. The optional NumPy check compares coherent formulas against small full matrices and explicit Poisson-binomial convolutions only.
data.strongest_baseline: The available full-chain critical trace and fixed-m limits imply escape from every fixed N cutoff and log Xi_L=o(L), but do not provide these mesoscopic lower orders. They still do not give a matching upper bound.
data.falsifier: A counterexample to the stated coherent expansion, a failure of the conditioning-energy estimate with the displayed O(L^3) norm and L^-12 tail, or a Gibbs-variational contradiction at a finite L.

data.claim: For the continuum functional E(theta)=(J/2)int|theta'|^2-(lambda_c/3)int sin^4(theta/2)-lambda_c int sin^2(theta/2), theta in H^1_0(0,1), lambda_c=2J*pi^2, the all-shape fixed-mass minimum F(p)=inf_{int sin^2(theta/2)=p}E(theta) equals (4lambda_c/9)p^3+O_J(p^4) as p down to zero; minimizers have non-first-mode H^1 component O_J(p^2).
data.quantifiers: There exist p0(J)>0 and C(J)<infinity such that the remainder is at most C(J)p^4 for 0<p<p0; the statement concerns the continuum functional, not finite XXZ sectors.
data.proof: At kappa=lambda_c/3 the expansion is E=Q+(lambda_c/360)int theta^6+O(int|theta|^8), with Q=(J/2)(||theta'||^2-pi^2||theta||^2). A sine trial gives O(p^3); Poincare and Sobolev bounds force ||theta||H1=O(sqrt p). Decompose into the normalized first sine mode plus eta. The Dirichlet spectral gap controls Q(eta), the mass equation gives first-mode amplitude squared=4p+O(p^2), and int theta^6=160p^3+O(p^4). This gives the lower coefficient; the mass-matched sine trial gives the upper coefficient. Comparing both yields ||eta||H1=O(p^2). Full derivation is leaf_continuum_sixth/RESULT.txt.

data.claim: For J>0, lambda_c=2J*pi^2, kappa=lambda_c/3 and E(theta)=(J/2)int|theta'|^2-kappa int sin^4(theta/2)-lambda_c int sin^2(theta/2), the global fixed-mass infimum F(p)=inf{E(theta):theta in H^1_0(0,1), int sin^2(theta/2)=p} obeys F(p)=(4lambda_c/9)p^3+O_J(p^4) as p down to zero.
data.quantifiers: There exist p0(J)>0 and C(J)<infinity such that for every 0<p<p0 the absolute remainder is at most C(J)p^4.
data.proof: A sine trial gives F(p)<=C p^3. For minimizing sequences, K=E+kappa int rho^2+lambda_c p and int rho^2<=p^2 imply ||theta||H1=O(sqrt(p)); hence ||theta||infinity=O(sqrt(p)) and Taylor remainders are O(p^4). At the tricritical values, E=Q+(lambda_c/360)int theta^6+O(p^4), where Q=(J/2)(||theta'||^2-pi^2||theta||^2). Decompose theta=t sqrt(2)sin(pi x)+eta with eta orthogonal to the first mode. Q=(J*pi^2/2)sum_(k>=2)(k^2-1)eta_k^2 controls ||eta||H1^2. The trial bound yields eta=O(p^(3/2)); the mass equation then gives t^2=4p+O(p^2), so int theta^6=160p^3+O(p^4). Thus E=Q+(4lambda_c/9)p^3+O(p^4); Q>=0 gives the lower bound and the sine trial gives the matching upper bound. Comparing the two bounds further yields eta=O(p^2) in H^1 for minimizers.

data.falsifier: A small-p minimizing sequence violating the coercive decomposition or a verified mismatch in the exact expansion E=Q+(lambda_c/360)int theta^6+O(p^4).
